gerrit-schotte.s: Gerrit Schotte is a Curaçao politician who became the first prime minister of Curaçao when it became an autonomous country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands on 10 October 2010. His government fell in 2012, and he was later convicted of corruption and money laundering.

gey-van-pittius.s: Nicolaas Claudius Gey van Pittius was a Boer administrator of the Land Goshen, a small republic proclaimed in 1882 at Rooigrond near Mafikeng by Boer freebooters who had fought for a Tswana faction. Goshen merged with Stellaland in 1883, but Britain's Warren Expedition ended…

ghalib-ibn-awad-al-quaiti.s: Ghalib ibn Awad al-Qu'aiti was the last sultan of the Qu'aiti Sultanate of Hadhramaut, succeeding his father in 1966. While he was abroad in September 1967, the National Liberation Front seized Mukalla, and the sultanate was abolished as South Yemen became independent.

ghayur-khan.s: Ghayur Khan was the ruler of Simsir, a Muslim principality in Chechnya, mentioned by Sharaf al-Din Yazdi and other chroniclers of Timur. He sided with Tokhtamysh of the Golden Horde in his war with Timur, and Simsir was attacked by Timur's forces in 1395 during the campaign in…

ghazi-chelebi.s: Ghazi Chelebi was the last ruler of the Pervaneid principality of Sinop on the Black Sea coast of Anatolia, a descendant of the Seljuk minister Mu'in al-Din Pervane. He was famed for naval raids against the Genoese of Caffa and the Empire of Trebizond.

ghazi-muhammad.s: Ghazi Muhammad was an Avar scholar of the Naqshbandi order who became the first imam of Dagestan around 1828–1829. He preached holy war and strict sharia against Russian rule and local customary law, raiding Russian forts and towns such as Kizlyar.

ghazi-shah-chak.s: Ghazi Shah Chak was a Kashmiri noble who deposed the last Shah Mir sultan in 1561 and took the throne at Srinagar, founding the Chak dynasty, the first Shia dynasty of Kashmir. Illness forced him to hand power to his brother Husain Shah in 1563.

gheorghe-cantacuzino.s: Gheorghe Cantacuzino was a Wallachian boyar, son of Prince Șerban Cantacuzino, who served as the first ban of Craiova under Habsburg rule after Oltenia passed to Austria by the Treaty of Passarowitz in 1718. Imperial officials soon curtailed his authority as Vienna centralised…

gheorghe-gheorghiu-dej.s: Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej was the Communist leader of Romania from 1947 until his death in 1965. He nationalised industry, collectivised agriculture and imprisoned opponents in camps such as those on the Danube–Black Sea Canal.

gherardo-appiani.s: Gherardo Appiani was lord of Pisa who in 1399 sold the city to Gian Galeazzo Visconti of Milan while keeping Piombino, Elba and nearby islands for himself. This created the lordship, later principality, of Piombino, which his family ruled until the early 17th century.

ghiyath-al-din-muhammad.s: Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad was sultan of the Ghurid dynasty from 1163 to 1203, ruling from Firozkoh in the mountains of Ghor and later Herat. He shared power with his brother Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad, who led the conquests in northern India, while he himself fought the Khwarazmians…

ghiyath-al-din-pir-ali.s: Ghiyath al-Din Pir Ali was the last ruler of the Kart dynasty of Herat, reigning from 1370. He submitted to Timur, who took Herat in 1381 and deposed him.

ghulam-moinuddin-khanji.s: Ghulam Moinuddin Khanji was the last Khan of Manavadar, a small princely state in Kathiawar. In 1947 he acceded to Pakistan alongside the neighbouring Junagadh State.

gian-singh-rarewala.s: Gian Singh Rarewala was a Sikh politician and former official of Patiala State who served as chief minister of the Patiala and East Punjab States Union in 1951–1952 and again in 1954–1955. His Akali-supported coalition government of 1952 collapsed, leading to President's rule…

giberto-da-correggio.s: Giberto da Correggio was a noble of Parma who made himself lord of the city in 1303. A shifting ally of the Ghibellines and Guelphs, he extended his power over neighbouring cities for a time before being expelled from Parma in 1316.

gijsbert-karel-van-hogendorp.s: Gijsbert Karel van Hogendorp was a Dutch statesman who led the provisional government of November 1813 that ended French rule and invited William Frederick of Orange to return as sovereign prince. He drafted the constitution of 1814 and served as foreign minister, later…

gil-gavbara.s: Gil Gavbara was a prince from Gilan who, according to later tradition, took control of Tabaristan around 642 as the Sasanian Empire collapsed. He claimed Sasanian descent.

gil-gonzalez-davila.s: Gil González Dávila was a Spanish conquistador who led the first Spanish expedition into what is now Costa Rica and Nicaragua in 1522–1523. He met the chiefs of Nicoya and Nicarao, who accepted baptism, and gathered much gold.

gilbert-carter.s: Gilbert Carter was a British colonial administrator who served as governor of the Lagos Colony from 1891 to 1897. He forced a treaty on Ijebu after a military expedition in 1892 and toured the Yoruba interior in 1893, imposing peace terms that ended the long Yoruba wars…

gilbert-de-clare-1st-earl-of-pembroke.n: Gilbert de Clare, 1st Earl of Pembroke
gilbert-de-clare-1st-earl-of-pembroke.s: Gilbert de Clare, 1st Earl of Pembroke, was an Anglo-Norman baron created Earl of Pembroke by King Stephen in 1138, giving the lordship palatine powers. He supported Stephen during the Anarchy.

gilmar-pisas.s: Gilmar Pisas is a Curaçao politician who has been prime minister of Curaçao, a country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, since 2021. He leads the Movement for the Future of Curaçao party and previously headed an interim government in 2017.

giordano-pierleoni.s: Giordano Pierleoni was a member of the powerful Roman Pierleoni family and brother of the antipope Anacletus II. After the citizens of Rome rose against papal rule in 1143–1144 and revived the Senate on the Capitoline, he was named patrician, head of the new commune.

giorgio-iii-ghisi.s: Giorgio III Ghisi was the last Ghisi lord of Tinos and Mykonos in the Cyclades. When he died in 1390 he bequeathed the islands to the Republic of Venice, which ruled Tinos until it fell to the Ottomans in 1715.

giovanni-antonio-ranza.s: Giovanni Antonio Ranza was a Piedmontese priest-scholar turned Jacobin publicist who, with Ignazio Bonafous, proclaimed the short-lived Republic of Alba in April 1796 during Napoleon's first Italian campaign. The French did not support the venture, and it ended within days…

giovanni-di-vico.s: Giovanni di Vico was prefect of Rome and lord of Viterbo and much of northern Lazio in the mid-14th century, while the popes lived at Avignon. Cardinal Gil Álvarez de Albornoz defeated him in 1354 and restored papal authority over Viterbo, though he was allowed to keep some…

giovanni-ii-bentivoglio.s: Giovanni II Bentivoglio was the effective ruler of Bologna from 1463 to 1506, governing through the city's councils while keeping its formal ties to the Papal States. He was a patron of art and architecture.

giovanni-sforza.s: Giovanni Sforza was lord of Pesaro from 1483 and the first husband of Lucrezia Borgia, whom he married in 1493. Pope Alexander VI had the marriage annulled in 1497, and Cesare Borgia drove Giovanni from Pesaro in 1500.

girard-ii-of-roussillon.s: Girard II was the last count of Roussillon from the local dynasty, ruling from Perpignan. When he died without heirs in 1172, he left the county to Alfonso II of Aragon, count of Barcelona, bringing Roussillon into the Crown of Aragon.

girolamo-serra.s: Girolamo Serra was a Genoese patrician and historian who headed the provisional government of the restored Republic of Genoa in 1814. He lobbied the allies at the Congress of Vienna for its independence, but Genoa was annexed to the Kingdom of Sardinia in 1815.

gissur-thorvaldsson.s: Gissur Þorvaldsson was an Icelandic chieftain of the Haukdælir family and a leading figure of the Sturlung Age. He survived the burning of his farm at Flugumýri in 1253 and acted as an agent of King Haakon IV of Norway.

giulio-cesare-da-varano.s: Giulio Cesare da Varano was lord of Camerino from 1444, a condottiero and patron who rebuilt the ducal palace. In 1502 Cesare Borgia seized Camerino, and Giulio Cesare and several of his sons were strangled.

gjergj-thopia.s: Gjergj Thopia was lord of Durrës and the last ruler of the Thopia family's Principality of Albania, succeeding his father Karl Thopia in 1388. Under Ottoman pressure he handed Durrës to Venice in 1392, shortly before his death, and the rest of the Thopia lands later fell to…

gjon-kastrioti.s: Gjon Kastrioti was an Albanian lord who built a principality in the Mat valley and Dibër region, reaching towards the Adriatic near Lezhë. He accepted Ottoman overlordship while trading with Venice and Ragusa, and sent his sons as hostages to the Ottoman court.

gjon-zenebishi.s: Gjon Zenebishi was an Albanian chieftain who took the fortress of Gjirokastër around 1386 and ruled a principality in southern Albania and Epirus. He received the title of sebastokrator from the Despotate of Epirus and fought the Ottomans, who took Gjirokastër in 1418, the…

gleb-vasilkovich.s: Gleb Vasilkovich was the first prince of Beloozero, an appanage separated from Rostov in 1238 after his father Vasilko of Rostov was killed by the Mongols. He cooperated with the Golden Horde, married a Mongol princess and later also ruled Rostov.

gleb-vseslavich.s: Gleb Vseslavich was the first prince of Minsk, a son of Vseslav of Polotsk who received the town on his father's death in 1101. He fought the princes of Kiev and Vladimir Monomakh, who captured him in 1119.

glorious-revolution.s: The Glorious Revolution of 1688–1689 overthrew James II of England, whose Catholicism and absolutism had alienated his subjects. William of Orange landed with a Dutch army in November 1688, James fled, and Parliament offered the crown to William III and Mary II with the Bill…

glorious-revolution-spain.s: The Glorious Revolution of September 1868 was a military rising led by Generals Juan Prim and Francisco Serrano and Admiral Juan Bautista Topete that drove Queen Isabella II of Spain into exile. It opened the Sexenio Democrático, with universal male suffrage, the liberal…

gnaeus-cornelius-scipio-calvus.s: Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio Calvus was a Roman general who landed at Emporion in 218 BCE at the start of the Second Punic War, opening the Roman campaign in Hispania. He defeated Hanno and won over or subdued peoples north of the Ebro.

go-deokmu.s: Go Deokmu was a son of King Bojang, the last king of Goguryeo. In 699 the Tang court appointed him to govern the former Goguryeo population of the Liaodong region.

godfrey-i-of-louvain.s: Godfrey I of Louvain, called the Bearded, was Count of Louvain and Brussels and, from 1106, Duke of Lower Lorraine. Although he later lost the ducal office, his family kept the title and became the dukes of Brabant.

godred-crovan.s: Godred Crovan was a Norse-Gaelic warrior who, after surviving the Battle of Stamford Bridge in 1066, seized the Isle of Man in 1079 following a battle at Sky Hill. He founded the Crovan dynasty, which ruled Man and the Hebrides for nearly two centuries, and also held Dublin…

goias-velho.s: Goiás Velho, founded in 1727 as Vila Boa de Goiás during the gold rush of central Brazil, was the capital of the Captaincy of Goiás and later of the state of Goiás until 1937, when the capital moved to Goiânia. Its colonial churches and streets were declared a UNESCO World…

golden-bull-of-sicily.s: The Golden Bull of Sicily was a charter issued in Basel in 1212 by Frederick II, then King of Sicily and claimant to the German throne. It confirmed the hereditary royal title of Ottokar I of Bohemia and his successors and granted the Bohemian kings privileges within the Holy…

golden-gate-vladimir.s: The Golden Gate of Vladimir is the main surviving gate of the city walls of Vladimir, built in 1164 under Prince Andrei Bogolyubsky. Modelled on the Golden Gates of Kiev and Constantinople, it combined a defensive tower with a gate church.

golden-gate-bhaktapur.s: The Golden Gate of Bhaktapur is a gilded copper gateway at the entrance to the royal palace of fifty-five windows in Durbar Square, Bhaktapur, Nepal. Commissioned by King Ranajit Malla in 1754, it is decorated with images of the goddess Taleju and Garuda, and is one of the…

golden-horn.s: The Golden Horn is an inlet of the Bosporus in Istanbul that forms a deep natural harbour between the old city and Galata. It sheltered the shipping of Byzantium and Constantinople, and could be closed by a great chain in times of siege.

gomes-freire-de-andrade.s: Gomes Freire de Andrade, Count of Bobadela, was a Portuguese general who governed Rio de Janeiro from 1733 to 1763, at times also Minas Gerais and much of southern Brazil. He reorganised gold taxation and built public works such as the Carioca Aqueduct, and commanded the…

gongsun-du.s: Gongsun Du was appointed governor of Liaodong in 189 as the Han dynasty disintegrated, and made himself its independent ruler from Xiangping. He campaigned against Goguryeo and the Wuhuan and extended his control over the Han commanderies in northern Korea, founding the regime…

gongsun-kang.s: Gongsun Kang was the son and successor of Gongsun Du as ruler of Liaodong. Around 204 he created the Daifang Commandery south of Lelang in Korea, and in 207 he sent Cao Cao the heads of the fugitive Yuan brothers, Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi, securing recognition from the Han court.

gonka-ii.s: Gonka II was a ruler of the Velanati Chodas, a dynasty of chiefs in coastal Andhra. As Chola power in the Vengi region weakened in the 12th century, he ruled much of the land between the Krishna and Godavari rivers from Chandavolu, nominally under the Chola emperors but in…

gonzalo-pizarro.s: Gonzalo Pizarro was a Spanish conquistador and younger half-brother of Francisco Pizarro. He took part in the conquest of the Inca Empire and led an expedition to the Amazon in 1541.

gonzalo-portillo.s: Gonzalo Portillo was the last Spanish governor of Spanish Formosa, the colony in northern Taiwan centred on Keelung. With his garrison much reduced, he surrendered to a Dutch force in August 1642, and northern Taiwan passed to the Dutch East India Company's colony of Dutch…

gopal-singh-of-garrauli.s: Gopal Singh was a Bundela chief who resisted the British in Bundelkhand for several years after they took control of the region in 1803. In 1812 he submitted and received Garrauli and nearby villages by sanad as a hereditary holding, founding the small princely state of Garrauli.

gopalrao-patwardhan.s: Gopalrao Patwardhan was a member of the Patwardhan family of Maratha military commanders who became the first ruler of Jamkhandi State when the family's lands in the Southern Maratha Country were divided in 1811. Jamkhandi remained a princely state under the British until it…

gottfried-heinrich-graf-zu-pappenheim.s: Gottfried Heinrich Graf zu Pappenheim was a Bavarian-born field marshal of the Catholic League and the Holy Roman Emperor during the Thirty Years' War. A convert to Catholicism, he became famous as a bold cavalry commander, took part in the sack of Magdeburg in 1631 and was…

govardhan-chand.s: Govardhan Chand was Raja of Guler, a small Rajput hill state in the Kangra region of the western Himalayas, in the mid-18th century. His court patronised the painter Pandit Seu and his sons Manaku and Nainsukh, whose refined, naturalistic work founded the Guler style of Pahari…

govinda-iii.s: Govinda III was a king of the Rashtrakuta dynasty of the Deccan, the son of Dhruva. He led campaigns as far north as the Ganges plain and the Himalayan foothills, defeating the Gurjara-Pratihara king Nagabhata II and receiving the submission of the Pala ruler Dharmapala.

govindachandra-of-the-chandra-dynasty.s: Govindachandra was the last notable king of the Chandra dynasty of eastern Bengal in the early 11th century. Inscriptions of the Chola king Rajendra I record that his northern expedition of around 1021–1024 defeated Govindachandra of Vangala on its march to the Ganges.

govindachandra-of-the-gahadavala-dynasty.s: Govindachandra was the most powerful king of the Gahadavala dynasty, which ruled from Kannauj and Varanasi in northern India. He fought the Palas of Bengal and resisted Ghaznavid raids, and he issued more land grants than any other ruler of his line.

goz-beida.s: Goz Beida is a town in the Ouaddaï highlands of south-eastern Chad, near the border with Sudan. It became the seat of the sultans of Dar Sila, a small Muslim sultanate that paid tribute to its larger neighbour Wadai.

gran-sasso.s: The Gran Sasso d'Italia is the highest massif of the Apennines, in Abruzzo, central Italy, rising to 2,912 metres at Corno Grande. In antiquity its valleys were home to the Vestini.

grand-bahama.s: Grand Bahama is the northernmost of the larger islands of the Bahamas, lying about 90 kilometres off the coast of Florida. Its main town, Freeport, was developed from 1955 as a free-trade zone and became the country's second city and a centre of tourism, shipping and industry.

grand-duke-konstantin-pavlovich-of-russi.n: Grand Duke Konstantin Pavlovich of Russia
grand-duke-konstantin-pavlovich-of-russi.s: Grand Duke Konstantin Pavlovich was the second son of Emperor Paul I of Russia and brother of Alexander I and Nicholas I. From 1815 he was commander-in-chief of the army of Congress Poland and its effective governor, ruling harshly and ignoring the kingdom's constitution.

grand-magne.s: The Castle of Grand Magne was a fortress built around 1248 by William II of Villehardouin, Prince of Achaea, on the Mani peninsula in the southern Peloponnese, to control the local Slavs and Maniots. After his capture at the Battle of Pelagonia in 1259, William ceded it with…

grand-port.s: Grand Port is a large bay and harbour on the south-east coast of Mauritius, on which the town of Mahébourg now stands. The Dutch East India Company built its first settlement, Fort Frederik Hendrik, there in 1638.

geza-grand-prince-of-the-hungarians.n: Géza, Grand Prince of the Hungarians
geza-grand-prince-of-the-hungarians.s: Géza was Grand Prince of the Hungarians from about 972 until his death in 997, a member of the Árpád dynasty. He made peace with the Holy Roman Empire, invited Western missionaries and was baptised, beginning the conversion of the Hungarians to Latin Christianity.

grand-village-of-the-natchez.s: The Grand Village of the Natchez is an archaeological site on St Catherine Creek in Natchez, Mississippi, the main ceremonial centre of the Natchez people in the late 17th and early 18th centuries. It holds platform mounds on which stood the house of the Great Sun, the sacred…

grand-village-of-the-illinois.s: The Grand Village of the Illinois was a large settlement of the Kaskaskia and other Illinois peoples on the upper Illinois River, opposite Starved Rock in present-day Illinois. Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet visited it in 1673, and it then held thousands of people in many…

granville-sharp.s: Granville Sharp was an English scholar and campaigner, one of the first British activists for the abolition of the slave trade. He brought legal cases on behalf of enslaved Africans, including that of James Somerset in 1772.

great-courland-bay.s: Great Courland Bay is a bay on the north-west coast of Tobago in the Caribbean, near the village of Plymouth. Settlers sent by Duke Jacob Kettler of Courland landed there in 1654 and built Fort Jacobus, founding the colony of New Courland.

great-depression.s: The Great Depression was the worldwide economic slump that followed the Wall Street Crash of October 1929 and lasted through much of the 1930s. World trade and commodity prices collapsed, causing mass unemployment and bank failures.

great-illyrian-revolt.s: The Great Illyrian Revolt was a rising of the peoples of Pannonia and Dalmatia against Roman rule from 6 to 9 CE. It began when Rome levied troops for a war against the Marcomanni and was led by two men named Bato, of the Daesitiates and of the Breuci.

great-syrian-revolt.s: The Great Syrian Revolt was a rising against French Mandate rule in Syria and Lebanon from 1925 to 1927. It began in the Jabal al-Druze under Sultan al-Atrash and spread to Damascus and other regions, where nationalists joined it.

great-turkish-war.s: The Great Turkish War was fought between the Ottoman Empire and the Holy League of the Habsburgs, Poland-Lithuania, Venice and Russia from 1683 to 1699. It began with the failed Ottoman siege of Vienna and saw the Habsburgs conquer Hungary, Slavonia and Transylvania while…

great-zab.s: The Great Zab is a river rising in the mountains of south-eastern Turkey and flowing through Iraqi Kurdistan to join the Tigris south of Mosul. Its valleys formed the heartland of Kurdish principalities such as Bahdinan and Soran.

greater-hamburg-act.s: The Greater Hamburg Act was a Nazi German law of 1937 that redrew the boundaries of several northern German states. It enlarged Hamburg with Altona, Wandsbek and Harburg-Wilhelmsburg, ended the independence of the Free City of Lübeck, and transferred Oldenburg's exclaves of…

greater-kabylia.s: Greater Kabylia is the mountainous Berber region of northern Algeria centred on the Djurdjura range, east of Algiers, with Tizi Ouzou as its main town today. Its Kabyle villages long kept strong self-government.

gregoire-kayibanda.s: Grégoire Kayibanda was the first President of Rwanda, from 1962 to 1973. A Hutu journalist and leader of the Parmehutu party, he co-wrote the Hutu Manifesto of 1957 and led the revolution that overthrew the Tutsi monarchy.

gregory-the-patrician.s: Gregory the Patrician was the Byzantine exarch of Africa and a relative of the Heraclian dynasty. Opposing the Monothelete religious policy of Constans II, he proclaimed himself emperor in 646.

grigol-dadiani.s: Grigol Dadiani was Prince of Mingrelia in western Georgia, ruling with interruptions from 1788 to 1804. Contested by rival relatives and pressed by the King of Imereti, he placed his principality under the protection of the Russian Empire in 1803.

grimoald-alferanites.s: Grimoald Alferanites was a citizen of Bari who seized power in the city in 1119, during the weak rule of the Norman duke William II of Apulia, and styled himself prince. He governed Bari as an independent lordship for over a decade.

gruffydd-maelor-i.s: Gruffydd Maelor I was a Welsh prince who ruled northern Powys after the death of his father, Madog ap Maredudd, the last king of all Powys, in 1160. His territory, centred on Maelor and Ial, became the principality later named Powys Fadog after his son Madog ap Gruffydd Maelor.

guadalupe-victoria.s: Guadalupe Victoria, born José Miguel Fernández y Félix, was a general of the Mexican War of Independence and the first President of Mexico, from 1824 to 1829. He took his adopted name in honour of the Virgin of Guadalupe and of victory.

guan-yu.s: Guan Yu was a general of the late Han dynasty and a sworn companion of Liu Bei, founder of Shu Han. He held Jing province for Liu Bei until Sun Quan's forces under Lü Meng seized it in 219; he was captured and executed early in 220.

guanabara-bay.s: Guanabara Bay is a large bay on the south-eastern coast of Brazil, on whose shores stand the cities of Rio de Janeiro and Niterói. In 1555 French settlers under Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon founded France Antarctique on an island in the bay.

guglielmo-embriaco.s: Guglielmo Embriaco was a Genoese merchant and commander in the First Crusade. In 1099 he dismantled his ships to build siege engines for the capture of Jerusalem, and he later helped take Arsuf and Caesarea, bringing rich booty back to Genoa.

guhyeong-of-geumgwan-gaya.s: Guhyeong was the last king of Geumgwan Gaya, the leading state of the early Gaya confederacy in southern Korea, centred on modern Gimhae. In 532 he surrendered his kingdom to Silla and was received into the Silla aristocracy with his family.

guido-novello-da-polenta.s: Guido Novello da Polenta was lord of Ravenna from 1316 to 1322 and a poet and patron of letters. He welcomed the exiled Dante Alighieri to his court, where Dante completed the Divine Comedy before dying in Ravenna in 1321.

guido-pallavicini.s: Guido Pallavicini was an Italian knight from the Pallavicini family of Lombardy who joined the Fourth Crusade. In 1204 Boniface of Montferrat, King of Thessalonica, granted him Bodonitsa above the pass of Thermopylae, and he became its first marquis.

guido-tarlati.s: Guido Tarlati was Bishop of Arezzo from 1312 and lord of the city from 1321 until his death in 1327, leading the Ghibelline party in Tuscany. He expanded Arezzo's territory, rebuilt its walls and crowned Louis the Bavarian King of Italy in Milan in 1327, despite papal…

guido-torelli.s: Guido Torelli was an Italian condottiere who served the Visconti dukes of Milan and commanded their forces in several wars. In 1406 he received the town of Guastalla on the Po, later raised to a county, and he also held Montechiarugolo.

guigues-i-of-albon.s: Guigues I, known as Guigues the Old, was a count of Albon in the Kingdom of Arles who from about 1029 gathered lands in the Viennois, the Grésivaudan and around Grenoble. He founded the house of Albon, whose counts took the name Dauphin in the 12th century, giving the region…

guillaume-farel.s: Guillaume Farel was a French evangelist and Protestant reformer who spread the Reformation in French-speaking Switzerland. He preached at Montbéliard in 1524–1525, brought Neuchâtel to Protestantism in 1530 and helped win Geneva in 1535, where he persuaded John Calvin to stay…

guillem-ii-of-pallars-sobira.s: Guillem II was the first count of Pallars Sobirà, a mountain county in the Catalan Pyrenees. When his father Sunyer of Pallars divided his lands in 1011, Guillem received the upper valleys of the Noguera Pallaresa around Sort and Àneu, while his brother Ramon III took Pallars…

guled-abdi.s: Guled Abdi was the first sultan of the Isaaq Sultanate in northern Somaliland, chosen by the Isaaq clans in the mid-18th century after their victory at the battle of Lafaruug. He belonged to the Eidagale clan, and his descendants, the Rer Guled, kept the title with their seat…

gulf-of-bone.s: The Gulf of Bone is a large gulf of the Flores Sea between the south-western and south-eastern peninsulas of Sulawesi, Indonesia. Its coasts were the heartland of Bugis kingdoms: Luwu at its head was considered the oldest, and Bone, based at Watampone on the western shore,…

gulf-of-khambhat.s: The Gulf of Khambhat is an inlet of the Arabian Sea in Gujarat, western India, separating the Kathiawar peninsula from the mainland. It has some of the highest tides in the world.

gulf-of-mannar.s: The Gulf of Mannar is a shallow bay of the Indian Ocean between south-eastern India and north-western Sri Lanka, bounded by Adam's Bridge to the north. Its pearl oyster beds were fished from ancient times and enriched the Pandya kingdom, whose port of Korkai traded with Rome.

gulf-of-salerno.s: The Gulf of Salerno is an inlet of the Tyrrhenian Sea in Campania, southern Italy, between the Sorrento peninsula and the Cilento coast. Its shores held the Greek city of Poseidonia (Paestum) and later Salerno.

gulf-of-sirte.s: The Gulf of Sirte is a large gulf of the Mediterranean on the coast of Libya, between Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, known in antiquity as the Greater Syrtis. Its shallow waters and shifting sands were feared by ancient sailors, and its desert shore long divided the Punic and…

gulf-of-taranto.s: The Gulf of Taranto is a gulf of the Ionian Sea in southern Italy, between the heel and toe of the peninsula. In the 8th and 7th centuries BCE Greek colonists founded cities on its shores, including Taras (Taranto), Metapontum, Sybaris and Croton, which formed part of Magna…

gulf-war.s: The Gulf War was the conflict that followed Iraq's invasion and annexation of Kuwait in August 1990. A coalition of 35 states led by the United States assembled forces in Saudi Arabia and, after an air campaign from January 1991, drove the Iraqi army out of Kuwait in a short…

guman-singh.s: Guman Singh was a Bundela chief descended from Chhatrasal, the founder of Panna. Around 1765 he received a share of the family lands in Bundelkhand, with his seat at Banda.

gunther-victor-prince-of-schwarzburg.s: Günther Victor was Prince of Schwarzburg-Rudolstadt from 1890 and, after the death of his cousin in 1909, also of Schwarzburg-Sondershausen, ruling the two states in personal union. He abdicated in November 1918 for Rudolstadt and Sondershausen, among the last German monarchs…

gunzelin-of-hagen.s: Gunzelin of Hagen was a Saxon nobleman and vassal of Henry the Lion, Duke of Saxony. After Henry conquered the Obotrite lands, he made Gunzelin governor of Schwerin and in 1167 created the County of Schwerin for him.

gurbakhsh-singh-of-kalsia.s: Gurbakhsh Singh was a Sikh sardar of the Sandhu Jat clan from the village of Kalsia near Lahore and a member of the Karorsinghia misl. Around 1760 he seized territory south of the Sutlej around Chhachhrauli.

gurbanguly-berdimuhamedow.s: Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow is a Turkmen politician, a dentist by training, who became President of Turkmenistan after the death of Saparmurat Niyazov in 2006. He ruled as an authoritarian leader and built a personality cult of his own, with the title Arkadag (Protector).

gurdit-singh-of-ladwa.s: Gurdit Singh was a Sikh sardar who seized Ladwa and nearby lands near Kurukshetra around 1763, when the Sikh misls overran the Mughal province of Sirhind. His chiefship became one of the Cis-Sutlej states under British protection from 1809.

gurgen-king-of-the-iberians.s: Gurgen was a Georgian Bagratid prince of Tao-Klarjeti who held the title King of Kings of the Iberians from 994 until his death in 1008. He was the father of Bagrat III, who was adopted by David III Kouropalates and inherited Abkhazia through his mother.

gurgen-i-of-lori.s: Gurgen, also known as Kiurike I, was the son of King Ashot III of Bagratid Armenia and founder of the Kingdom of Lori, also called Tashir-Dzoraget, in northern Armenia. Around 979 he received the northern provinces and took the title of king, founding the Kiurikian dynasty.

gustav-adolph-duke-of-mecklenburg-gustro.s: Gustav Adolph was the last Duke of Mecklenburg-Güstrow, reigning from 1636 under a regency and in person from 1654 until his death in 1695. A Lutheran ruler, he rebuilt a land devastated by the Thirty Years' War.

gustav-iv-adolf.s: Gustav IV Adolf was King of Sweden from 1792 to 1809. A determined enemy of Napoleon, he joined the coalitions against France, abolished serfdom in Swedish Pomerania in 1806 and lost the territory to French occupation in 1807.

gustav-nachtigal.s: Gustav Nachtigal was a German physician and explorer who travelled through the Sahara and the central Sudan between 1869 and 1874, visiting Bornu, Wadai and Bagirmi. In 1884, as imperial commissioner for West Africa, he signed protection treaties that established German rule…

gusti-ketut-jelantik.s: Gusti Ketut Jelantik was the patih (chief minister) of the Balinese kingdom of Buleleng and the leader of its resistance to the Dutch. He refused Dutch demands over the plundering of shipwrecks and in 1848 defeated a Dutch expedition at the fortress of Jagaraga.

gusti-ngurah-agung.s: Gusti Ngurah Agung was the last raja of the Balinese kingdom of Tabanan. In 1906, after the Dutch conquest of Badung and its puputan, Dutch troops advanced on Tabanan and he surrendered.

gusti-panji-sakti.s: Gusti Panji Sakti was a Balinese warrior noble of the Gelgel court who founded the kingdom of Buleleng on the north coast of Bali around 1660. He made Singaraja his capital and extended his power across the Bali Strait to Blambangan in eastern Java.

gwanggaeto-the-great.s: Gwanggaeto the Great was the nineteenth king of Goguryeo, reigning from 391 to 413. He conquered wide lands in Manchuria from the Later Yan and the Khitan, defeated Baekje, and sent an army to help Silla against Wa (Japanese) and Gaya forces in 400.

gyula-andrassy.s: Count Gyula Andrássy was a Hungarian statesman who, after fighting in the revolution of 1848–1849 and years in exile, negotiated the Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867 with Ferenc Deák. He became the first Prime Minister of Hungary under the Dual Monarchy, from 1867 to 1871,…

gyula-the-younger.s: Gyula the Younger was the last independent gyula, or ruler, of Transylvania, the maternal uncle of Stephen I of Hungary. He kept a separate realm oriented towards Byzantium and resisted Stephen's authority.

green-corn-ceremony.s: The Green Corn Ceremony is the most important annual festival of the Muscogee (Creek), Seminole and other peoples of the south-eastern woodlands of North America. Held in midsummer when the new maize ripens, it is a rite of renewal: fires are extinguished and relit, offences…

geunchogo-of-baekje.s: Geunchogo was king of Baekje from 346 to 375, the period of its greatest early power. He subdued the remaining Mahan statelets of south-western Korea, extended Baekje's influence towards the Gaya region and in 371 attacked Goguryeo, killing its King Gogugwon at Pyongyang.

gojong-of-korea.s: Gojong was the 26th king of the Joseon dynasty from 1863 and the first emperor of the Korean Empire, which he proclaimed in 1897. His reign saw the forced opening of Korea by the Treaty of Ganghwa, the murder of Queen Min and growing Japanese domination.

gyanendra-of-nepal.s: Gyanendra was the last King of Nepal, reigning from 2001 to 2008. He came to the throne after the royal massacre of June 2001 killed his brother King Birendra and much of the royal family.

gerard-lake-1st-viscount-lake.s: Gerard Lake, 1st Viscount Lake, was a British general who became commander-in-chief in India in 1801. In the Second Anglo-Maratha War he defeated the Marathas at Delhi and Laswari in 1803, bringing Delhi and the Mughal emperor under British protection.

george-carteret.s: Sir George Carteret was a Jersey-born royalist naval officer who held Jersey for Charles I and became a courtier after the Restoration. In 1664 he and John Berkeley received the land between the Hudson and Delaware rivers, named New Jersey after his island; after its division…

gilbert-elliot-1st-earl-of-minto.s: Gilbert Elliot, 1st Earl of Minto, was a Scottish politician and diplomat. He served as viceroy of the Anglo-Corsican Kingdom from 1794 to 1796, governing from Bastia under a British-backed constitution, until the British evacuated the island.

gaius-suetonius-paulinus.s: Gaius Suetonius Paulinus was a Roman general and governor of Britain from about 58 to 61 CE. He campaigned in Wales against tribes such as the Ordovices and attacked the druid centre on Anglesey in 60 CE.

grand-pre.s: Grand-Pré is a village in Nova Scotia, on the Minas Basin, that was a major Acadian settlement from the 1680s. Its farmers reclaimed tidal marshes with dykes and sluices.

garoua.s: Garoua is a city in northern Cameroon on the Benue River and the capital of the country's North Region. It was founded by Fulani settlers in the 19th century and became one of the lamidates of the Adamawa Emirate.

gordian-i.s: Gordian I was a Roman emperor in 238. As the elderly proconsul of Africa he was proclaimed emperor at Thysdrus by rebels against Maximinus Thrax, and the Senate recognised him and his son Gordian II as co-emperors.

gebel-sheikh-suleiman.s: Gebel Sheikh Suleiman is a rock outcrop near Wadi Halfa at the Second Cataract of the Nile in Sudan, which bore a rock relief of around 3000 BCE. The relief shows a captive tied to a boat and fallen enemies beside Egyptian royal symbols, recording one of the earliest Egyptian…

gonbad-e-sorkh.s: The Gonbad-e Sorkh, or Red Dome, is a brick tomb tower built in 1147–48 in Maragheh, north-western Iran, under the Ahmadili rulers. Square in plan, with a domed chamber above a crypt, it is decorated with intricate patterned brickwork and touches of glazed tile.

gamo-hideyuki.s: Gamō Hideyuki was a Japanese daimyo, the son of Gamō Ujisato. He inherited the great domain of Aizu in 1595 but was moved to the smaller Utsunomiya in 1598.

gunderic.s: Gunderic was king of the Hasding Vandals from about 407 to 428. He led the Vandals across the Rhine into Gaul and in 409 into Hispania, where they first settled in Gallaecia.

gilaks.s: The Gilaks are an Iranian people of Gilan, the humid lowland on the south-western shore of the Caspian Sea, who speak the Gilaki language. In early Islamic times the Gil and their Daylamite neighbours long resisted Arab rule, and in the late 9th and early 10th centuries many…

geraldine-of-albania.s: Geraldine of Albania, born Countess Géraldine Apponyi de Nagy-Appony, was a Hungarian-American noblewoman who married King Zog in 1938. Two days after the birth of their son Leka in April 1939, the family fled the Italian invasion.

geneva.s: Geneva is a city in western Switzerland where the Rhône flows out of Lake Geneva. As Genava it was a frontier town of the Allobroges, mentioned by Julius Caesar in 58 BCE, and later a Roman and episcopal city.

gassantoda-castle.s: Gassantoda Castle was a mountain castle at Hirose in Izumo province, now part of Yasugi in Shimane Prefecture, Japan. As the seat of the Amago clan it withstood a siege by the Ōuchi in 1542–1543 but fell to Mōri Motonari in 1566 after a long siege.

geoffrey-i-of-villehardouin.s: Geoffrey I of Villehardouin was a French knight of the Fourth Crusade who helped William of Champlitte conquer the western Peloponnese in 1205 and became Prince of Achaea around 1209. He organised the principality on feudal lines under the nominal suzerainty of the Latin…

gezira-scheme.s: The Gezira Scheme is a large irrigation project on the Gezira plain between the Blue and White Niles in Sudan, opened in 1925 when the Sennar Dam was completed. Run as a partnership between the government, a British company and tenant farmers, it grew cotton for export and…

golan-heights.s: The Golan Heights is a basalt plateau in the Levant between the Sea of Galilee and Mount Hermon. In antiquity it held the Aramaean kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah, and later Ghassanid camps such as Jabiyah.

gorani-language.s: Gorani is a Northwestern Iranian language spoken in parts of the Zagros on both sides of the Iran–Iraq border, closely related to Zazaki. From the 16th to the 19th century it served as the literary language of the Ardalan court at Sanandaj and of many Kurdish poets, before…

gaius-maecenas.s: Gaius Maecenas was a Roman statesman and friend of Augustus, descended from an Etruscan noble family of Arretium. He acted as Octavian's diplomatic agent and deputy in Rome during the civil wars, but he is best remembered as patron of poets such as Virgil, Horace and Propertius.

gergovia.s: Gergovia was a fortified hilltop town of the Arverni in Gaul, on a plateau south of modern Clermont-Ferrand. In 52 BCE Vercingetorix defended it against Julius Caesar, whose assault was repulsed with heavy losses, one of Caesar's rare defeats.

ginkaku-ji.s: Ginkaku-ji, the Temple of the Silver Pavilion, is a Zen temple in eastern Kyoto, Japan, built from 1482 as the retirement villa of the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimasa. Despite its name, the pavilion was never covered in silver.

gascony.s: Gascony is a historic region of south-western France between the Garonne, the Pyrenees and the Atlantic. Its name derives from the Vascones, Basque-speaking people who extended their rule north of the Pyrenees in the late 6th century.

gers.s: The Gers is a department of Gascony in south-western France, named after the river Gers, a tributary of the Garonne, with its capital at Auch. A rural area of hills, it covers the historic Armagnac district, known for its brandy, and in antiquity was home to the Ausci and…

galway.s: Galway is a city on the west coast of Ireland, at the mouth of the River Corrib on Galway Bay, and gives its name to County Galway. Founded as an Anglo-Norman town by the de Burgh family in the 13th century, it was governed by merchant families known as the Tribes of Galway…

georges-thierry-dargenlieu.s: Georges Thierry d'Argenlieu was a French naval officer and Carmelite friar who joined de Gaulle's Free French in 1940 and rose to admiral. As High Commissioner for Indochina from 1945 to 1947 he worked to restore French rule, proclaiming the Autonomous Republic of Cochinchina…

ghazi-ud-din-haidar-shah.s: Ghazi-ud-Din Haidar was the ruler of Awadh from 1814 and its first king, from 1819 until his death in 1827. Encouraged by the British, who wished to weaken the authority of the Mughal emperor, he renounced his allegiance to Delhi and took the royal title.

gongju.s: Gongju is a city in South Chungcheong province, South Korea, on the Geum river. As Ungjin it was the capital of Baekje from 475, when Goguryeo drove the kingdom from the Han river, until the move to Sabi in 538.

gagik-i-of-armenia.s: Gagik I of Armenia was a king of the Bagratid dynasty who ruled Armenia from 989 until about 1020, the period of the kingdom's greatest prosperity. From his capital at Ani he extended Bagratid authority over rival Armenian princes, and his reign saw major building, including…

gagik-ii-of-armenia.s: Gagik II of Armenia was the last king of the Bagratid dynasty of Ani, crowned in 1042 as a young man. Summoned to Constantinople, he was pressured into surrendering his capital and kingdom to the Byzantine Empire in 1045, in line with the bequest of his uncle Hovhannes-Smbat.

grameen-bank.s: Grameen Bank is a microfinance organisation in Bangladesh that makes small loans without collateral to poor people, most of them rural women. Begun as a project by the economist Muhammad Yunus in 1976 and established as a bank in 1983, it pioneered group lending and influenced…

gabes.s: Gabès is a coastal city in south-eastern Tunisia, on the gulf of the same name, built around a large seaside oasis. On the site of the Roman Tacapae, it was an important stop on the route between Ifriqiya and Tripolitania.

ghazi-ud-din-khan-imad-ul-mulk.s: Ghazi-ud-din Khan Imad-ul-Mulk was a Mughal noble, a grandson of Asaf Jah I, who became vizier in 1753 and dominated the court at Delhi. In 1754 he deposed and blinded Ahmad Shah Bahadur and set up Alamgir II, whom he had murdered in 1759.

gytheio.s: Gytheio is a port town in Laconia, southern Greece, on the Laconian Gulf at the entrance to the Mani peninsula. In antiquity it was the port of Sparta.

grand-bassa-county.s: Grand Bassa County is a county on the central coast of Liberia, with its capital at Buchanan. It covers the lower St John river, where the colonisation societies of Pennsylvania and New York founded Bassa Cove in the 1830s.

gaius-antonius-hybrida.s: Gaius Antonius Hybrida was a Roman politician, uncle of Mark Antony, who was consul with Cicero in 63 BCE. As governor of Macedonia he was defeated by the Bastarnae and local peoples near Histria around 62 BCE.

grand-pensionary.s: The Grand Pensionary was the leading official of the province of Holland in the Dutch Republic, its chief legal adviser and spokesman in the States General, and often the effective director of the Republic's policy. Holders included Johan de Witt.

galeshewe.s: Galeshewe was a chief of the Batlhaping in the northern Cape, South Africa, who resisted colonial expansion. He took part in a rising in 1878 and led a further rebellion in 1896–1897, after cattle were shot during the rinderpest epidemic.

griqua.s: The Griqua are a people of southern Africa of mixed Khoikhoi, European and other descent, who speak Afrikaans. Mounted and armed with guns, they moved beyond the Cape Colony's northern frontier in the late 18th and early 19th centuries and formed communities under the Kok and…

gustav-landauer.s: Gustav Landauer was a German anarchist philosopher and writer who argued for a socialism built on voluntary communities. In April 1919 he became commissioner for education in the first Bavarian Soviet Republic.

gaborone.s: Gaborone is the capital and largest city of Botswana, in the south-east of the country near the South African border. It was built from 1964 as a planned capital for independence, since the Bechuanaland Protectorate had been run from Mafikeng in South Africa.

goa-gajah.s: Goa Gajah ('Elephant Cave') is a sanctuary near Bedulu in Gianyar, Bali, dating from around the 11th century. Its rock-cut cave is entered through a carved mouth of a demonic face, and it contains Hindu images, while Buddhist remains lie nearby.

gunung-kawi.s: Gunung Kawi is an 11th-century temple complex at Tampaksiring, Bali, where ten shrine facades about seven metres high are carved into cliffs on both sides of the Pakerisan river. They are traditionally held to be memorials to King Anak Wungsu and members of his family.

gournay-sur-aronde.s: Gournay-sur-Aronde is a village in the Oise department of northern France and the site of an Iron Age Gallic sanctuary excavated from 1977 by Jean-Louis Brunaux. The enclosed sanctuary, in the territory of the Bellovaci, held deposits of thousands of deliberately broken…

ganesha.s: Ganesha is an elephant-headed Hindu god, son of Shiva and Parvati, worshipped as the remover of obstacles and the patron of beginnings, learning and the arts. He is invoked at the start of rituals, journeys and undertakings, and is honoured across India and in Buddhist and…

gawilgarh.s: Gawilgarh is a ruined hill fortress in the Satpura range in the Amravati district of Maharashtra, India, above the town of Chikhaldara. It was strengthened by the Bahmani and Imad Shahi rulers of Berar and later held by the Marathas.

gyo-dong-and-songhyeon-dong-tombs.s: The Gyo-dong and Songhyeon-dong tombs are a group of large burial mounds in Changnyeong, South Korea, built mainly in the 5th and early 6th centuries by the elite of Bihwa Gaya. Excavations have yielded pottery, gold ornaments and weapons.

gol-gumbaz.s: The Gol Gumbaz is the mausoleum of Sultan Muhammad Adil Shah of the Bijapur Sultanate at Bijapur in Karnataka, India, completed around 1656. Its great hemispherical dome, about 44 metres across, rests on a cube with four domed corner towers and is one of the largest domes of…

gang-canal.s: The Gang Canal is an irrigation canal in north-western India, built by Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner and opened in 1927. It carries water from the Sutlej at Ferozepur in Punjab into the desert of northern Bikaner, where it turned the area around Sri Ganganagar into…

ganga-risala.s: The Ganga Risala was the camel corps of Bikaner State, named after Maharaja Ganga Singh, who expanded it. Part of the Imperial Service Troops of the Indian princely states, it served in China in 1900, in Somaliland and, during the First World War, in Egypt, where it helped…

ganga-singh.s: Ganga Singh was Maharaja of Bikaner from 1887 to 1943 and one of the most prominent Indian princes of his time. He modernised his desert state, built the Gang Canal to irrigate its north and expanded the Ganga Risala camel corps.

gobind-sagar.s: Gobind Sagar is a reservoir on the Sutlej in the Bilaspur and Una districts of Himachal Pradesh, India, formed by the Bhakra Dam, completed in 1963. Named after Guru Gobind Singh, it stretches for about 90 km and submerged the old town of Bilaspur and many villages.

gurkhas.s: The Gurkhas, or Gorkhas, were originally the soldiers of the Gorkha kingdom, whose king Prithvi Narayan Shah unified Nepal from 1768. Their armies conquered Kumaon, Garhwal and the hill states as far as the Sutlej until the Anglo-Nepalese War of 1814–1816 drove them back.

georg-von-polentz.s: Georg von Polentz was bishop of Samland from 1519 until his death in 1550 and the first Catholic bishop to join the Reformation. In 1523 he preached Lutheran doctrine in Königsberg cathedral.

gusi.s: Gusi was an Aramaean chief in northern Syria in the early 9th century BCE, from whom the kingdom of Bit-Agusi, the 'House of Gusi', took its name. Assyrian records of Ashurnasirpal II name him as a ruler of the land of Yahan who paid tribute.

gallia-aquitania.s: Gallia Aquitania was a province of the Roman Empire in south-western Gaul, organised under Augustus. It originally covered the land of the Aquitani between the Pyrenees and the Garonne, but was extended north to the Loire, taking in many Celtic peoples.

grigory-potemkin.s: Grigory Potemkin was a Russian statesman and field marshal, the favourite and close partner in government of Catherine the Great. As governor of New Russia he directed the annexation of Crimea in 1783, founded towns such as Kherson and Mykolaiv, and built the Black Sea Fleet.

gorgobina.s: Gorgobina was a town of the Boii in Gaul, given to them by the Aedui after the Boii joined the Helvetian migration and were defeated by Julius Caesar in 58 BCE. In 52 BCE Vercingetorix besieged it to punish the Boii for their loyalty to Rome, drawing Caesar to its relief.

gelao-people.s: The Gelao are an ethnic group of south-western China, living mainly in Guizhou, with smaller groups in Guangxi, Yunnan and northern Vietnam. They are among the oldest inhabitants of Guizhou and speak languages of the Kra–Dai family, although most now speak Chinese.

gross-friedrichsburg.s: Gross Friedrichsburg was a fort founded in 1683 by Brandenburg at Pokesu, now Princes Town, on the western coast of Ghana. The chief post of the Brandenburg African Company, it was sold to the Dutch West India Company in 1717, though the local leader John Konny held it until…

gustav-noske.s: Gustav Noske was a German Social Democratic politician. As people's commissioner and then minister of defence in 1919–1920, he used the army and the Freikorps to crush the Spartacist uprising in Berlin, the Bremen Soviet Republic and other left-wing risings, earning lasting…

george-grivas.s: George Grivas was a Cypriot-born Greek army officer who led EOKA, the guerrilla campaign against British rule in Cyprus, from 1955 to 1959 under the code name Digenis. He opposed the independence settlement, which ruled out union with Greece, and in 1971 he returned secretly…

george-keppel-3rd-earl-of-albemarle.s: George Keppel, 3rd Earl of Albemarle, was a British army officer and politician. A favourite of the Duke of Cumberland, he served at Fontenoy and Culloden.

george-pocock.s: Sir George Pocock was a British admiral. In the Seven Years' War he fought three indecisive battles against the French fleet off the coast of India in 1758–1759, and in 1762 he commanded the fleet that, with the army of the Earl of Albemarle, captured Havana from Spain.

government-of-india-act-1858.s: The Government of India Act 1858 was an act of the British Parliament passed in August 1858 after the Indian Rebellion of 1857. It abolished the rule of the East India Company and transferred its territories, army and powers to the Crown, creating the office of Secretary of…

gadabuursi.s: The Gadabuursi are a Somali clan of the Dir family, living in the north-west of Somaliland, especially the Awdal region around Borama, and in neighbouring parts of Ethiopia and Djibouti. In the 1880s their leaders signed protection treaties with Britain that helped establish…

guntram.s: Guntram was a Merovingian king of the Franks who ruled the kingdom of Burgundy from 561 to 592. A son of Chlothar I, he received Burgundy with Orléans when the kingdom was divided among the brothers, and he ruled from Chalon-sur-Saône.

gimhae.s: Gimhae is a city in South Gyeongsang province, South Korea, west of Busan near the mouth of the Nakdong River. It was the centre of Geumgwan Gaya, the leading state of the Gaya confederacy, whose founder Suro established it, according to tradition, in 42 CE.

guarionex.s: Guarionex was the paramount cacique of Maguá, in the Vega Real of north-central Hispaniola, when Columbus arrived. Burdened by Spanish demands for tribute in gold and food, he led a revolt in 1497–1498 but was captured.

guacanagari.s: Guacanagarí was the cacique of Marién in north-western Hispaniola when Columbus arrived in 1492. He helped the Spanish salvage the wrecked Santa María, and Columbus built La Navidad, the first European settlement in the Americas, on his land.

gotthard-pass.s: The Gotthard Pass is a 2,106-metre pass in the Swiss Alps linking Uri in the north with Ticino in the south. It became a major trade route around 1230, after a bridge was built across the Schöllenen gorge, giving the valley communities of central Switzerland strategic value.

great-trek.s: The Great Trek was the migration of Dutch-speaking settlers, the Voortrekkers, from the Cape Colony into the interior of southern Africa from 1835. Some 12,000 to 15,000 people left, resenting British rule, the abolition of slavery and insecurity on the frontier.

goitaca.s: The Goitacá were an indigenous people of the coastal plain of south-eastern Brazil, around the lower Paraíba do Sul river between Espírito Santo and Rio de Janeiro. Feared as warriors, they repeatedly attacked the early Portuguese settlements of the 16th century.

goiania.s: Goiânia is the capital of the Brazilian state of Goiás, a planned city founded in 1933 under the governor Pedro Ludovico Teixeira to replace the old colonial capital of Goiás Velho. It became the capital in 1937 and is known for its Art Deco buildings.

guapore-river.s: The Guaporé, called the Iténez in Bolivia, is a river of central South America that forms a long stretch of the border between Brazil and Bolivia before joining the Mamoré. In the 18th century it was the frontier between Portuguese Mato Grosso and the Spanish Jesuit missions…

gorazd-of-carantania.s: Gorazd was a prince of Carantania, the son of Borut, who succeeded his father around 750. He had been brought up as a Christian hostage in Bavaria, and his short rule, lasting only a few years, continued the Christianisation of the Carantanian Slavs under Bavarian overlordship.

gutuater.s: Gutuater was a leader of the Carnutes in Gaul, held responsible by the Romans for the massacre of Roman merchants at Cenabum in 52 BCE, which began the great revolt of Vercingetorix. After the revolt failed, he was handed over to Julius Caesar, who had him executed in 51 BCE.

galerius.s: Galerius was a Roman emperor of the Tetrarchy, made Caesar under Diocletian in 293 and senior emperor in the east from 305 to 311. He fought on the Danube against the Carpi and other peoples and won a major victory over the Persian king Narseh in 298.

garcia-ramirez-of-navarre.s: García Ramírez, called the Restorer, was King of Navarre from 1134 to 1150. On the death of Alfonso the Battler, who had ruled both Aragon and Navarre, the Navarrese nobles chose him as king, restoring Navarre's independence.

gimry.s: Gimry is an Avar village in the mountains of Dagestan, Russia, the birthplace of both Ghazi Muhammad, the first imam of the Caucasian Imamate, and Imam Shamil. In 1832 Russian troops stormed it; Ghazi Muhammad was killed defending it, while the wounded Shamil escaped.

gunib.s: Gunib is a village on a high mountain plateau in central Dagestan, Russia. It was Imam Shamil's last refuge, where on 6 September 1859 (25 August, Old Style) he surrendered to the Russian commander Prince Aleksandr Baryatinsky, ending the Caucasian Imamate.

george-town-cayman-islands.s: George Town is the capital of the Cayman Islands, a British Overseas Territory in the western Caribbean, on the west coast of Grand Cayman. A small port for much of its history, it grew rapidly from the 1960s as the islands became an offshore financial centre, and it is now…

grand-cayman.s: Grand Cayman is the largest of the three Cayman Islands in the western Caribbean, south of Cuba, and holds most of the territory's population. Permanent settlement began in the 18th century with settlers from Jamaica and the enslaved Africans they brought.

guadalajara-spain.s: Guadalajara is a city in central Spain, capital of the province of the same name in Castilla–La Mancha, on the Henares river north-east of Madrid. Its name comes from the Arabic for 'valley of stones', from its time as a Muslim frontier town before Alfonso VI of Castile took…

guadalajara-mexico.s: Guadalajara is the capital of the Mexican state of Jalisco and one of the largest cities in Mexico. Founded by Spanish settlers in 1532 and moved to its present site in the Atemajac valley in 1542, it became the seat of the Audiencia of New Galicia and the main centre of…

guadiana.s: The Guadiana is a river of the Iberian Peninsula, about 750 km long, flowing west through La Mancha and Extremadura past Mérida and Badajoz, then south to form part of the Spanish–Portuguese border before reaching the Atlantic. The Romans called it the Anas, and it separated…

gabran-mac-domangairt.s: Gabrán mac Domangairt was a king of Dál Riata in the mid-6th century, said to be a grandson of Fergus Mór. The Cenél nGabráin, rulers of Kintyre and later dominant in Dál Riata, took their name from him, and his son Áedán mac Gabráin became the kingdom's most powerful ruler.

gond-people.s: The Gonds are one of the largest Adivasi peoples of India, living mainly in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Telangana and Odisha, many speaking the Dravidian Gondi language. From the 14th to the 18th century Gond dynasties ruled kingdoms such as Garha-Mandla,…

gannascus.s: Gannascus was a Germanic leader of the Cananefates who led Chauci raids on the coast of Roman Gaul in 47 CE. Tacitus reports that he had earlier served Rome as an auxiliary before deserting.

germanicus.s: Germanicus Julius Caesar (15 BCE–19 CE) was a Roman general, nephew and adopted son of the emperor Tiberius. From 14 to 16 CE he led campaigns across the Rhine against Arminius and the Germanic peoples, visiting the site of the Teutoburg disaster and recovering two of Varus'…

gonzalo-guerrero.s: Gonzalo Guerrero was a Spanish sailor from Palos who was shipwrecked on the coast of Yucatán in 1511 and enslaved by the Maya. He later rose in the service of the lord of Chetumal, married into a noble family, adopted Maya dress and tattoos, and refused to rejoin the Spanish…

gulf-of-nicoya.s: The Gulf of Nicoya is an inlet of the Pacific Ocean on the north-west coast of Costa Rica, separating the Nicoya peninsula from the mainland. Its islands and shores were home to Chorotega chiefdoms at the time of the Spanish conquest, and Gil González Dávila's expedition…

grumbates.s: Grumbates was a king of the Chionites in the mid-4th century CE. After fighting the Sasanian king Shapur II on his eastern frontier, he became Shapur's ally and in 359 led Chionite troops alongside the Persians at the siege of the Roman city of Amida, described by the…

gangaikondacholapuram.s: Gangaikondacholapuram, "city of the Chola who took the Ganges", in Tamil Nadu, India, was founded by the Chola king Rajendra I around 1025 to celebrate his northern campaign to the Ganges. It served as the Chola capital for about 250 years.

gerald-fitzgerald-8th-earl-of-kildare.s: Gerald FitzGerald, 8th Earl of Kildare, known as Garret Mór or the Great Earl, was the leading Anglo-Irish magnate of his age and Lord Deputy of Ireland for most of the period from 1478 to 1513. He backed the Yorkist pretender Lambert Simnel in 1487 but kept his office under…

george-calvert-1st-baron-baltimore.s: George Calvert, 1st Baron Baltimore, was an English politician who served as Secretary of State to James I before resigning in 1625 on his conversion to Catholicism. He founded the Colony of Avalon at Ferryland in Newfoundland in 1621 but found its climate too harsh.

gympie.s: Gympie is a town in south-east Queensland, Australia, on the Mary River. James Nash found gold there in 1867, and the rush that followed is credited with rescuing the young colony of Queensland from bankruptcy.

gaspee-affair.s: The Gaspee affair was the burning of the British customs schooner HMS Gaspee by Rhode Island colonists in June 1772. After the ship ran aground near Warwick while chasing a smuggling vessel, men led by the merchant John Brown boarded her at night, wounded her commander and set…

grenadines.s: The Grenadines are a chain of about 600 small islands and islets in the Windward Islands of the Caribbean, between Saint Vincent and Grenada. The northern islands, including Bequia, Mustique, Canouan and Union Island, belong to Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, and the…

guanaja.s: Guanaja is the easternmost of the main Bay Islands of Honduras, in the western Caribbean. Christopher Columbus landed there in 1502 on his fourth voyage and met a large Maya trading canoe nearby.

george-monck.s: George Monck was an English soldier who fought for the king and then for Parliament and was Cromwell's commander in Scotland in the 1650s. After the collapse of the Protectorate he marched his army from Scotland to London in 1660, restored the excluded members of Parliament…

guglielmino-degli-ubertini.s: Guglielmino degli Ubertini was bishop of Arezzo from 1248 to 1289 and the leading Ghibelline figure in the city, ruling much of its territory as a feudal lord. Allied with the Ghibelline faction of Tuscany, he led Arezzo against Guelph Florence and was killed fighting at the…

ghirlandina.s: The Ghirlandina is the bell tower of Modena Cathedral, about 87 metres tall, begun at the end of the 11th century and completed in its Gothic upper stages in the early 14th century. A civic symbol of Modena, it is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site with the cathedral and the…

giotto.s: Giotto di Bondone was a Florentine painter and architect whose naturalistic figures and sense of space broke with the Byzantine style and laid foundations for Renaissance painting. His major works include the frescoes of the Scrovegni Chapel in Padua of around 1305 and the…

galeazzo-ii-visconti.s: Galeazzo II Visconti was co-ruler of the Lordship of Milan from 1354 with his brother Bernabò, governing its western half. In 1359 he took Pavia after a long siege, made it his residence, built its great castle and in 1361 founded its university.

giovanni-pisano.s: Giovanni Pisano was an Italian sculptor and architect, son of Nicola Pisano, whose dramatic, Gothic figures moved beyond his father's classical style. He worked with Nicola on the Fontana Maggiore in Perugia, designed the façade sculpture of Siena Cathedral and carved the…

gherardo-da-camino.s: Gherardo da Camino was lord of Treviso from 1283 to 1306, captain-general of the city after the fall of the da Romano family. His court welcomed troubadours and poets, and Dante praised him in the Purgatorio as the good Gherardo, an example of courtesy.

guala-bicchieri.s: Guala Bicchieri was a cardinal from Vercelli who served as papal legate in England from 1216 to 1218. He supported the young Henry III against the barons and French invaders, presided over his coronation and backed the reissue of Magna Carta in 1216.

gola-people.s: The Gola are a people of western Liberia and eastern Sierra Leone who speak a Mel language of the Atlantic family. Long settled in the forest belt behind the coast, they were known for their Poro and Sande societies and took part in the trade networks linking the interior to…

gayatri-devi.s: Gayatri Devi was an Indian princess and politician, born into the royal family of Cooch Behar, who became the third wife of Man Singh II, Maharaja of Jaipur. Admired for her beauty and style, she founded schools for girls in Jaipur and in 1962 won a seat in parliament for the…

gorgon.s: In Greek mythology the Gorgons were three monstrous sisters, Stheno, Euryale and Medusa, whose gaze turned onlookers to stone; the hero Perseus beheaded Medusa. The Gorgon's head, the gorgoneion, was widely used as a protective emblem on shields, temples, armour and coins.

grouville-hoard.s: The Grouville Hoard, also called the Le Câtillon II hoard, is a large Iron Age coin hoard found in 2012 at Grouville in Jersey by two metal detectorists. It contains around 70,000 Celtic coins, mostly of the Coriosolites of northern Brittany, together with gold torcs and…

gradlon.s: Gradlon is a legendary king of Cornouaille in Brittany, said to have ruled in the 5th or 6th century. In Breton legend he gave land to Saint Corentin and Saint Guénolé and ruled from the city of Ys, which was drowned by the sea when his daughter Dahut opened its floodgates,…

grafschaft-bentheim.s: Grafschaft Bentheim is a district in the south-west of Lower Saxony, Germany, on the Dutch border, with Nordhorn as its seat. It corresponds largely to the former County of Bentheim, which passed to the Kingdom of Hanover in 1815 and to Prussia in 1866.

guy-ii-of-blois.s: Guy II was the last count of Blois of the House of Châtillon, ruling from 1381. Heavily in debt and left without an heir after the death of his son, he sold the county in 1391 to Louis, Duke of Orléans, brother of Charles VI, who took possession at Guy's death in 1397.

garcia-sanchez-of-castile.s: García Sánchez was count of Castile from 1017 to 1029, succeeding his father Sancho García as a child. He was murdered in León in 1029 by members of the Vela family on the eve of his marriage to Sancha of León.

garsenda-of-forcalquier.s: Garsenda was countess of Forcalquier, the granddaughter and heiress of Count William IV. Her marriage in 1193 to Alfonso II, Count of Provence, brought Forcalquier back into union with Provence, and their son Ramon Berenguer IV ruled both.

girona.s: Girona is a city in north-eastern Catalonia, Spain, at the confluence of the Onyar and Ter rivers. The Roman Gerunda, it surrendered to Charlemagne's forces in 785 and became the seat of a county of the Spanish March, later held by the counts of Barcelona.

gruyeres.s: Gruyères is a small medieval town in the canton of Fribourg, Switzerland, on a hill in the pre-Alps above the Saane valley. Its castle was the seat of the counts of Gruyère from the 11th century until 1555, when their creditors Fribourg and Bern divided the county.

geislingen-an-der-steige.s: Geislingen an der Steige is a town in the Göppingen district of Baden-Württemberg, Germany, on the Fils where the road and railway from Stuttgart to Ulm climb the Swabian Jura by the steep Geislinger Steige. It grew below the castle of the counts of Helfenstein, who sold it to…

george-ernest-count-of-henneberg-schleus.s: George Ernest (1511–1583) was the last Count of Henneberg-Schleusingen. He introduced the Lutheran Reformation in his lands in 1544 and founded the gymnasium at Schleusingen in 1577.

goldene-aue.s: The Goldene Aue ('Golden Meadow') is a fertile lowland in central Germany between the southern Harz and the Kyffhäuser hills, drained by the Helme and divided between Thuringia and Saxony-Anhalt. Its rich farmland around Nordhausen and Sangerhausen was held in the Middle Ages…

gerhard-iii-count-of-holstein-rendsburg.s: Gerhard III (c. 1292–1340), called the Great or the Bald, was Count of Holstein-Rendsburg and the dominant power in Denmark during the interregnum of 1332–1340.

guelphs-and-ghibellines.s: The Guelphs and Ghibellines were rival factions in the city-states of medieval Italy from the 12th to the 15th century. The Guelphs, named after the Welf dynasty, generally supported the papacy, while the Ghibellines, named after the Hohenstaufen castle of Waiblingen,…

gueret.s: Guéret is a town in central France, prefecture of the Creuse department in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region. It grew around an early medieval monastery and became the chief town of the County of La Marche in the later Middle Ages.

guy-i-count-of-ponthieu.s: Guy I was Count of Ponthieu, on the Channel coast of northern France, from 1053 until his death in 1100. In 1064 he seized Harold Godwinson after his shipwreck and handed him over to Duke William of Normandy, an episode shown on the Bayeux Tapestry.

guy-i-de-la-roche.s: Guy I de la Roche was ruler of Athens and Thebes from 1225 to 1263, succeeding his uncle Otho de la Roche. He rebelled against William of Villehardouin, Prince of Achaea, and was defeated at Mount Karydi in 1258, but was pardoned after appearing before Louis IX of France, who…

guimaraes.s: Guimarães is a city in the Minho region of northern Portugal, often called the birthplace of the nation. Its castle was begun in the 10th century by Countess Mumadona Dias to protect a monastery against raids, and it became a seat of Henry of Burgundy and Teresa, counts of…

galaxidi.s: Galaxidi is a small port town in Phocis, central Greece, on the northern shore of the Gulf of Corinth. In the Middle Ages it lay within the county of Salona, and in the 19th century it became a prosperous centre of sailing-ship building and sea trade.

gunther-von-schwarzburg.s: Günther XXI of Schwarzburg was a Thuringian count elected King of the Romans in January 1349 by the Wittelsbach party as a rival to Charles IV. Lacking support and seriously ill, he renounced his claim in May 1349 in exchange for money and died weeks later in Frankfurt, where…

georg-truchsess-von-waldburg.s: Georg III, Truchsess von Waldburg, known as Bauernjörg, was a Swabian noble who commanded the army of the Swabian League in the German Peasants' War of 1525. His victories at Leipheim, Böblingen and Königshofen crushed the peasant armies of Swabia and Franconia and earned him…

gerbod-the-fleming.s: Gerbod the Fleming was a Flemish nobleman who received the earldom of Chester from William the Conqueror around 1070, after the suppression of English resistance in the north and west. He soon returned to Flanders, where he was captured in the fighting of 1071, and the earldom…

greco-turkish-war-1897.s: The Greco-Turkish War of 1897, also called the Thirty Days' War, was fought between Greece and the Ottoman Empire over Crete, where Christians had risen against Ottoman rule. Ottoman forces defeated the Greek army in Thessaly within weeks.

gao-shengtai.s: Gao Shengtai was a chief minister of the Dali Kingdom in Yunnan who in 1094 deposed the Duan king and took the throne, renaming the state Dazhong. Before his death around 1096 he arranged for the throne to return to the Duan family, but his descendants kept hereditary power as…

gumustekin-gazi.s: Gümüştekin Gazi was the Danishmendid emir from about 1104 to 1134, son of Danishmend Gazi. He held the crusader Bohemond of Antioch captive until 1103, took Malatya in 1103 and fought both the Byzantines and the crusader states.

guereda.s: Guéréda is a town in the Wadi Fira region of eastern Chad, near the border with Sudan. It is the main centre of the Tama people and of the former sultanate of Dar Tama, which was set up in the surrounding hills by the 17th century and later fell under the influence of Wadai.

gargano.s: The Gargano is a mountainous peninsula on the Adriatic coast of northern Apulia, forming the spur of the Italian boot. It is covered by the Foresta Umbra beech forest and since 1991 has been protected as a national park.

grenoble.s: Grenoble is a city in south-eastern France, at the meeting of the Isère and Drac rivers among the Alps. It was the capital of the Dauphiné, whose ruler Humbert II founded its university in 1339, and it was the seat of a parlement.

gresivaudan.s: The Grésivaudan is the wide valley of the Isère upstream from Grenoble, in south-eastern France, running north-east between the Belledonne and Chartreuse mountains towards Savoy. It was one of the first lands gathered by the counts of Albon, the future Dauphins, in the 11th…

guigues-iv-of-albon.s: Guigues IV was count of Albon in the early 12th century, a ruler of the lands around Grenoble in the Kingdom of Arles. He was the first of his family to bear the nickname Dauphin, which his successors adopted as a title, giving their principality the name Dauphiné.

gaoyou.s: Gaoyou is a city in Jiangsu province, eastern China, on the Grand Canal beside Gaoyou Lake. In 1354 the rebel Zhang Shicheng proclaimed his kingdom of Great Zhou there, and a large Yuan army under the chancellor Toghto besieged it until Toghto's sudden dismissal broke up the…

gadara.s: Gadara was a Hellenistic and Roman city of the Decapolis on a ridge above the Yarmouk valley, at modern Umm Qais in northern Jordan. It was famous as a centre of learning, the home of the satirist Menippus, the poet Meleager and the philosopher Philodemus.

gospels.s: The Gospels are the four accounts of the life, teaching, death and resurrection of Jesus in the New Testament, attributed to Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. Written in Greek in the later 1st century CE, they are the main sources for Jesus' ministry in Galilee, Judaea and…

great-mosque-of-demak.s: The Great Mosque of Demak, in Central Java, Indonesia, is one of the oldest mosques in Java, traditionally said to have been built in the late 15th century by the Wali Songo, the nine saints who spread Islam on the island. It has a Javanese tiered roof rather than a dome, and…

georgetown-guyana.s: Georgetown is the capital and largest city of Guyana, at the mouth of the Demerara river on the Atlantic coast. Founded by the French in 1782 and named Stabroek by the Dutch in 1784, it was renamed Georgetown after George III in 1812 under British rule.

goukouni-oueddei.s: Goukouni Oueddei is a Chadian politician from the Tibesti, son of the derde Oueddei Kichidemi, the traditional leader of the Teda. He led a wing of the Frolinat rebel movement and became head of state in 1979 as president of the Transitional Government of National Unity.

gemistos-plethon.s: George Gemistos Plethon was a Byzantine philosopher who taught at Mistra in the Despotate of the Morea. A follower of Plato, he proposed radical reforms of the Morea's government, army and land, and wrote a Book of Laws describing a revived pagan religion, which was later burned.

gohad.s: Gohad is a town in Bhind district, Madhya Pradesh, India, with a large fort. In the 18th century it was the capital of the Jat Ranas, who held lands in the Gwalior region and allied with the East India Company by the Treaty of Gohad in 1779.

gerontius-general.s: Gerontius was a Roman general who served the usurper Constantine III, proclaimed emperor in Britain in 407. Sent to Hispania with Constantine's son Constans, he rebelled in 409, raised his own emperor, Maximus, and is said to have let the Vandals, Alans and Suebi cross the…

grat-beal-gebri.s: Grat Beal Gebri is a ruined monumental building at Yeha in northern Ethiopia, dating from the early 1st millennium BCE. Built of dressed stone on a high platform with a portico of large square pillars, it is interpreted as a palace of the rulers of Dʿmt, the kingdom with close…

great-temple-of-yeha.s: The Great Temple of Yeha is a stone temple at Yeha in the Tigray region of northern Ethiopia, built around the 7th century BCE. Constructed of large, finely dressed blocks laid without mortar, it was dedicated to the South Arabian god Almaqah and closely resembles Sabaean…

gloucestershire.s: Gloucestershire is a county in south-west England, with its county town at Gloucester. It includes the Cotswold hills, the vale of the Severn and the Forest of Dean, and contains Cirencester, the Roman Corinium.

gangwon-province.s: Gangwon is a region on the east coast of the Korean Peninsula, crossed by the Taebaek Mountains. One of the eight provinces of Joseon, it was divided in 1945 between the South Korean province, centred on Chuncheon, and North Korea's Kangwon Province.

garibald-i-of-bavaria.s: Garibald I was the first known Duke of Bavaria, ruling from about 555 to about 591 as a member of the Agilolfing family under Frankish overlordship. He married Walderada, widow of the Frankish king Theudebald, and his daughter Theodelinda married the Lombard king Authari.

gauboden.s: The Gäuboden is a fertile loess plain along the Danube in Lower Bavaria, centred on the town of Straubing. Its rich soils have made it one of the most productive farming regions of Germany, often called the granary of Bavaria.

grimoald-i-of-benevento.s: Grimoald I was Duke of Benevento from 651 and King of the Lombards from 662 to 671. A son of Duke Gisulf II of Friuli, he seized the Lombard throne during a quarrel between two royal brothers.

godefroy-maurice-de-la-tour-dauvergne.n: Godefroy Maurice de La Tour d'Auvergne
godefroy-maurice-de-la-tour-dauvergne.s: Godefroy Maurice de La Tour d'Auvergne was a French nobleman, Duke of Bouillon and a nephew of Marshal Turenne. After French troops took Bouillon in 1678, Louis XIV gave him the duchy, which his family had long claimed, to hold under French protection, and his descendants…

gallo-language.s: Gallo is a Romance language of the langue d'oïl group, spoken in eastern Brittany around Rennes, Saint-Malo and Nantes. For centuries it was the everyday speech of Upper Brittany, while Breton, a Celtic language, prevailed in the west.

gottingen.s: Göttingen is a university town on the Leine river in Lower Saxony, Germany. A member of the Hanseatic League in the Middle Ages, it became famous after George II, as Elector of Hanover, founded its university in 1734.

gliwice.s: Gliwice is a city in Upper Silesia, southern Poland. Founded as a town in the 13th century, it belonged to Silesian Piast duchies and then to Bohemia, the Habsburgs and from 1742 Prussia, growing into an industrial centre.

giovanni-maria-da-varano.s: Giovanni Maria da Varano was lord and from 1515 the first Duke of Camerino in the Marche. A son of Giulio Cesare da Varano, he escaped when Cesare Borgia seized Camerino in 1502 and killed his father and brothers, and he regained the city in 1503 after Borgia's fall.

giulia-da-varano.s: Giulia da Varano was Duchess of Camerino, the heiress of Duke Giovanni Maria da Varano. In 1534 she married Guidobaldo II della Rovere, heir to the Duchy of Urbino, a match that threatened to unite the two states.

guidobaldo-ii-della-rovere.s: Guidobaldo II della Rovere was Duke of Urbino from 1538 to 1574. His first marriage, to Giulia da Varano, gave him a claim to Camerino, but Pope Paul III forced him to give it up in 1539.

gongyi.s: Gongyi is a county-level city in Henan province, China, between Zhengzhou and Luoyang near the Yellow River. Known in antiquity as Gong, it was the seat of the Duchy of Eastern Zhou from 367 BCE until Qin annexed it in 249 BCE.

gripsholm-castle.s: Gripsholm Castle stands on Lake Mälaren at Mariefred in Sweden. King Gustav Vasa built it from 1537 on the site of a medieval fortress, and it served as a royal residence and a state prison: Duke John and Catherine Jagiellon were held there from 1563, and later the deposed…

giorgio-vasari.s: Giorgio Vasari was an Italian painter, architect and writer from Arezzo who worked for Cosimo I de' Medici in Florence. He designed the Uffizi offices from 1560 and the Vasari Corridor, and redecorated the Palazzo Vecchio.

gisulf-i-of-friuli.s: Gisulf I was the first Lombard Duke of Friuli, a nephew of King Alboin, who left him at Forum Iulii, modern Cividale, around 568 to guard the passes into Italy from the east. According to Paul the Deacon, he asked for chosen Lombard families to settle with him, founding the…

gisulf-ii-of-friuli.s: Gisulf II was Duke of Friuli from about 590 to 610. He was killed fighting the Avars, who invaded in 610 and sacked Cividale; according to Paul the Deacon his widow Romilda betrayed the city to the khagan.

gisulf-ii-of-salerno.s: Gisulf II was the last Lombard Prince of Salerno, ruling from 1052. His sister Sichelgaita married the Norman Robert Guiscard, but relations between the two broke down, and Robert besieged Salerno and took it in 1077.
