gaeta.s: Gaeta is a port town on a fortified promontory of the Tyrrhenian coast of southern Lazio, Italy. A Byzantine outpost that became an independent duchy in the 9th century, it later served as a key fortress of the Kingdom of Naples.

garigliano.s: The Garigliano is a river in central Italy, formed by the Liri and Gari rivers and flowing into the Gulf of Gaeta. In the late 9th century Arab raiders built a fortified base near its mouth, destroyed in 915 by a Christian coalition of the papacy, the Byzantines and southern…

gulf-of-gaeta.s: The Gulf of Gaeta is an inlet of the Tyrrhenian Sea on the coast of southern Lazio and northern Campania, Italy, named after the port of Gaeta at its northern end. The Garigliano and Volturno rivers flow into it, and its shores include Formia, the ancient Formiae, where Cicero…

gelou.s: Gelou is a ruler described in the Gesta Hungarorum, written around 1200, as a Vlach duke in Transylvania at the time of the Hungarian conquest around 900. According to the chronicle he was defeated by the Hungarian chieftain Tuhutum and killed while fleeing, after which his…

glad.s: Glad is a duke named in the Gesta Hungarorum as ruler of the land between the Mureș, the Tisza and the Danube, the later Banat, at the time of the Hungarian conquest around 900. The chronicle says he came from Vidin and fought the Hungarians with Cuman, Bulgarian and Vlach…

glogow.s: Głogów is a town on the Oder in Lower Silesia, Poland. One of the oldest Polish strongholds, it resisted Emperor Henry V in a famous siege in 1109, and from about 1251 it was the capital of a Piast Duchy of Głogów.

geldern.s: Geldern is a town in the Lower Rhine region of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, near the Dutch border. Its castle was the early seat of the counts of Guelders, who took their name from it, although their county and later duchy grew mainly to the north.

gluckstadt.s: Glückstadt is a town on the lower Elbe in Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, founded in 1617 by King Christian IV of Denmark as a rival to Hamburg. Planned with a radial street pattern and strong fortifications, it became the seat of the royal Danish government of Holstein.

grodziec-castle.s: Grodziec Castle stands on a basalt hill in Lower Silesia, Poland, near Złotoryja. A stronghold there is first recorded in the 12th century; the castle was rebuilt in stone by the dukes of Legnica in the 15th century and wrecked in the Thirty Years' War.

gebhard-duke-of-lotharingia.s: Gebhard (d. 910) was a member of the Conradine family whom the East Frankish king Louis the Child appointed Duke of Lotharingia in 903.

gianfrancesco-i-gonzaga.s: Gianfrancesco I Gonzaga (1395–1444) was ruler of Mantua from 1407. In 1433 Emperor Sigismund made him the first Marquis of Mantua, raising the Gonzaga from captains of the people to imperial princes.

giulio-romano.s: Giulio Romano (c. 1499–1546) was an Italian painter and architect, a pupil and leading assistant of Raphael in Rome.

gertrude-of-merania.s: Gertrude of Merania (c. 1185–1213) was queen of Hungary as the first wife of Andrew II, and a daughter of Berthold IV, Duke of Merania.

giovanni-pico-della-mirandola.s: Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494) was an Italian Renaissance philosopher, a younger son of the lords of Mirandola. In 1486 he proposed to defend 900 theses in public debate in Rome, introduced by his Oration on the Dignity of Man, but Pope Innocent VIII condemned…

guglielmo-gonzaga-duke-of-mantua.s: Guglielmo Gonzaga (1538–1587) was Duke of Mantua from 1550 and became Duke of Montferrat when Emperor Maximilian II raised it to a duchy in 1574. Despite a hunched back he proved a careful administrator who curbed the power of the nobility of Montferrat.

guillaume-du-tillot.s: Guillaume du Tillot (1711–1774) was a French-born statesman who served as chief minister of the Duchy of Parma under Duke Philip and his son Ferdinand. An Enlightenment reformer, he limited clerical privileges, expelled the Jesuits in 1768, promoted manufacturing and founded…

greifswald.s: Greifswald is a university town in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Germany, near the Baltic coast. Founded near the Cistercian abbey of Eldena and granted town rights in 1250, it joined the Hanseatic League, and its university was founded in 1456.

gostynin.s: Gostynin is a town in the Masovian Voivodeship of central Poland, north of Łódź and west of Warsaw. In the Middle Ages it was a castle town of the dukes of Masovia, and after 1462 its land formed part of the Rawa Voivodeship of the Polish Crown.

georg-philipp-telemann.s: Georg Philipp Telemann was a German composer and one of the most prolific of all time. After posts at Sorau and as Kapellmeister at the Eisenach court from 1708, he worked in Frankfurt and from 1721 until his death as director of music for the five main churches of Hamburg.

gotha.s: Gotha is a town in Thuringia, Germany, west of Erfurt. It was the residence of the dukes of Saxe-Gotha from 1640 and later one of the two capitals of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha.

george-frideric-handel.s: George Frideric Handel was a German-born composer who spent most of his career in London. Born in Halle, the son of a surgeon to the Duke of Saxe-Weissenfels, he studied in Italy and settled in England from 1712, becoming a British subject in 1727.

guaimar-iv-of-salerno.s: Guaimar IV was the Lombard Prince of Salerno from 1027 to 1052, under whom the principality reached its greatest extent. He took Capua, Amalfi and Sorrento and in 1042 recognised the Norman leaders William Iron Arm and later Drogo as counts in Apulia, helping establish Norman…

georgenberg-pact.s: The Georgenberg Pact was an inheritance treaty concluded on 17 August 1186 at the Georgenberg near Enns between Duke Ottokar IV of Styria, who was childless and ill, and Duke Leopold V of Austria. It provided that Styria would pass to the Babenbergs while guaranteeing the…

giacomo-iv-crispo.s: Giacomo IV Crispo was the last Duke of Naxos, ruler of the Duchy of the Archipelago in the Cyclades from 1564. The duchy had long been an Ottoman tributary, and in 1566 his Greek subjects complained of his misrule, after which Sultan Selim II deposed him.

guidobaldo-da-montefeltro.s: Guidobaldo da Montefeltro was Duke of Urbino from 1482, succeeding his father Federico. Sickly from youth, he was driven out by Cesare Borgia in 1502 and recovered his duchy after the death of Pope Alexander VI in 1503.

georg-marcgraf.s: Georg Marcgraf was a German naturalist, astronomer and cartographer who joined Johan Maurits in Dutch Brazil, where he built an observatory in Recife and studied the plants, animals and geography of the colony. His work formed the core of the Historia Naturalis Brasiliae,…

galle-fort.s: Galle Fort is a fortified old town on the south-west coast of Sri Lanka. The Portuguese built the first fortifications in the late 16th century, and after taking Galle in 1640 the Dutch rebuilt them on a much larger scale, with bastions and sea walls enclosing streets,…

georgius-candidius.s: Georgius Candidius was a Dutch Reformed missionary, the first Protestant missionary in Taiwan, who arrived in 1627 and worked among the Siraya people around the village of Sinkan. He learned their language and wrote a description of their customs and religion.

guo-huaiyi-rebellion.s: The Guo Huaiyi rebellion was a rising of Chinese farmers in Dutch Formosa in September 1652, led by the village head Guo Huaiyi, against the heavy taxes and controls of the Dutch East India Company. The poorly armed rebels were defeated within weeks by Dutch soldiers and their…

great-heathen-army.s: The Great Heathen Army was a large coalition of Scandinavian warriors that invaded England in 865. It took York in 867, overran East Anglia and much of Mercia, and attacked Wessex until Alfred the Great defeated it at Edington in 878.

gerald-fitzgerald-3rd-earl-of-desmond.s: Gerald FitzGerald, 3rd Earl of Desmond, known in Irish as Gearóid Iarla, was a Hiberno-Norman lord who served as Justiciar of Ireland from 1367. He is best known as a poet in the Irish language, whose courtly love poems are among the earliest of their kind in Irish.

gerald-fitzgerald-14th-earl-of-desmond.s: Gerald FitzGerald, Earl of Desmond, numbered the 14th or 15th earl, was the last of the great FitzGerald lords of Desmond in Munster. Defeated by his rival the Earl of Ormond at Affane in 1565, he spent years in detention in England.

geumwa.s: Geumwa is a king of Eastern Buyeo in Korean tradition, recorded in the Samguk sagi as the successor of Haeburu. In the legend Haeburu found him as a child under a stone, shining like gold.

guo-state.s: Guo was the name of several states of Zhou-period China ruled by kinsmen of the Zhou royal house, descended from younger brothers of King Wen. Eastern Guo, near modern Xingyang in Henan, was destroyed by the State of Zheng around 767 BCE, while Western Guo, later based at…

george-martinuzzi.s: George Martinuzzi was a Croatian-born Pauline monk and statesman who served John Zápolya as treasurer and became bishop of Várad. After Zápolya's death in 1540 he governed the eastern Hungarian lands for the infant John Sigismund, balancing between the Habsburgs and the Ottomans.

gu-kaizhi.s: Gu Kaizhi was a Chinese painter of the Eastern Jin dynasty, regarded as one of the founders of Chinese figure painting. He served as an official and wrote some of the earliest Chinese essays on painting.

guyuk-khan.s: Güyük Khan was the third Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, reigning from 1246 to 1248. A son of Ögedei, he campaigned in Manchuria in 1233, when his army captured Puxian Wannu of Eastern Xia, and later took part in the western campaign against the Rus'.

gbadebo-i.s: Gbadebo I was the Alake of Abeokuta, paramount ruler of the Egba in south-western Nigeria, from 1898 until his death in 1920. His reign coincided with the reformed Egba United Government, which ran its own treasury, courts and roads under British influence, and in 1904 he…

george-william-johnson.s: George William Johnson was a Sierra Leone-born tailor, one of the Saro returnees who settled in Yoruba country in the mid-19th century. In 1865 he organised the Egba United Board of Management at Abeokuta, an attempt to create a modern government with customs revenue and a…

gaius-julius-sohaemus.s: Gaius Julius Sohaemus was the last king of Emesa in Syria, ruling from 54 CE as a client of Rome. He sent troops to support the Romans in the Jewish War of 66–73, backed Vespasian's bid for the empire in 69, and took part in the annexation of Commagene in 72.

gurma-people.s: The Gurma, or Gourmantché, are a Gur-speaking people of eastern Burkina Faso and neighbouring parts of Niger, Togo and Benin. Their traditional kingdoms, centred on Fada N'Gourma, were among the Mossi-related states of the Volta basin.

garden-of-the-hesperides.s: The Garden of the Hesperides was in Greek myth the garden of the goddess Hera at the western edge of the world, where golden apples were guarded by the nymphs called Hesperides and the dragon Ladon. Fetching the apples was one of the labours of Heracles.

gylippus.s: Gylippus was a Spartan general of the Peloponnesian War. Sent to help Syracuse in 414 BCE, he stopped at Euesperides on the Libyan coast and helped the city against local tribes before reaching Sicily, where he organised the defence and destroyed the Athenian expedition in 413…

ghartey-iv.s: Ghartey IV, born Robert Johnson Ghartey, was a Fante merchant from the Gold Coast who became king of Winneba. A Western-educated businessman, he was chosen as king-president of the Fante Confederacy, the alliance of coastal Fante states formed at Mankessim in 1868 to resist…

guzgan.s: Guzgan, known in Arabic as Juzjan, was a historical region of northern Afghanistan between Balkh and Merv, roughly the modern provinces of Jowzjan and Faryab. From the late 9th century it was ruled by the Farighunid dynasty, patrons of learning to whom the Persian geography…

gerald-templer.s: Gerald Templer was a British army officer who served as High Commissioner in Malaya from 1952 to 1954 during the Malayan Emergency. Combining civil and military command, he pressed on with the resettlement of rural Chinese into new villages, strict food control and a campaign…

gulating.s: The Gulating was the law assembly of western Norway, which met at Gulen near the mouth of the Sognefjord from the Viking Age. It served the districts of the west coast, and its law, the Gulating Law, is one of the oldest Norwegian law codes, surviving in a 13th-century version.

gonaives.s: Gonaïves is a port city on the west coast of Haiti, the capital of the Artibonite department. On 1 January 1804 Jean-Jacques Dessalines proclaimed the independence of Haiti there, and it is known as the City of Independence.

great-dortmund-feud.s: The Great Dortmund Feud was a war of 1388 to 1389 in which Archbishop Frederick III of Cologne and Count Engelbert III of the Mark besieged the free imperial city of Dortmund. The city withstood the siege, and the peace of 1389 confirmed its independence, though at the cost of…

giengen-an-der-brenz.s: Giengen an der Brenz is a town in eastern Baden-Württemberg that grew as a Hohenstaufen royal town and was a free imperial city from the late Middle Ages until 1802, when it passed to Württemberg. It adopted the Lutheran Reformation.

gotz-von-berlichingen.s: Götz von Berlichingen was a Franconian imperial knight and mercenary known as Götz of the Iron Hand after he lost his right hand in 1504 and wore an iron prosthesis. He waged many private feuds, was held prisoner at Heilbronn from 1519, and in 1525 led a band of rebels in the…

great-ravensburg-trading-company.s: The Great Ravensburg Trading Company was a merchant company formed around 1380 by families of Ravensburg, Konstanz and other Swabian towns, among them the Humpis. One of the largest trading firms of late medieval Germany, it dealt in linen, fustian, saffron and other goods…

george-frederick-margrave-of-baden-durla.s: George Frederick was Margrave of Baden-Durlach from 1604 to 1622, a Protestant prince and military writer. To fight for the Protestant cause in the Thirty Years' War he handed the government to his son in 1622, but was defeated by Tilly at Wimpfen that year.

guayaquil-conference.s: The Guayaquil Conference was the meeting of the two leading liberators of South America, Simón Bolívar and José de San Martín, at Guayaquil on 26 and 27 July 1822. Held in private, it left no reliable record, but soon afterwards San Martín withdrew from Peru and public life,…

gaziantep.s: Gaziantep, historically Aintab or Antep, is a city in south-eastern Turkey near the Syrian border. Occupied by British and then French troops after the First World War, it resisted a long French siege in 1920–1921 before surrendering in February 1921, and the Turkish…

guiana-space-centre.s: The Guiana Space Centre is the spaceport of France and the European Space Agency at Kourou in French Guiana. Chosen for its position near the equator and its open ocean to the east, the site was selected by the French space agency CNES in 1964, and the first launch took place…

gabriel-angoulvant.s: Gabriel Angoulvant was a French colonial administrator who governed the Ivory Coast from 1908 to 1916. Abandoning earlier policies of gradual penetration, he launched systematic military campaigns against the peoples of the forest zone, disarming them, regrouping villages and…

grand-bassam.s: Grand-Bassam is a town on the coast of Ivory Coast, east of Abidjan. France signed treaties with local rulers and built a fort there in 1843, and it served as the first capital of the French colony from 1893 until yellow fever epidemics prompted the move to Bingerville in 1900.

gothenburg.s: Gothenburg is the second-largest city of Sweden, on the west coast at the mouth of the Göta älv. Founded by King Gustavus Adolphus in 1621, it gave Sweden an outlet to the North Sea outside the Danish-controlled Sound.

gustave-borgnis-desbordes.s: Gustave Borgnis-Desbordes was a French artillery officer who led the advance of French power from the upper Senegal to the Niger. As commander of Upper Senegal from 1880 to 1883 he built forts at Kita and Bamako, fought the forces of Samori Ture and laid the foundations of the…

gezira.s: The Gezira ('island') is the fertile plain between the Blue Nile and the White Nile south of Khartoum in Sudan. It was a heartland of the Funj Sultanate of Sennar from the 16th century.

gevaudan.s: Gévaudan is a historic region of southern France in the Massif Central, roughly the present department of Lozère. Its name derives from the Gabali, the Gallic people who lived there in antiquity, and in the Middle Ages it formed a county and bishopric centred on Mende.

guadalete.s: The Guadalete is a river of Andalusia in southern Spain, flowing from the Sierra de Grazalema past Arcos de la Frontera and Jerez to the Bay of Cádiz at El Puerto de Santa María. Near it in 711 Tariq ibn Ziyad defeated the Visigothic king Roderic, opening the Muslim conquest…

germania.s: Germania was the Roman name for the lands east of the Rhine and north of the Danube inhabited by Germanic peoples, which Rome never permanently conquered after its defeat in the Teutoburg Forest in 9 CE. The name was also given to the Roman provinces of Germania Inferior and…

gaius-marius.s: Gaius Marius was a Roman general and politician who held the consulship seven times. He ended the war against Jugurtha of Numidia, defeated the Cimbri and Teutones at Aquae Sextiae and Vercellae, and opened the legions to men without property.

golden-urn.s: The Golden Urn was a method introduced by the Qing Qianlong Emperor in 1793 for choosing high Tibetan and Mongolian reincarnate lamas, including the Dalai and Panchen Lamas. The names of candidates were written on slips placed in an urn and one was drawn by lot under the…

ganja-azerbaijan.s: Ganja is the second-largest city of Azerbaijan, in the west of the country. A major centre of the medieval Caucasus, it was the home of the poet Nizami Ganjavi in the 12th century.

garifuna.s: The Garifuna are a people of mixed African and Indigenous Caribbean descent who formed on Saint Vincent from the 17th century, known to the British as Black Caribs. After their defeat in the Second Carib War most were deported in 1797 to Roatán, and they spread along the…

goliath.s: Goliath is the Philistine giant of Gath in the Hebrew Bible, killed by the young David with a sling in the Valley of Elah in the story told in 1 Samuel 17. The episode became a proverbial image of a weak opponent defeating a strong one.

goryeong.s: Goryeong is a county in North Gyeongsang Province, South Korea, west of Daegu. It was the centre of Daegaya, the leading Gaya state of the 5th and 6th centuries, until Silla annexed it in 562.

galata.s: Galata, known in the Middle Ages also as Pera, is a quarter of Istanbul on the north side of the Golden Horn. In 1267 the Byzantine emperor Michael VIII granted it to the Genoese, who walled it and made it their main colony in the region, governed by a podestà sent from Genoa.

galata-tower.s: The Galata Tower is a medieval stone tower in the Galata quarter of Istanbul. The Genoese built it in 1348 as the Tower of Christ, the highest point in the walls of their colony of Pera.

german-east-africa-company.s: The German East Africa Company was a chartered company founded by Carl Peters in 1885 to administer and exploit the lands claimed through his treaties on the East African mainland. Its takeover of the coast leased from the Sultan of Zanzibar provoked the Abushiri revolt of…

ghor.s: Ghor is a mountainous province of central Afghanistan, in the upper valleys of the Hari Rud and Farah rivers. Long isolated and slow to convert to Islam, it was the homeland of the Shansabani chiefs who founded the Ghurid dynasty and in the late 12th century ruled from…

george-rooke.s: Sir George Rooke was an English admiral. In the War of the Spanish Succession he destroyed the Spanish treasure fleet and its French escort at Vigo Bay in 1702.

gingee.s: Gingee, also called Senji, is a town in Viluppuram district of Tamil Nadu, India, known for its great fortress spread over three granite hills. The fort was the seat of the Gingee Nayaks from the early sixteenth century and later passed to Bijapur and the Marathas, whose king…

gresik.s: Gresik is a port town on the north coast of East Java, Indonesia, just north-west of Surabaya. From the fourteenth century it was a busy harbour for Chinese, Gujarati and Javanese traders and an early centre of Islam in Java: Maulana Malik Ibrahim was buried there in 1419, and…

gungnae.s: Gungnae was the second capital of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo, at modern Ji'an on the middle Yalu river in Jilin, China. Tradition dates the move there to 3 CE, and it remained the royal centre until King Jangsu moved the capital to Pyongyang in 427.

gordon-guggisberg.s: Sir Gordon Guggisberg was a Canadian-born British army engineer who was governor of the Gold Coast from 1919 to 1927. His ten-year development plan built Takoradi harbour, railways, roads and the Korle Bu Hospital in Accra, and he founded Achimota School.

great-troubles.s: The Great Troubles were a period of civil war in the Golden Horde from 1359 to 1381, after the murder of Khan Berdi Beg. Over twenty khans rose and fell, while the warlord Mamai ruled the west through puppet khans.

gongola-river.s: The Gongola is a river in north-eastern Nigeria and the largest tributary of the Benue. It rises on the Jos Plateau, flows north-east and then south through Bauchi and Gombe states, and joins the Benue near Numan.

gortyn-code.s: The Gortyn Code is the longest surviving ancient Greek law code, inscribed in the Doric dialect of Crete on a curved stone wall at Gortyn around 450 BCE. Its twelve columns, written in alternating directions, set out rules on marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption, property…

gongmin-of-goryeo.s: Gongmin was king of Goryeo from 1351 to 1374. Raised at the Yuan court and married to the Mongol princess Noguk, he turned against Yuan control as the dynasty weakened, purging the pro-Mongol Gi family in 1356 and recovering northern lands.

gwangjong-of-goryeo.s: Gwangjong was the fourth king of Goryeo, ruling from 949 to 975. To strengthen the crown against powerful clans he freed people who had been wrongly enslaved in 956, introduced civil service examinations on the Chinese model in 958 and purged many great nobles.

gutalag.s: The Gutalag is the medieval law code of Gotland, written in the Old Gutnish language, probably in the thirteenth century. It sets out the rules of the island's self-governing farmers, covering church matters, inheritance, compensation for injuries and the duties of the islanders.

gutasaga.s: The Gutasaga is a short Old Gutnish account of the early history of Gotland, written down in the thirteenth century and preserved with the island's law, the Gutalag. It tells of the legendary settler Tjelvar, who brought fire to the island, of the emigration of part of its…

gutnalthing.s: The Gutnalthing was the general assembly of medieval Gotland, where representatives of the free farmers of the island's districts met to make laws, settle disputes and decide matters of common concern. It met at Roma in the middle of the island and governed Gotland as a…

guarani-people.s: The Guaraní are an indigenous people of South America, living in Paraguay and neighbouring parts of Brazil, Argentina and Bolivia. Spanish settlers at Asunción allied with them from the 1530s, taking Guaraní wives and labour, and from 1609 Jesuit missionaries gathered many of…

guarani-language.s: Guarani is a Tupi–Guarani language of South America and one of the two official languages of Paraguay, alongside Spanish, spoken by most Paraguayans regardless of background. Jesuit missionaries wrote grammars and dictionaries of it in the seventeenth century, and it survived…

gustav-struve.s: Gustav Struve was a German lawyer, journalist and radical republican who, with Friedrich Hecker, led the revolutionary risings in Baden in 1848. After the failure of his own attempt in September 1848 he was imprisoned, freed during the Baden revolution of 1849, and then fled…

guillaume-grand-duke-of-luxembourg.s: Guillaume is Grand Duke of Luxembourg, having succeeded his father Henri on Henri's abdication in October 2025. Born in 1981, the eldest son of Henri and Maria Teresa, he was educated in Luxembourg, Switzerland, Britain and France, trained at Sandhurst, and served as his…

germanisation.s: Germanisation is the spread of the German language, people and culture into other lands, through settlement or state policy. In modern history the term refers above all to Prussian and German policies in Polish lands from the 1830s to 1918, including language laws and the…

galileo-galilei.s: Galileo Galilei was an Italian astronomer, physicist and mathematician whose telescopic discoveries of 1609–1610, including the moons of Jupiter and the phases of Venus, supported the Copernican view of the solar system. Court mathematician to Grand Duke Cosimo II of Tuscany…

george-armstrong-custer.s: George Armstrong Custer was a United States Army officer who rose to fame as a cavalry commander in the American Civil War. After the war he led the 7th Cavalry on the Great Plains, and his expedition of 1874 confirmed the presence of gold in the Black Hills.

great-sioux-reservation.s: The Great Sioux Reservation was the territory reserved for the Lakota and other Sioux by the Treaty of Fort Laramie of 1868, covering present-day South Dakota west of the Missouri River, including the Black Hills. The United States took the Black Hills in 1877 after the Great…

great-sioux-war-of-1876.s: The Great Sioux War of 1876, also called the Black Hills War, was fought between the United States and the Lakota and Northern Cheyenne after gold was found in the Black Hills. Warriors under Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse won at the Rosebud and the Little Bighorn in June 1876,…

graubunden.s: Graubünden, known in French and English as the Grisons, is the largest and easternmost canton of Switzerland, with its capital at Chur. It grew from the Three Leagues, an alliance of the Grey League, the League of God's House and the League of the Ten Jurisdictions, which…

griquatown.s: Griquatown is a small town in the Northern Cape province of South Africa, north of the Orange River. It began as Klaarwater, a London Missionary Society station founded in the early 1800s among the Griqua, and was renamed in 1813, when the missionary John Campbell helped the…

guam-organic-act-of-1950.s: The Guam Organic Act of 1950 is a law of the United States Congress that established Guam as an unincorporated territory with a civilian government. It made the people of Guam US citizens, created an elected legislature and a court system, and moved the island from naval to…

ghent.s: Ghent is a city in Flanders, Belgium, at the meeting of the Scheldt and Lys rivers. In the Middle Ages it was one of the largest cities north of the Alps, rich from the cloth industry and often in revolt against the counts of Flanders.

groningen.s: Groningen is the main city of the northern Netherlands and capital of the province of the same name. A trading town and member of the Hanseatic League in the Middle Ages, it long dominated the surrounding Frisian countryside, the Ommelanden.

georgios-tsolakoglou.s: Georgios Tsolakoglou was a Greek army officer who surrendered the Army of Epirus to the Germans in April 1941 without authority and became the first prime minister of the collaborationist Hellenic State, serving until December 1942. After liberation he was tried and sentenced…

gaius-valerius-caburus.s: Gaius Valerius Caburus was a noble of the Gallic Helvii who received Roman citizenship from the governor Gaius Valerius Flaccus, taking his patron's names. Julius Caesar mentions him as the father of Gaius Valerius Procillus, Caesar's interpreter and envoy, and of Gaius…

gaius-valerius-flaccus.s: Gaius Valerius Flaccus was a Roman politician, consul in 93 BCE, who governed provinces in Spain and Gaul for an unusually long period in the 90s and 80s BCE. He granted Roman citizenship to Gallic nobles, among them the Helvian Caburus, and is named on the Tabula…

glaphyra.s: Glaphyra was a Cappadocian princess, daughter of King Archelaus of Cappadocia. She married Alexander, a son of Herod the Great executed in 7 BCE, then Juba II of Mauretania, and finally Herod Archelaus, ethnarch of Judaea and her first husband's half-brother.

gulf-of-sant-eufemia.s: The Gulf of Sant'Eufemia is a bay of the Tyrrhenian Sea on the western coast of Calabria, southern Italy, at the narrowest point of the peninsula, where only about 30 km of land separates it from the Gulf of Squillace on the Ionian side. Ancient Hipponion, modern Vibo…

guadalquivir.s: The Guadalquivir is the main river of Andalusia in southern Spain, flowing about 650 km west from the Sierra de Cazorla past Córdoba and Seville to the Atlantic at Sanlúcar de Barrameda. Called the Baetis by the Romans, it gave its name to the province of Baetica.

gaius-claudius-pulcher-consul-177-bce.s: Gaius Claudius Pulcher was a Roman politician and general who served as consul in 177 BCE. In that year he completed the conquest of the Histri in Istria, storming their stronghold of Nesactium, after which the Histrian king Epulo took his own life, and he then campaigned…

giovanni-paolo-lascaris.s: Giovanni Paolo Lascaris was Grand Master of the Knights Hospitaller from 1636 to 1657, one of the longest reigns in the order's history. He strengthened the fortifications of Malta and in 1651 approved the purchase of French Caribbean islands, including Saint Kitts and Saint…

gozo.s: Gozo is the second-largest island of the Maltese archipelago, north-west of Malta. It holds the Ġgantija megalithic temples, among the oldest free-standing structures in the world.

george-xi-of-kartli.s: George XI was king of Kartli in eastern Georgia, reigning in 1676-1688 and 1703-1709 under Safavid overlordship. Having accepted Islam, he served the shahs as a commander under the name Gurgin Khan and was made governor of Kandahar to suppress Afghan unrest.

gaius-sempronius-tuditanus.s: Gaius Sempronius Tuditanus was a Roman politician and writer who served as consul in 129 BCE. In that year he campaigned in the north-eastern Adriatic against the Iapydes and other peoples, and he celebrated a triumph over them.

gaspar-de-guzman-count-duke-of-olivares.n: Gaspar de Guzmán, Count-Duke of Olivares
gaspar-de-guzman-count-duke-of-olivares.s: Gaspar de Guzmán, Count-Duke of Olivares, was the chief minister of Philip IV of Spain from 1621 to 1643. He sought to restore Spanish power in the Thirty Years' War and to share its costs among all the king's realms through the Union of Arms.

gauja.s: The Gauja is a river in Latvia, about 450 kilometres long, flowing through Vidzeme to the Gulf of Riga. Its lower valley, with towns such as Sigulda and Turaida, was the land of the Livonians and was conquered by German crusaders in the early 13th century.

gentius.s: Gentius was the last king of the Ardiaean Illyrian kingdom, ruling from Scodra on the eastern Adriatic coast from about 181 BCE. Allied with Perseus of Macedon in the Third Macedonian War, he was defeated by the Roman praetor Lucius Anicius Gallus in 168 BCE, captured at…

gorizia.s: Gorizia is a town on the Isonzo river in north-eastern Italy, on the border with Slovenia. From around 1100 it was the seat of the counts of Gorizia, who built up lands in Friuli, Carinthia and Tyrol, and in 1500 it passed to the Habsburgs.

ghalib-alhinai.s: Ghalib ibn Ali al-Hinai was the last Imam of Oman, elected in 1954 after the death of Muhammad al-Khalili. His attempts to win international recognition for the interior imamate, amid disputes over oil concessions, led to conflict with the Sultan of Muscat, who with British…

golden-madonna-of-essen.s: The Golden Madonna of Essen is a statue of the Virgin and Child made around 980 for Essen Abbey, probably under Abbess Mathilde. Carved in poplar wood and covered with sheet gold, it is the oldest known fully sculpted figure of the Virgin in the Western world.

guebwiller.s: Guebwiller is a town in the Haut-Rhin department of Alsace, France, at the entrance to the Florival valley of the southern Vosges. It was the main town of the territory of the prince-abbots of Murbach, who moved their seat there in the 18th century and built its neoclassical…

gorze-abbey.s: Gorze Abbey was a Benedictine monastery near Metz in Lorraine, founded in 757 by Bishop Chrodegang of Metz. Restored in 933 by Bishop Adalbero I of Metz under Abbot Einold and John of Gorze, it became the centre of a reform movement that spread strict monastic observance to…

gondophares.s: Gondophares was the founder of the Indo-Parthian Kingdom, ruling in the early 1st century CE over Sistan, Arachosia, Gandhara and Taxila, which he took from the Indo-Scythians. The Takht-i-Bahi inscription is dated to his 26th regnal year.

golasecca-culture.s: The Golasecca culture was an Iron Age culture of north-western Italy and southern Switzerland, from about the 9th to the 4th century BCE, named after a site near Lake Maggiore. Its people traded between the Etruscans and the Celts north of the Alps and wrote inscriptions in…

garda-siochana.s: The Garda Síochána, 'Guardians of the Peace', is the national police force of Ireland, founded in 1922 to replace the Royal Irish Constabulary in the Irish Free State. Unusually for the time and place, it was established as a largely unarmed force.

great-peacemaker.s: The Great Peacemaker, Deganawida, is the founder of the Iroquois Confederacy in Haudenosaunee tradition. Said to have been born among the Huron, he brought a message of peace to the warring Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca and, with his spokesman Hiawatha, persuaded…

gulbuddin-hekmatyar.s: Gulbuddin Hekmatyar is an Afghan Islamist leader who founded the Hezb-e Islami party in the 1970s and became one of the main mujahideen commanders against the Soviet Union, receiving much Pakistani and American aid. In the civil war after 1992 his forces shelled Kabul heavily.

galeazzo-ciano.s: Galeazzo Ciano was an Italian Fascist politician, Benito Mussolini's son-in-law and foreign minister from 1936 to 1943. His diaries are a major source for Fascist foreign policy.

gnaeus-pompeius-strabo.s: Gnaeus Pompeius Strabo was a Roman general and politician, the father of Pompey the Great. As consul in 89 BCE he commanded in the Social War, captured the rebel city of Asculum after a long siege, and passed a law granting Latin rights to Transpadane Gaul.

gaius-papius-mutilus.s: Gaius Papius Mutilus was a Samnite general and one of the two consuls of the rebel Italian confederation in the Social War of 91–87 BCE. He led the southern rebel forces, invading Campania and taking several towns, but was defeated by Sulla.

gangadhar-rao.s: Gangadhar Rao was the Maratha Raja of Jhansi of the Newalkar family, who ruled until his death in 1853. He married Manikarnika, later famous as Rani Lakshmibai.

gyeongju.s: Gyeongju is a city in south-eastern South Korea that was the capital of Silla for nearly a thousand years, until 935. It is rich in royal tombs, temples and palace sites, including Bulguksa temple, the Seokguram grotto and the Cheomseongdae observatory, and its historic areas…

gyeongguk-daejeon.s: The Gyeongguk daejeon, or National Code, was the basic law code of Joseon Korea. Compilation began under King Sejo, and it was completed and promulgated in 1485 under King Seongjong.

gulf-of-oristano.s: The Gulf of Oristano is a wide bay on the west coast of Sardinia, Italy, bordered by lagoons and wetlands. The ancient city of Tharros stood on the Sinis peninsula at its northern end, and the town of Oristano lies just inland.

gallura.s: Gallura is a region of north-eastern Sardinia, Italy, known for its granite hills, cork oak forests and indented coast. In the Middle Ages it formed one of the four Sardinian judicates, with its capital at Civita, near modern Olbia.

govinda-chandra-narayan.s: Govinda Chandra Narayan was the last king of the Kachari kingdom in north-east India. Driven out by rivals and by the Burmese invasions of the early 1820s, he was restored under British protection after the First Anglo-Burmese War.

gwalior-fort.s: Gwalior Fort is a hill fort above the city of Gwalior in Madhya Pradesh, India, one of the strongest fortresses of northern India. Held by successive dynasties, including the Kachchhapaghatas and Tomaras, it contains the Teli ka Mandir and Sas-Bahu temples, Jain rock-cut…

goa-velha.s: Goa Velha, the ancient Gopakapattana, is a village on the Zuari river in Goa, India, that was the capital and main port of the Kadambas of Goa from the 11th century. Its harbour traded with Arabia, East Africa and Gujarat, and Arab merchants settled there.

ganapati-kakatiya.s: Ganapatideva was the longest-reigning ruler of the Kakatiya dynasty, governing from Warangal from 1199 to 1262. He united most Telugu-speaking lands, extending Kakatiya rule to the coastal Andhra country, and encouraged foreign trade through the port of Motupalli.

gangeyadeva.s: Gangeyadeva was a king of the Kalachuris of Tripuri in central India in the early 11th century. He took the title Vikramaditya and expanded the kingdom northwards, extending his rule as far as Varanasi.

gajayana.s: Gajayana was a king of Kanjuruhan in East Java in the mid-8th century, known from the Dinoyo inscription of 760. The son of King Dewasimha, he built a temple to the sage Agastya near modern Malang and replaced an old wooden image of the sage with one of black stone, endowing…

gallipoli.s: Gallipoli (Turkish Gelibolu) is a town and peninsula on the European shore of the Dardanelles in north-western Turkey, known in antiquity as the Thracian Chersonese. The Ottomans seized the town in 1354 after an earthquake damaged its walls, gaining their first lasting…

gallipoli-campaign.s: The Gallipoli campaign was an Allied attempt in the First World War to force the Dardanelles and knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war. British, French, Australian and New Zealand troops landed on the Gallipoli peninsula in April 1915 but were held by Ottoman forces,…

ghiyath-al-din-tughluq.s: Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq, earlier known as Ghazi Malik, was sultan of Delhi from 1320 to 1325 and founder of the Tughluq dynasty. A frontier commander who had fought the Mongols, he seized power after the fall of the Khalji dynasty and built the fortress city of Tughlaqabad.

gobarau-minaret.s: The Gobarau Minaret is a tall mud-brick tower in Katsina, northern Nigeria, the remnant of a mosque traditionally dated to the late 15th or early 16th century. Tradition links it to the first Muslim king of Katsina, Muhammadu Korau.

garhwal.s: Garhwal is the western of the two divisions of Uttarakhand in the central Himalaya of India, containing the sources of the Ganges and Yamuna and the shrines of Badrinath and Kedarnath. It took its name from the many forts (garh) of local chiefs, united by the Panwar dynasty.

gulag.s: The Gulag was the Soviet system of forced labour camps, named from the acronym of its Main Camps Administration, set up in 1930. Millions of people, many of them political prisoners, were held in camps across Siberia, the far north and Kazakhstan, where they worked on mines,…

ghat.s: Ghat is an oasis town in south-western Libya, near the Algerian border. It was a key stop on the trans-Saharan caravan route from Tripoli to Kano and a centre of the Kel Ajjer Tuareg.

gaur.s: Gaur, also known as Lakhnauti, is a ruined city in the Malda district of West Bengal, India, on the border with Bangladesh. It was a capital of the Sena kings and, from the early 13th century, of Bengal's Muslim rulers, and under the Bengal Sultanate it became one of the…

garhjat-states.s: The Garhjat states were the small princely states of the hill and forest country of Odisha, whose name refers to the forts, garh, from which their Rajas ruled. Under British rule most were grouped as the Orissa Tributary States, including Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar, Dhenkanal and…

gardizi.s: Gardizi was a Persian historian of the 11th century, from Gardez in eastern Afghanistan, who wrote the Zayn al-Akhbar around 1050 for the Ghaznavid sultan Abd al-Rashid. The work is a history of Persia and Khurasan, and its chapter on the Turks and their neighbours is a key…

godred-olafsson.s: Godred Olafsson was king of Mann and the Isles from 1153 to 1187, son of Olaf I. His harsh rule drove some island chiefs to support his brother-in-law Somerled, who fought him in a sea battle off Islay in 1156 and in 1158 drove him from the kingdom.

gregory-the-illuminator.s: Gregory the Illuminator was the founder and first head of the Armenian Church. According to tradition he was imprisoned for years in a pit at Khor Virap by King Tiridates III, then healed and converted the king, so that Armenia adopted Christianity as its state religion in the…

gerald-durrell.s: Gerald Durrell was a British naturalist, writer and conservationist. He led animal-collecting expeditions to Cameroon, British Guiana and elsewhere and described them in popular books such as The Bafut Beagles, while My Family and Other Animals told of his childhood on Corfu.

gross-national-happiness.s: Gross National Happiness is a development philosophy associated with Bhutan, usually traced to the fourth king, Jigme Singye Wangchuck, who in the 1970s declared it more important than gross national product. It holds that policy should balance economic growth with cultural…

great-lakes-twa.s: The Twa are a Pygmy people of the African Great Lakes, living in Rwanda, Burundi, eastern Congo and south-western Uganda, where they form a small minority. Traditionally forest hunters and potters, some also held ritual and court roles in the kingdoms of Rwanda and Burundi.

gafsa.s: Gafsa is a city in west-central Tunisia, built around an oasis at the edge of the desert. As Capsa it was a Numidian town taken by Marius in the Jugurthine War, then a Roman town and a Byzantine stronghold; in the 6th century it was the centre of the Berber principality of…

germania-inferior.s: Germania Inferior was a Roman province on the lower Rhine, covering parts of the present-day Netherlands, Belgium and western Germany, with its capital at Cologne (Colonia Agrippina). Organised as a province around 85 CE, it was a frontier zone guarded by legions along the Rhine.

ghezo.s: Ghezo was king of Dahomey, in present-day Benin, from 1818 to 1858. He came to power in a coup against his brother Adandozan, ended Dahomey's tribute to the Oyo Empire in 1823 and expanded the army, including the corps of women soldiers.

gruffydd-ap-llywelyn.s: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn was king of Gwynedd and Powys from 1039 and, from about 1055, ruler of nearly all of Wales, the only king ever to unite it. He defeated English and Welsh rivals, raided across the border with Mercian allies and took lands east of Offa's Dyke.

gruffydd-ap-gwenwynwyn.s: Gruffydd ap Gwenwynwyn was prince of Powys Wenwynwyn in mid-Wales in the 13th century. He alternated between alliance and conflict with Llywelyn ap Gruffudd of Gwynedd, plotting against him in 1274, and supported Edward I in the conquest of Wales in 1282–1283.

gorm-the-old.s: Gorm the Old was king of Denmark from about 936 until his death around 958, and is regarded as the founder of the continuous Danish royal line. He ruled from Jelling in central Jutland, where he raised a runestone in memory of his wife Thyra.

gar-tongtsen.s: Gar Tongtsen Yulsung was chief minister of the Tibetan Empire under Songtsen Gampo and, after his death, effective regent for the young Mangsong Mangtsen. Tibetan tradition credits him with negotiating Songtsen Gampo's marriage to the Chinese princess Wencheng, and he directed…

gonpo-namgyal.s: Gönpo Namgyal was a chieftain of Nyarong in Kham, eastern Tibet, who in the mid-19th century built a regional power by conquest. From 1848 he overran neighbouring states including Derge, until an army sent by the Tibetan government at Lhasa defeated him in 1865 and he died in…

gebel-adda.s: Gebel Adda was a fortified hilltop town on the east bank of the Nile in Lower Nubia, near the modern border of Egypt and Sudan. Occupied from the Meroitic period into Ottoman times, it is generally identified with Daw, the late medieval seat of the Nubian kingdom of Dotawo.

gildas.s: Gildas was a 6th-century British monk whose Latin work On the Ruin of Britain (De Excidio Britanniae) is the only contemporary narrative source for post-Roman Britain. In it he denounced five British kings, among them Constantine of Dumnonia, Vortiporius of the Demetae and…

gwallawg-ap-lleenog.s: Gwallawg ap Lleenog was a 6th-century British king in northern Britain, possibly of Elmet. Poems attributed to Taliesin praise him, and the Historia Brittonum names him among the kings who fought with Urien of Rheged against the Angles of Bernicia.

gibe-river.s: The Gibe is a river of south-western Ethiopia that rises in the highlands west of Addis Ababa and flows south to become the Omo. Its basin, the Gibe region, was home to Ennarea and other Gonga kingdoms and, from the 19th century, to the Oromo kingdoms of Limmu-Ennarea, Gumma,…

guan-people.s: The Guan are a group of peoples of Ghana who speak Guang languages and are thought to be among the earliest inhabitants of the region. Guan communities live in scattered areas from the coast, including the Efutu of Winneba, to the Akuapem ridge and the Volta basin, and many…

galician-portuguese.s: Galician-Portuguese was the Romance language of medieval Galicia and northern Portugal, from which modern Galician and Portuguese developed. From the late 12th to the mid-14th century it was the main language of lyric poetry across the Iberian kingdoms, used by troubadours and…

gadaladeniya-vihara.s: Gadaladeniya is a Buddhist temple near Kandy in central Sri Lanka, built in 1344 under King Bhuvanaikabahu IV of Gampola. Designed by a south Indian architect, its stone shrine combines Sinhalese and Dravidian styles and is one of the finest monuments of the Gampola period.

gusti-agung-maruti.s: Gusti Agung Maruti was a chief minister of the Balinese kingdom of Gelgel who seized power from his king around 1651. He held Gelgel until 1686, when he was defeated by princes of the old dynasty, who then established a new royal seat at Klungkung.

giovanni-chiarini.s: Giovanni Chiarini was an Italian engineer and explorer who joined Antonio Cecchi's expedition to the Gibe region of south-western Ethiopia. Seized with Cecchi by the rulers of the kingdom of Gera in 1879, he died in captivity there later that year.

gyorgy-dozsa.s: György Dózsa was a Székely soldier from Transylvania chosen to lead a crusade against the Ottomans proclaimed in Hungary in 1514. The mostly peasant army turned against the nobility instead, and the revolt spread across the kingdom before it was crushed near Temesvár.

grattans-parliament.s: Grattan's Parliament is the name given to the Irish Parliament between 1782 and 1800, after it won legislative independence from Westminster through the repeal of the Declaratory Act and changes to Poynings' Law. Named after the patriot leader Henry Grattan, it remained an…

giuseppe-prina.s: Giuseppe Prina was finance minister of the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy from 1805. His heavy taxes, raised to pay for Napoleon's wars, made him widely hated.

gojeb-river.s: The Gojeb is a river of south-western Ethiopia, a tributary of the Omo. Rising in the western highlands, it flows east through forested country and long formed the northern boundary of the Kingdom of Kaffa, separating it from the Gibe kingdoms such as Jimma, and the frontier…

gremi.s: Gremi is a 16th-century architectural complex in Kakheti, eastern Georgia, the remains of the royal town built by King Levan of Kakheti. Founded around 1565, it was a thriving town on the trade route between Persia and Russia until Shah Abbas I destroyed it in 1615–1616.

gidan-rumfa.s: Gidan Rumfa is the palace of the emir of Kano in northern Nigeria, built by Sarki Muhammad Rumfa in the late 15th century. Set in a large walled compound, it has remained the royal residence ever since, used by the Fulani emirs after the jihad of the early 19th century, and is…

george-iv-of-the-united-kingdom.n: George IV of the United Kingdom
george-iv-of-the-united-kingdom.s: George IV was king of the United Kingdom and of Hanover from 1820 to 1830, after ruling as Prince Regent from 1811 during the illness of his father George III. Known for his extravagance and his patronage of architecture, including the Brighton Pavilion, he was unpopular for…

george-iv-of-georgia.s: George IV, known as Lasha Giorgi, was king of Georgia from 1213 to 1223, the son of Queen Tamar. He continued his mother's wars against neighbouring Muslim rulers and planned to join the Fifth Crusade, but in 1221 a Mongol force under Jebe and Subutai defeated him at Khunan.

great-mahele.s: The Great Māhele was the land division of 1848 in the Kingdom of Hawaii, carried out under King Kamehameha III. It divided the land, previously held under the chiefs, among the crown, the government and the chiefs, and later laws allowed commoners and, from 1850, foreigners to…

guanzhong.s: Guanzhong is the Wei River valley in Shaanxi province, China, a fertile basin enclosed by mountains and guarded passes. Its strategic strength made it the base of the Qin state and the seat of the capitals of Western Han, Sui and Tang at Chang'an, modern Xi'an.

gagik-abas-of-kars.s: Gagik-Abas was the last king of Kars, the Armenian Bagratid kingdom of Vanand in north-eastern Anatolia, reigning from 1029 to 1065. After the Byzantine annexation of Ani in 1045 and the Seljuk sack of the city in 1064, he ceded Kars to the Byzantine Empire in exchange for…

glele.s: Glele was king of Dahomey from 1858 to 1889, succeeding his father Ghezo. He continued Dahomey's yearly wars and slave raids against the Yoruba, destroying Ketu in 1886, and maintained the annual customs with their human sacrifices.

gomti-river.s: The Gomti is a tributary of the Ganges in Uttar Pradesh, India, rising near Pilibhit and flowing about 900 km south-east past Lucknow and Jaunpur before joining the Ganges below Varanasi. In ancient times it bounded the kingdom of Kosala, and it is named in the Rigveda and…

gurung.s: The Gurung, who call themselves Tamu, are a people of the hills of central Nepal, especially around the Annapurna range in Lamjung, Kaski and Gorkha. Speaking a Tibeto-Burman language and following Buddhist, shamanic and Hindu practices, they served as soldiers in the armies…

gubazes-ii-of-lazica.s: Gubazes II was king of Lazica in western Georgia from about 541 to 555. Resenting Byzantine control, he invited the Sasanian king Khosrow I into Lazica in 541, starting the Lazic War, but soon turned back to the Byzantine side.

glendalough.s: Glendalough is a glacial valley in the Wicklow Mountains of eastern Ireland, the site of an early medieval monastery founded by St Kevin in the 6th century. It became one of Ireland's leading monastic centres and places of pilgrimage, and its round tower, cathedral, churches…

gauteng.s: Gauteng is the smallest but most populous province of South Africa, created in 1994 from part of the old Transvaal province around the Witwatersrand. It contains Johannesburg, the country's largest city, and Pretoria, the administrative capital, and grew from the gold rush…

gyges-of-lydia.s: Gyges was king of Lydia from around 680 BCE and founder of the Mermnad dynasty. Herodotus tells how he killed the last Heraclid king, Candaules, and took his throne and queen.

gediz-river.s: The Gediz, the ancient Hermus, is a river of western Anatolia in Turkey that flows about 400 kilometres from the highlands near Kütahya to the Aegean north of İzmir. Its fertile plain was the heartland of the Kingdom of Lydia, with Sardis on its tributary the Pactolus, and…

gjakova.s: Gjakova, in Serbian Đakovica, is a city in western Kosovo, in the Metohija plain near the Albanian border. It grew in the Ottoman period around a market and the Hadum Mosque.

greenland.s: Greenland is the world's largest island, lying between the North Atlantic and Arctic oceans, and an autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark. Norse settlers led by Erik the Red founded colonies there around 985, which accepted Norwegian rule in 1261 but died out in the…

gordion.s: Gordion was the capital of ancient Phrygia, on the Sakarya River west of modern Ankara in Turkey. Its citadel, with large megaron halls, was destroyed by fire around 800 BCE and rebuilt.

gerard-of-roussillon.s: Gerard of Roussillon was a Frankish count, a supporter of the emperor Lothar I, who governed the kingdom of Provence for the young king Charles of Provence from 855. As count of Vienne he defended the kingdom against Charles the Bald and fought Vikings who raided up the Rhône…

griffin-warrior-tomb.s: The Griffin Warrior Tomb is a shaft grave of the early Mycenaean period near the Palace of Nestor at Pylos, discovered in 2015 by Jack Davis and Sharon Stocker. Dating from about 1450 BCE, it held a warrior buried with more than 1,400 objects, including weapons, gold rings, an…

godavaya.s: Godavaya is an archaeological site on the south coast of Sri Lanka, near the mouth of the Walawe river in Hambantota District. An ancient harbour there is recorded in an early inscription granting its customs dues to a Buddhist monastery, and a shipwreck found offshore, dated…

gwgon-ap-meurig.s: Gwgon ap Meurig was the last native king of Seisyllwg in south-west Wales. The Annales Cambriae record that he drowned in 871.

gracanica-monastery.s: Gračanica Monastery is a Serbian Orthodox monastery near Pristina in Kosovo, built by King Stefan Milutin around 1321. Its five-domed church is one of the finest works of late Byzantine-style architecture in the Balkans, and its interior is covered with frescoes, including…

gangtok.s: Gangtok is the capital and largest town of the Indian state of Sikkim, on a ridge in the eastern Himalayas. It became the capital of the kingdom of Sikkim in 1894, replacing Tumlong, and grew as a stop on the trade route between India and Tibet through the Nathu La pass.

guelowar.s: The Guelowar were a maternal royal lineage of Mandinka origin from Kaabu that, according to Serer tradition, settled in the Serer country of present-day Senegal around the 14th century. Marrying into the old Serer landholding families, they supplied the kings of Sine and…

glasgow.s: Glasgow is the largest city in Scotland, on the River Clyde. Tradition makes it the site of Saint Kentigern's church in the 6th century, and it grew around its medieval cathedral and the university founded in 1451.

govan.s: Govan is a district on the south bank of the River Clyde in Glasgow, Scotland. After the Vikings took Dumbarton Rock in 870 it became a royal and religious centre of the kingdom of Strathclyde, and Govan Old Parish Church holds a collection of carved stones of the 9th to 11th…

gallo-romans.s: The Gallo-Romans were the Romanised inhabitants of Gaul from the Roman conquest to the early Middle Ages. Speaking Latin and following Roman law and, by the 5th century, mostly Catholic Christianity, they formed the majority under the Visigothic, Burgundian and Frankish…

godomar-ii.s: Godomar II was the last king of the Burgundians, reigning from 524 to 534. He succeeded his brother Sigismund, who had been captured and killed by the Franks, and defeated the Franks at Vézeronce in 524.

gundahar.s: Gundahar was a king of the Burgundians in the early 5th century who, as a Roman ally, set up a Burgundian kingdom on the Rhine around 411, traditionally centred on Worms. When the Burgundians raided Roman territory, the general Aetius had them crushed by Hunnic troops in 436,…

gundobad.s: Gundobad was king of the Burgundians from about 473 to 516, after serving as a Roman general and briefly as kingmaker in Italy, where he raised Glycerius to the throne in 473. In his kingdom in the Rhône valley he issued the law code known as the Lex Burgundionum for his…

gepids.s: The Gepids were an East Germanic people closely related to the Goths, settled north of the lower Danube by the 3rd century. Subjects of the Huns under Attila, they led the revolt that won the Battle of Nedao in 454 and then ruled the Tisza plain and Transylvania, later taking…

gloucester.s: Gloucester is a cathedral city on the River Severn in western England. It began as the Roman legionary fortress and colonia of Glevum, fell to the West Saxons after 577 and became a centre of the Hwicce and of Mercia.

grigol-of-khandzta.s: Grigol of Khandzta was a Georgian monk and saint who founded the monastery of Khandzta in Klarjeti and organised a network of monasteries in the south-western borderlands of Georgia. Supported by the Bagratid princes, his foundations became centres of learning, manuscript…

garmul.s: Garmul was a Berber king in western North Africa who attacked Byzantine Africa in the 570s, killing several imperial commanders, including the praetorian prefect Theodore. In 578 the Byzantine general Gennadius defeated and killed him.

gennadius-exarch-of-africa.s: Gennadius was a Byzantine general who became military commander in Africa and, by the 590s, its first known exarch. In 578 he defeated and killed the Berber king Garmul, who had raided imperial territory.

giso.s: Giso was queen of the Rugians, wife of King Feletheus. Eugippius' Life of Saint Severinus portrays her as a harsh Arian who tried to rebaptise Catholics and was rebuked by the saint.

geats.s: The Geats were a North Germanic people of what is now southern Sweden, centred on Västergötland and Östergötland around lakes Vänern and Vättern. They appear in Ptolemy and Jordanes and as the hero's people in the Old English poem Beowulf.

gamla-uppsala.s: Gamla Uppsala is a village and ancient royal site north of modern Uppsala in Sweden. Its great burial mounds date from the 5th and 6th centuries, and Adam of Bremen described a pagan temple there in the 11th century.

great-st-bernard-pass.s: The Great St Bernard Pass is an Alpine pass at about 2,470 metres linking the Swiss canton of Valais with the Aosta valley in Italy. Used since Roman times, it carried traffic between northern Europe and Italy throughout the Middle Ages.

ghositarama.s: The Ghositarama was a Buddhist monastery at Kaushambi, the capital of Vatsa in northern India, said to have been given to the Buddha's community by the banker Ghosita. Buddhist texts record that the Buddha stayed there several times.

guthrum.s: Guthrum was a Danish Viking leader who became king of East Anglia. A commander of the Great Heathen Army, he nearly conquered Wessex in early 878 but was defeated by Alfred the Great at Edington.

gbe-languages.s: The Gbe languages are a group of closely related languages of the Volta–Niger family spoken from south-eastern Ghana through Togo and Benin to south-western Nigeria. The largest are Ewe and Fon, and others include Aja, Gun and Gen.

gurage-people.s: The Gurage are a people of south-central Ethiopia living south-west of Addis Ababa, mainly in the Gurage Zone. They speak a group of Ethiopian Semitic languages and traditionally farm enset, the false banana.

gottlieb-daimler.s: Gottlieb Daimler was a German engineer and industrialist from Württemberg and a pioneer of the motor car. Working with Wilhelm Maybach in Cannstatt, he developed a light, fast-running petrol engine in the 1880s and fitted it to a motorcycle and a carriage in 1885–1886.

guthfrith-of-york.s: Guthfrith was a Viking king of York who ruled Northumbria from about 883 until his death in 895. Later sources say that he was chosen king with the support of the community of St Cuthbert.

gopalarajavamshavali.s: The Gopalarajavamshavali is a chronicle of the kings of Nepal, written partly in Sanskrit and partly in Nepal Bhasa and compiled in the late 14th century, probably under King Jayasthiti Malla. It lists the dynasties of the Kathmandu Valley from the legendary cowherd kings and…

georg-hohermuth-von-speyer.s: Georg Hohermuth von Speyer was a German conquistador who served as governor of Venezuela for the Welser company from 1535. He led a long expedition from Coro across the llanos towards the eastern Andes between 1535 and 1538 in search of gold, losing most of his men to disease,…

guwahati.s: Guwahati is the largest city of Assam, in north-eastern India, on the south bank of the Brahmaputra. In ancient times, as Pragjyotishpura, it was a capital of the kingdom of Kamarupa, and the Kamakhya temple on Nilachal hill is a major Hindu pilgrimage site.

gwangmu-reform.s: The Gwangmu Reform was the modernisation programme of the Korean Empire, named after Emperor Gojong's era name Gwangmu, used from 1897 to 1907. Seeking to strengthen the state and the throne, the government surveyed land and issued land titles, founded schools, banks and…

goulfey.s: Goulfey is a town in the Far North Region of Cameroon, near the Chari River and the border with Chad, on the plains south of Lake Chad. It was one of the walled Kotoko towns that had become small kingdoms by the 16th century, paying tribute to Bornu, and its sultan remains a…

gandhari-language.s: Gandhari is a Middle Indo-Aryan language, or Prakrit, of the ancient region of Gandhara in what is now north-western Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan. Written in the Kharoshthi script, it was used for inscriptions, Buddhist texts and administration from the 3rd century BCE to…

girsu.s: Girsu was a Sumerian city in southern Iraq, at the mound now called Telloh, and the religious and political capital of the state of Lagash for much of the 3rd millennium BCE. It was the cult centre of the god Ningirsu, whose temple Eninnu was rebuilt by Gudea around 2100 BCE.

gudea.s: Gudea was a ruler of the Sumerian city-state of Lagash around 2100 BCE, in the period between the fall of the Akkadian Empire and the rise of the Third Dynasty of Ur. He is known for an unusual number of temple-building inscriptions and some two dozen diorite statues showing…

gudea-cylinders.s: The Gudea Cylinders are two large terracotta cylinders inscribed in Sumerian around 2125 BCE, recording how Gudea, ruler of Lagash, rebuilt the Eninnu temple of the god Ningirsu at Girsu after a dream. With about 1,400 lines, they form the longest surviving text in Sumerian…

gurzil.s: Gurzil was a Berber god worshipped by the Laguatan and other tribes of Tripolitania in late antiquity, represented as a bull and said to be the son of the god Ammon and a cow. The Latin poet Corippus describes his image being carried into battle against the Byzantines in the…

ganges-yamuna-doab.s: The Ganges–Yamuna Doab is the fertile alluvial land between the Ganges and Yamuna rivers in western Uttar Pradesh, India, stretching from the Shivalik foothills to their confluence at Prayagraj. One of the most productive farming regions of South Asia, it was the heartland of…

gerrit-van-wuysthoff.s: Gerrit van Wuysthoff was a merchant of the Dutch East India Company who led a trading mission up the Mekong from Cambodia to Vientiane, the capital of Lan Xang, in 1641 and 1642. His journal is one of the first European accounts of Laos, describing the court of King Sourigna…

gorgias.s: Gorgias was a Greek sophist and orator from Leontini in Sicily. Sent as ambassador to Athens in 427 BCE, he amazed the Athenians with his ornate style and helped spread the art of rhetoric in Greece.

gungunum.s: Gungunum was an Amorite king of Larsa in southern Mesopotamia. Larsa had stood in the shadow of Isin, but he captured Ur around 1926 BCE, gaining control of the trade through the Gulf, and took the royal titles of king of Sumer and Akkad.

gyeongae-of-silla.s: Gyeongae was king of Silla from 924 to 927, during the Later Three Kingdoms period, when Silla had shrunk to a small state around its capital. In 927 Gyeon Hwon of Later Baekje sacked the capital at Gyeongju and forced the king to take his own life, placing Gyeongsun on the…

gyeon-singeom.s: Gyeon Singeom was the last king of Later Baekje in Korea. In 935 he deposed and imprisoned his father, the founder Gyeon Hwon, who had chosen a younger son as heir.

gaudavaho.s: The Gaudavaho, 'the slaying of the Gauda king', is a Prakrit poem written in the 8th century by Vakpatiraja, court poet of Yashovarman of Kannauj. It celebrates Yashovarman's campaigns, including his victory over a king of Gauda and Magadha, though the slaying itself is only…

gulf-of-mirabello.s: The Gulf of Mirabello is a large bay on the north coast of eastern Crete, Greece. The ancient cities of Lato and Olous, the Minoan town of Gournia and the modern town of Agios Nikolaos lie on or near its shores.

generalkommissariat-lettland.s: The Generalkommissariat Lettland was the German civil administration of occupied Latvia during the Second World War, part of the Reichskommissariat Ostland. Headed by Generalkommissar Otto-Heinrich Drechsler from Riga, it ruled through German officials with a Latvian…

gusinje.s: Gusinje is a small town in eastern Montenegro, close to the Albanian border in the Prokletije mountains. The Congress of Berlin awarded it and Plav to Montenegro in 1878, but Albanians of the League of Prizren fought to keep them, and the great powers gave Montenegro the port…

girolamo-durazzo.s: Girolamo Luigi Durazzo was a Genoese nobleman and politician of the Durazzo family, one of the leading houses of the old Republic of Genoa. Under the constitution of 1802 he became the only doge of the Ligurian Republic, a French client state.

guernica.s: Guernica (Basque: Gernika) is a town in Biscay in the Basque Country of northern Spain. Its oak tree was the meeting place of the Juntas Generales of Biscay, where the lords of Biscay swore to uphold the province's fueros, and it remains a symbol of Basque liberties.

grutte-pier.s: Grutte Pier (Pier Gerlofs Donia) was a Frisian farmer and rebel leader, famed for his size and strength. After Saxon troops burned his village of Kimswerd in 1515, he waged a guerrilla war against the Saxon and Habsburg rulers of Friesland with the support of Charles of…

gaels.s: The Gaels are the Gaelic-speaking peoples of Ireland, Scotland and the Isle of Man, who share a common origin in early medieval Ireland. From the kingdom of Dál Riata in Argyll, Gaelic language and culture spread through Scotland, and the merging of Gaels and Picts in the 9th…

george-van-lalaing-count-of-rennenberg.n: George van Lalaing, Count of Rennenberg
george-van-lalaing-count-of-rennenberg.s: George van Lalaing, Count of Rennenberg, was a nobleman from the southern Netherlands who served as stadtholder of Friesland, Groningen, Drenthe and Overijssel during the Dutch Revolt. A Catholic who had sided with the rebel States-General, he went over to the Spanish side in…

galeazzo-maria-sforza.s: Galeazzo Maria Sforza was Duke of Milan from 1466 to 1476, eldest son of Francesco Sforza and Bianca Maria Visconti. He kept a lavish court, patronised music and art, and married his illegitimate daughter Caterina Sforza to Girolamo Riario.

gaildorf.s: Gaildorf is a small town on the Kocher river in north-eastern Baden-Württemberg, Germany. From the late Middle Ages it was a residence of the Schenks of Limpurg, whose castle still stands in the town, and the seat of one of their branches after the family divided.

gustrow.s: Güstrow is a town in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern in north-eastern Germany, south of Rostock. Founded under German law in the 13th century, it became a seat of the lords of Werle and later the residence of the dukes of Mecklenburg-Güstrow, whose Renaissance castle still dominates…

giusto-de-menabuoi.s: Giusto de' Menabuoi was a Florentine painter who worked mainly in Padua under the Carrara lords. His masterpiece is the fresco cycle of the Padua Baptistery, painted in the 1370s for Fina Buzzacarini, wife of Francesco I da Carrara, with a dome showing Christ surrounded by…

galeazzo-malatesta.s: Galeazzo Malatesta, nicknamed 'the Inept', was lord of Pesaro from 1429 to 1445. Burdened by debts and threatened by his cousin Sigismondo Pandolfo Malatesta, in 1445 he sold Pesaro to Alessandro Sforza, husband of his granddaughter Costanza da Varano, and Fossombrone to…

gattilusio.s: The Gattilusio were a Genoese family who ruled the island of Lesbos and other northern Aegean territories from 1355 to 1462. Their power began when Francesco I Gattilusio helped Emperor John V Palaiologos regain his throne and received Lesbos as a dowry.

guido-i-da-polenta.s: Guido I da Polenta, called the Elder, was lord of Ravenna from 1275 to 1297 and founder of the da Polenta lordship. A Guelph leader, he took control of the city with the help of the Malatesta of Rimini, and sealed the alliance by marrying his daughter Francesca to Giovanni…

generality-lands.s: The Generality Lands were territories of the Dutch Republic governed directly by the States General rather than forming provinces of their own. Conquered mainly from the Spanish Netherlands during the Eighty Years' War, they included States Brabant, States Flanders and parts…

giovanni-malatesta.s: Giovanni Malatesta, known as Gianciotto, was a son of Malatesta da Verucchio, lord of Rimini, and served as podestà of Pesaro. Married for political reasons to Francesca da Polenta of Ravenna, he killed her and his brother Paolo around 1285 after discovering their love affair.

gamprin.s: Gamprin is a small municipality in the Unterland of Liechtenstein, on the Eschnerberg, comprising the villages of Gamprin and Bendern. On the church hill at Bendern the people of the Lordship of Schellenberg swore allegiance to Prince Hans-Adam I of Liechtenstein in 1699.

glauchau.s: Glauchau is a town on the Zwickauer Mulde in western Saxony, Germany. From the late 12th century it was the main seat of the Schönburg family, whose two castles, Forderglauchau and Hinterglauchau, still stand there.

ghiyath-al-din-muhammad-damghani.s: Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad Damghani was sultan of Madurai, in southern India, from about 1340 to 1345. Ibn Battuta, his brother-in-law through marriage into the family of Sultan Ahsan Shah, visited his court in 1344 and described his cruelty towards Hindu captives and an epidemic…

gangadevi.s: Gangadevi was a 14th-century poet and princess of the Vijayanagara Empire, wife of the prince Kumara Kampana. Her Sanskrit poem Madhura Vijayam, also called Vira Kamparaya Charitam, describes her husband's campaigns against the Sambuvarayas and the Madurai Sultanate.

goncalo-caetano-pereira.s: Gonçalo Caetano Pereira was a Goan-Portuguese trader of the Zambezi valley in Mozambique, active in the late 18th and early 19th centuries. From estates near Tete he built up private forces of Chikunda and traded in ivory and gold north of the river.

georgios-i-of-makuria.s: Georgios I was king of Makuria, the medieval Christian kingdom of Nubia, in the 9th century. In the 830s, as heir to the throne, he travelled to Baghdad and negotiated with the Abbasid caliph al-Mu'tasim over the arrears of the Baqt tribute, which were cancelled.

guadalhorce.s: The Guadalhorce is the main river of the province of Málaga in Andalusia, southern Spain, flowing about 150 km to the Mediterranean just west of Málaga. In antiquity its estuary was a deep bay where the Phoenicians founded the settlement of Cerro del Villar.

gonzalo-de-alvarado.s: Gonzalo de Alvarado was a Spanish conquistador and relative of Pedro de Alvarado who took part in the conquest of Guatemala. In 1525 he besieged Zaculeu, the fortified capital of the Mam kingdom in the western highlands, for several months, until its starving defenders under…

gambaga.s: Gambaga is a town in the North East Region of Ghana, on the Gambaga escarpment. It was the early capital of the Mamprugu kingdom before the court moved to Nalerigu around 1700, and it remained a trading town on routes to the Hausa lands.

german-reunification.s: German reunification was the process by which the German Democratic Republic (East Germany) joined the Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany) on 3 October 1990, ending the division of the country that had lasted since 1949. After the fall of the Berlin Wall and East…

georges-danton.s: Georges Danton was a lawyer and orator who became one of the leading figures of the French Revolution. A founder of the Cordeliers Club, he was minister of justice after the fall of the monarchy in 1792 and rallied the nation against foreign invasion.

guru-nanak.s: Guru Nanak was the founder of Sikhism and the first of its ten gurus, born near Lahore in 1469. After a transforming religious experience he travelled widely, by tradition as far as Mecca, Baghdad and Tibet, teaching devotion to one formless God, the equality of all people…

georg-schweinfurth.s: Georg Schweinfurth was a Baltic German botanist and explorer born in Riga. On his journey through the upper Nile basin and Central Africa from 1868 to 1871 he reached the Uele river and became the first European to describe the Azande and the Mangbetu, including the court of…

guayaquil.s: Guayaquil is the largest city and main port of Ecuador, on the Guayas river near the Gulf of Guayaquil. Founded by the Spanish in the 1530s, it became the chief port and shipyard of the Audiencia of Quito.

guayas-province.s: Guayas is a province on the Pacific coast of Ecuador, with Guayaquil as its capital. Drained by the Guayas river system, it is the country's most populous province and a centre of banana, cacao, rice and shrimp production.

gulf-of-guayaquil.s: The Gulf of Guayaquil is a large inlet of the Pacific Ocean on the coast of Ecuador, with its southern shore reaching Peru. The Guayas river flows into it through a broad estuary, and its largest island is Puná.

giustiniani-family.s: The Giustiniani were a Genoese family association formed in 1362 by the shareholders of the Maona of Chios, who took the common surname and governed the island of Chios and its mastic trade until the Ottoman conquest of 1566. Its members included Giovanni Giustiniani Longo,…

gilgit.s: Gilgit is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan in northern Pakistan, on the Gilgit river near its junction with the Hunza. A stop on routes linking South and Central Asia, it is known for the Gilgit manuscripts, Buddhist texts of the 5th to 7th centuries found nearby.

gilgit-baltistan.s: Gilgit-Baltistan is a territory administered by Pakistan in the north of the disputed Kashmir region, bordering China and Afghanistan. It came under Pakistani control after the 1947 uprising against the Dogra rulers of Jammu and Kashmir, was long called the Northern Areas, and…

gernrode-abbey.s: Gernrode Abbey was a convent for noblewomen in the Harz foothills of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, founded in 959 by Margrave Gero, who was buried there. Its church of St Cyriakus is one of the best-preserved buildings of the Ottonian period, with an early copy of the Holy Sepulchre.

gero-the-great.s: Gero the Great was a Saxon noble whom Otto I appointed in 937 to command the eastern frontier of Saxony against the Slavs. He extended German rule over the Slavic lands between the Saale, Elbe and Oder through harsh campaigns and in 963 forced Mieszko I of Poland to pay tribute.

gunz.s: The Günz is a river in Bavarian Swabia, southern Germany, flowing north from the Alpine foothills to join the Danube at Günzburg. It gave its name to the Günz glaciation, an early Ice Age cold stage named by Albrecht Penck and Eduard Brückner.

gunzburg.s: Günzburg is a town in Bavarian Swabia at the mouth of the Günz on the Danube, on the site of the Roman fort of Guntia. It was the chief town of the Habsburg Margraviate of Burgau, residence of Margrave Charles of Burgau from 1609, and in the 18th century housed an important…

guben.s: Guben is a town in Lower Lusatia on the Lusatian Neisse river. In 1945 the river became the border between Germany and Poland, dividing the town into Guben in Brandenburg and Gubin in Poland, where most of the old centre lies.

gorlitz.s: Görlitz is a town on the Lusatian Neisse in Saxony, Germany's easternmost town. It prospered on the cloth trade and the Via Regia road and was a leading member of the Six Towns League of Upper Lusatia from 1346.

gomani-i.s: Gomani I, also called Chikuse, was paramount chief of the Maseko Ngoni in what is now southern Malawi in the late nineteenth century. The son of Mputa, he ruled from the highlands south-west of Lake Malawi, resisted British demands for labour and tax, and stopped his people…

gyptis.s: Gyptis is the daughter of Nannus, king of the Segobrigii, in the foundation legend of Massalia (Marseille). In the version told by the Roman historian Justin, she chose the Greek leader Protis as her husband at a wedding feast by offering him a cup of water, and her father…

gaia-numidian-king.s: Gaia, also called Gala, was king of the Massylii, the eastern Numidian people of North Africa, in the late third century BCE and the father of Masinissa. An ally of Carthage, he sent his son to fight for the Carthaginians in Spain during the Second Punic War.

gauda-region.s: Gauda was a region of ancient and medieval Bengal, roughly the north-western part of present-day West Bengal and neighbouring Bangladesh. In the sixth century its people, the Gaudas, were rivals of the Maukharis, and under King Shashanka in the early seventh century Gauda…

grahavarman.s: Grahavarman was the last king of the Maukhari dynasty, ruling from Kannauj in northern India around 600 CE. He married Rajyashri, daughter of Prabhakaravardhana of Thanesar and sister of Harsha.

gildo.s: Gildo was a Berber prince, son of Nubel and brother of Firmus, who served Rome as military commander in Africa from 386. In 397 he transferred his allegiance from the western to the eastern emperor and withheld the grain fleet from Rome, starting the Gildonic revolt.

gorumahisani.s: Gorumahisani is an iron-ore hill in Mayurbhanj district, northern Odisha, India. Its deposits were identified by the geologist P.

gazi-kenya.s: Gazi is a coastal village south of Mombasa in Kwale County, Kenya. In the nineteenth century it became the seat of a branch of the Mazrui family who had lost Mombasa to the Busaidi of Oman, and from there Mbaruk bin Rashid al-Mazrui led a rebellion against British rule in…

ganzak.s: Ganzak was the capital of the kingdom of Media Atropatene and later a major city of Sasanian Azerbaijan, in north-western Iran. It lay near the sanctuary of the sacred fire Adur Gushnasp at Takht-e Soleyman.

great-chief-of-the-ma.s: Great Chief of the Ma was the title of the leaders of the Meshwesh, Libyan settlers in Egypt, during the Third Intermediate Period. Descended from Libyan captives and soldiers settled in the Delta and around Herakleopolis from the twelfth century BCE, such chiefs ruled towns…

gulf-of-riga.s: The Gulf of Riga is a large bay of the Baltic Sea between Latvia and Estonia, partly closed off from the open sea by the Estonian island of Saaremaa. The Daugava and other rivers flow into it, and the ports of Riga and Pärnu stand on its shores.

gardman.s: Gardman was a district of Caucasian Albania in the hills west of the Kura river, in present-day western Azerbaijan. In the late 6th century it became the domain of the Mihranids, a branch of a great Parthian noble family, who made it the base from which they ruled Albania as…
