guifang.s: The Guifang were a people on the northern or north-western frontier of Shang China, named in oracle-bone inscriptions and in later texts. The Book of Changes records that the Shang king Wu Ding attacked the Guifang and subdued them after three years, and bronze inscriptions…

gulf-of-oman.s: The Gulf of Oman is an arm of the Arabian Sea that connects it with the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz. It is bordered by Iran and Pakistan to the north, Oman to the south and the United Arab Emirates to the west.

gwanggaeto-stele.s: The Gwanggaeto Stele is a granite monument about six metres tall erected in 414 by King Jangsu of Goguryeo at the old capital, present-day Ji'an in Jilin, China, in honour of his father Gwanggaeto the Great. Its inscription of some 1,800 Chinese characters records Goguryeo's…

gyebaek.s: Gyebaek was a general of the Korean kingdom of Baekje. In 660, as Silla and Tang China invaded, he led a small army against a much larger Silla force at Hwangsanbeol; according to tradition he first killed his own family so that they would not be enslaved.

gyeongdeok-of-silla.s: Gyeongdeok was king of Silla from 742 to 765, at the height of Unified Silla's culture. He gave place names and official titles Chinese forms and tried to strengthen royal authority against the aristocracy.

gukhak.s: The Gukhak was the national Confucian academy of Silla, founded in 682 under King Sinmun to train young aristocrats for government service. Students studied the Confucian classics such as the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety.

george-pomeroy-colley.s: Sir George Pomeroy Colley was a British general and colonial administrator, governor of Natal and high commissioner for south-eastern Africa at the outbreak of the First Boer War. He led the relief force against the Transvaal Boers but was defeated at Laing's Nek and Ingogo,…

great-rhetra.s: The Great Rhetra is an early Spartan constitutional text preserved by Plutarch in his Life of Lycurgus, presented as an oracle from Delphi given to the lawgiver Lycurgus. It orders the founding of a cult, the organisation of the people into tribes and obai, a council of thirty…

guanzi.s: The Guanzi is a large Chinese compilation of political, economic and philosophical writings named after Guan Zhong, minister of Duke Huan of Qi in the seventh century BCE. Most of it was written later by scholars of Qi, and it was edited by Liu Xiang in about 26 BCE into 86…

guoyu.s: The Guoyu (Discourses of the States) is an ancient Chinese collection of speeches and anecdotes arranged by state, covering Zhou, Lu, Qi, Jin, Zheng, Chu, Wu and Yue from about the tenth to the fifth century BCE. Traditionally attributed to Zuo Qiuming, it was compiled in the…

golden-bull-of-rimini.s: The Golden Bull of Rimini was a decree of Emperor Frederick II, dated March 1226 at Rimini, though possibly issued later. It confirmed the Teutonic Order's possession of the Chełmno Land, granted by Duke Konrad I of Masovia, and of any lands it conquered from the pagan…

gollub-war.s: The Gollub War was a brief conflict in 1422 between the Teutonic Order and the allied Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania, named after the town of Golub (Gollub), which the allies captured. The Order received no help from the Empire and was ravaged by the invading…

gok-madrasa.s: The Gök Madrasa is a theological college in Sivas, Turkey, built in 1271 for the Seljuk vizier Sahib Ata Fakhr al-Din Ali. Its name, meaning blue madrasa, comes from the turquoise tiles of its interior.

guillaume-henri-dufour.s: Guillaume-Henri Dufour was a Swiss general and engineer from Geneva. He commanded the federal army that defeated the Sonderbund in November 1847 with few casualties, paving the way for the federal state of 1848.

gottfried-keller.s: Gottfried Keller was a Swiss writer from Zurich and one of the major authors of German-language realism. His novel Green Henry (Der grüne Heinrich) and the stories of The People of Seldwyla portray Swiss life with humour and moral seriousness.

gotthard-railway.s: The Gotthard Railway is a Swiss trans-Alpine line linking central Switzerland with Ticino and Italy, opened in 1882. Its summit tunnel, about fifteen kilometres long, was built between 1872 and 1882 under the engineer Louis Favre, at the cost of many workers' lives.

george-cowgill.s: George Cowgill was an American archaeologist who spent much of his career studying Teotihuacan, beginning with René Millon's Teotihuacan Mapping Project in the 1960s. He pioneered the use of computers and quantitative methods in archaeology, and his book Ancient Teotihuacan…

gao-xianzhi.s: Gao Xianzhi was a Tang general of Goguryeo descent who served in the Tang garrisons of the Tarim Basin. In 747 he led an army across the Pamirs to seize Little Balur, cutting Tibet's link with its western allies, but in 751 he was defeated by the Abbasid Caliphate at the…

gar-clan.s: The Gar were a powerful aristocratic clan of imperial Tibet. Gar Tongtsen, chief minister of Songtsen Gampo, negotiated the marriage with the Tang princess Wencheng, and he and his sons governed the empire after Songtsen Gampo's death, conquering the Tuyuhun and fighting the…

gar-trinring-tsendro.s: Gar Trinring Tsendro was a Tibetan general and minister, a son of Gar Tongtsen, who led the Tibetan armies in their greatest victories over the Tang. In 670 he defeated a Tang army under Xue Rengui at the Dafei River, and in 678 he won another major victory near Kokonor.

guregen.s: Güregen, meaning 'royal son-in-law', was a title borne in the Mongol world by men who married into the family of Genghis Khan. Timur, who was not a Chinggisid and therefore could not call himself khan, adopted it after marrying a Chinggisid princess, Saray Mulk Khanum, in…

grand-embassy-of-peter-the-great.n: Grand Embassy of Peter the Great
grand-embassy-of-peter-the-great.s: The Grand Embassy was a Russian diplomatic mission to western Europe in 1697–1698, formally led by Franz Lefort and Fyodor Golovin, in which Tsar Peter I travelled incognito as Pyotr Mikhailov. It sought allies against the Ottoman Empire and recruited specialists, while Peter…

guhila-dynasty.s: The Guhilas were a Rajput dynasty that ruled Mewar in southern Rajasthan from the seventh century, first from Nagda and Ahar as feudatories of larger powers and later from Chittor. After Alauddin Khalji took Chittor in 1303 the main line ended, and the Sisodia branch under…

godfrey-binaisa.s: Godfrey Binaisa was a Ugandan lawyer who served as attorney general under Milton Obote in the 1960s and as president of Uganda from June 1979 to May 1980, after the overthrow of Idi Amin. Chosen by the National Consultative Council to replace Yusuf Lule, he was deposed by the…

group-areas-act.s: The Group Areas Act of 1950 was a central law of apartheid in South Africa that assigned separate residential and business areas in towns and cities to each racial group. Enforced over the following decades, it led to the forced removal of hundreds of thousands of people,…

gulf-cooperation-council.s: The Gulf Cooperation Council is a regional political and economic union of six Arab states of the Persian Gulf: Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Oman. Founded at Abu Dhabi on 25 May 1981 amid the Iranian Revolution and the Iran–Iraq War, it…

greater-and-lesser-tunbs.s: The Greater and Lesser Tunbs are two small islands in the Persian Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz. Claimed by the emirate of Ras al-Khaimah, they were occupied by Iran on 30 November 1971, on the eve of the formation of the United Arab Emirates.

george-vi.s: George VI was king of the United Kingdom and the Dominions from 1936 to 1952, succeeding his brother Edward VIII after the abdication crisis. He stayed in London through the Blitz and became a symbol of national resistance in the Second World War; he was the last emperor of…

general-strike-of-1926.s: The General Strike of 1926 was a nine-day strike in the United Kingdom from 3 to 12 May 1926, called by the Trades Union Congress in support of coal miners facing wage cuts and longer hours. About 1.7 million workers came out, but the government kept services running with…

george-eliot.s: George Eliot was the pen name of Mary Ann Evans, an English novelist and one of the leading writers of the Victorian era. Her novels, including Adam Bede, The Mill on the Floss, Silas Marner and Middlemarch, are known for their psychological depth and realistic portrayal of…

great-exhibition.s: The Great Exhibition of the Works of Industry of All Nations was an international exhibition held in the Crystal Palace in Hyde Park, London, from May to October 1851. Organised by Prince Albert and Henry Cole, it displayed manufactures and inventions from around the world,…

great-famine-ireland.s: The Great Famine was a period of mass starvation and disease in Ireland from 1845 to 1852, caused by a potato blight that destroyed the staple crop of the rural poor. Worsened by British government policy, evictions and continued food exports, it killed about a million people…

gibeah.s: Gibeah was a town of the tribe of Benjamin, a few kilometres north of Jerusalem, described in the Hebrew Bible as the home and royal seat of Saul, the first king of Israel. It is usually identified with Tell el-Ful, where excavations found a fortified structure of the Iron…

gulf-of-aqaba.s: The Gulf of Aqaba is the north-eastern arm of the Red Sea, between the Sinai Peninsula and the Arabian Peninsula, bordered today by Egypt, Israel, Jordan and Saudi Arabia. In antiquity it gave the Levant access to the Red Sea trade through ports such as Ezion-Geber, and…

government-of-india.s: The Government of India is the union government of the Republic of India, seated in New Delhi and constituted since 1950 under the Constitution of India. Its executive consists of the president and the council of ministers headed by the prime minister, responsible to…

godin-tepe.s: Godin Tepe is an archaeological site in the Kangavar valley of western Iran, on the route through the Zagros Mountains towards Mesopotamia. Excavations found a walled enclave with Uruk-style pottery and tablets of the late fourth millennium BCE, early chemical evidence of wine…

gajapati-dynasty.s: The Gajapati dynasty, or Suryavamsi Gajapatis, ruled Odisha in eastern India from 1434, when Kapilendra Deva seized power from the Eastern Gangas, until about 1541. Under Kapilendra Deva their kingdom stretched far south along the east coast.

gooty.s: Gooty is a town in the Anantapur district of Andhra Pradesh, India, dominated by a hill fortress on a granite outcrop. The fort was one of the chain of strongholds that defended the Vijayanagara Empire, and it was later held by the Maratha chief Murari Rao and then by Hyder…

gleb-of-ryazan.s: Gleb of Ryazan (Gleb Rostislavich) was prince of Ryazan from about 1145 to 1177. In the succession struggle for Vladimir after Andrei Bogolyubsky's murder he backed his brothers-in-law against Vsevolod the Big Nest, and his forces burned Moscow in 1177.

gorodets.s: Gorodets is an old town on the left bank of the Volga in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, Russia, founded in the twelfth century, traditionally in 1152 by Yuri Dolgoruky. It was a frontier fortress of Vladimir-Suzdal and the seat of an appanage principality, held in the late thirteenth…

gadayuddha.s: The Gadayuddha ('battle of maces') is a Kannada poem by Ranna, composed around 982, that retells the final duel between Bhima and Duryodhana from the Mahabharata. Written in the champu style, it compares its patron, the Western Chalukya prince Satyashraya, to Bhima and is…

gugong-danfu.s: Gugong Danfu, 'the Ancient Duke Danfu', was a legendary ancestor of the Zhou royal house and the grandfather of King Wen. According to tradition he led the Zhou people from Bin to the plain of Zhouyuan below Mount Qi in present-day Shaanxi to escape attacks by nomadic peoples,…

gonghe-regency.s: The Gonghe Regency was the period from 841 to 828 BCE when the Zhou state was governed without a king after a revolt in the capital drove King Li into exile. Traditional sources describe joint rule by the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, while others credit a noble named He, the Earl…

guan-shu-xian.s: Guan Shu Xian was the third son of King Wen of Zhou and an elder brother of the Duke of Zhou. After the Zhou conquest of the Shang he was enfeoffed at Guan and, with his brothers Cai Shu Du and Huo Shu, set to watch over the Shang heir Wu Geng.

guoji-zi-bai-pan.s: The Guoji Zi Bai pan is a large Western Zhou bronze basin, found at Baoji in Shaanxi in the nineteenth century, made for Zi Bai, a member of the ruling family of Western Guo. Its rhymed inscription of 111 characters celebrates a victory over the Xianyun under King Xuan, with…

greater-khingan.s: The Greater Khingan is a mountain range in north-eastern China, running about 1,200 km from north to south through Inner Mongolia and Heilongjiang and separating the Mongolian Plateau from the Manchurian plain. Its forested slopes were the homeland of several nomadic and…

gol-mod.s: Gol Mod is an archaeological site in Arkhangai Province in central Mongolia with large cemeteries of elite Xiongnu tombs. Its terraced burials, excavated from the 2000s, contained Chinese lacquerware and bronzes, horse gear, gold ornaments and imported glass, showing the…

guan-hanqing.s: Guan Hanqing was a Chinese playwright of the Yuan dynasty, regarded as the foremost writer of zaju drama. Working in Dadu, he is credited with some sixty plays, of which about eighteen survive, including The Injustice to Dou E, a tragedy of a wronged young widow.

guo-shoujing.s: Guo Shoujing was a Chinese astronomer, mathematician and hydraulic engineer of the Yuan dynasty. He built new astronomical instruments and observatories and helped create the Shoushi calendar of 1281, one of the most accurate of its time.

gopala-pala-dynasty.s: Gopala was the founder of the Pala dynasty of Bengal, chosen as king around 750 to end a century of disorder known as matsyanyaya, 'the law of the fish'. The Khalimpur copper plate of his son Dharmapala records that the people elected him, a rare claim in Indian history.

george-john-i-count-palatine-of-veldenz.n: George John I, Count Palatine of Veldenz
george-john-i-count-palatine-of-veldenz.s: George John I was Count Palatine of Veldenz and Lützelstein from 1544 to 1592, ruling a small Lutheran principality on the edge of the Vosges. Ambitious and full of projects, he founded the town of Phalsbourg in 1570, planning it as a fortified refuge for Protestants, but…

gallienus.s: Gallienus was Roman emperor from 253 to 268, first with his father Valerian and alone after Valerian's capture by the Persians in 260. His reign saw the worst of the 3rd-century crisis: the Gallic and Palmyrene regions broke away, and Alemanni, Goths and others invaded.

garton-slack.s: Garton Slack is a dry valley in the Yorkshire Wolds near Driffield in England, where excavations in the 1960s and 1970s uncovered extensive prehistoric settlements and burials. Its Iron Age cemeteries of the Arras culture included square-ditched barrows and a chariot burial,…

gurugram.s: Gurugram, known until 2016 as Gurgaon, is a city in Haryana, India, south-west of Delhi and part of the National Capital Region. Once a small town and district headquarters, it grew from the 1990s into a major centre of finance, information technology and corporate offices.

great-leap-forward.s: The Great Leap Forward was a campaign launched by Mao Zedong in 1958 to turn China rapidly into an industrial and communist society. Peasants were organised into vast people's communes, labour was diverted to backyard steel furnaces, and officials reported inflated harvests…

giessen.s: Giessen is a university town on the Lahn river in Hesse, Germany. It was the main town of Upper Hesse, a province of the landgraviate and later grand duchy of Hesse-Darmstadt, whose ruler founded its university in 1607.

greater-hesse.s: Greater Hesse was a state created in September 1945 in the American zone of occupied Germany. It combined the parts of the People's State of Hesse east of the Rhine with most of the former Prussian province of Hesse-Nassau.

gandhinagar.s: Gandhinagar is the capital of the Indian state of Gujarat, a planned city on the Sabarmati river north of Ahmedabad named after Mahatma Gandhi. It was built from the 1960s and became the capital in 1970, replacing Ahmedabad.

ganden-monastery.s: Ganden Monastery is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery on a mountain about 40 kilometres east of Lhasa, founded by Tsongkhapa in 1409. It was the first and mother monastery of the Gelug school, whose head, the Ganden Tripa, is its abbot.

greek-peoples-liberation-army.s: The Greek People's Liberation Army (ELAS) was the military wing of EAM and the largest Greek resistance force during the Axis occupation. Formed in 1942, with Aris Velouchiotis as its leading figure and Stefanos Sarafis as military commander, it fought the occupiers and rival…

gal-vihara.s: The Gal Vihara is a rock temple at Polonnaruwa in Sri Lanka, made under King Parakramabahu I in the 12th century. Four large images of the Buddha, two seated, one standing and one reclining about 14 metres long, are carved into a single granite outcrop.

gulf-of-kissamos.s: The Gulf of Kissamos is a bay at the north-western end of Crete, Greece, enclosed by the Gramvousa peninsula to the west and the Rodopou peninsula to the east. The town of Kissamos lies on its southern shore, and the ancient city of Polyrrhenia stood on a hill inland.

garuda-pancasila.s: The Garuda Pancasila is the national emblem of Indonesia, adopted in February 1950. It shows a golden Garuda, the mythical bird of Hindu–Buddhist tradition, carrying a shield with symbols of the five principles of Pancasila, and holding a scroll with the motto Bhinneka Tunggal…

gulf-of-baratti.s: The Gulf of Baratti is a small bay on the Tuscan coast of Italy, north of Piombino, below the Etruscan city of Populonia. Its shore holds the main necropolis of Populonia, where great tumulus tombs were buried under slag from the iron furnaces that smelted ore from Elba.

galle.s: Galle is a port city on the south-western coast of Sri Lanka. Long a trading harbour, it was fortified by the Portuguese in the late 16th century and captured by the Dutch East India Company in 1640, which made it their main base on the island until they took Colombo.

gwenwynwyn-ab-owain.s: Gwenwynwyn ab Owain was prince of southern Powys from 1195, which was known after him as Powys Wenwynwyn. Son of Owain Cyfeiliog, he tried to lead the Welsh princes against the English but was overshadowed by Llywelyn the Great of Gwynedd, who seized his lands in 1208.

gaius-marius-the-younger.s: Gaius Marius the Younger was a Roman politician, the son, probably by adoption, of the general Gaius Marius. Elected consul in 82 BCE at about 27 during the civil war against Sulla, he was defeated at Sacriportus and besieged in Praeneste, where he killed himself as the town…

gastein-valley.s: The Gastein Valley is an Alpine valley in the Austrian state of Salzburg, south of the Salzach. Its gold and silver mines made it a major source of wealth for the prince-archbishops of Salzburg in the 15th and 16th centuries, and its hot springs have drawn visitors since the…

gabriel-de-gabrieli.s: Gabriel de Gabrieli was a Baroque architect from Roveredo in the Italian-speaking part of Graubünden. After serving as court architect at Ansbach, he became court architect to the prince-bishops of Eichstätt in 1714 and designed many of the buildings that give the town its…

gniezno.s: Gniezno is a city in Greater Poland, western Poland, one of the earliest centres of the Polish state under the Piast dynasty. In 1000, at the Congress of Gniezno, Emperor Otto III and Bolesław I founded an archbishopric there, and early kings of Poland were crowned in its…

giovanni-battista-tiepolo.s: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was a Venetian painter, the leading European decorative painter of the 18th century. Known for luminous ceiling frescoes filled with figures in open skies, he worked in Venice and northern Italy, at Würzburg from 1750 to 1753, where he painted the…

gottfried-wilhelm-leibniz.s: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was a German philosopher, mathematician and scholar. He developed the differential and integral calculus independently of Isaac Newton, designed a calculating machine and worked on binary arithmetic.

galich-kostroma-oblast.s: Galich is a small town on the shore of Lake Galich in Kostroma Oblast, Russia, first mentioned in the 12th century. Known for its salt springs, it was the seat of a principality from the 13th century until Moscow annexed it in 1363.

gjirokaster.s: Gjirokastër is a town in southern Albania, built on a mountainside above the Drino valley and dominated by a large castle. It was taken around 1386 by the Albanian chieftain Gjon Zenebishi and fell to the Ottomans in 1419.

geza-i-of-hungary.s: Géza I was King of Hungary from 1074 to 1077, a son of King Béla I. As holder of the ducal third of the kingdom, he and his brother Ladislaus fought their cousin King Solomon and defeated him at Mogyoród in 1074.

gisela-of-bavaria.s: Gisela of Bavaria was the first queen of Hungary, wife of King Stephen I and sister of Emperor Henry II. Her marriage around 996 tied the new Christian Hungarian monarchy to the Ottonian Empire and brought Bavarian clergy and knights to Hungary.

guaram-i-of-iberia.s: Guaram I was the first presiding prince of Iberia in eastern Georgia, chosen by the nobility in 588 with Byzantine backing after the Sasanians had abolished the Iberian monarchy. He held the Byzantine title of kouropalates and founded the Guaramid line, which shared the office…

guaramid-dynasty.s: The Guaramids were a Georgian princely family descended from Guaram I, presiding prince of Iberia from 588. Alternating with the Chosroid dynasty, members of the family held the office of presiding prince of Iberia under Byzantine and later Arab overlordship.

grigol-of-kakheti.s: Grigol was the first chorepiscopus, or ruling prince, of Kakheti in eastern Georgia, from 786 to 827. He united the communities east of Tbilisi into a principality independent of the presiding princes of Iberia and of Arab Tbilisi.

gandzasar-monastery.s: Gandzasar is an Armenian monastery in the mountains of Nagorno-Karabakh, built for Prince Hasan-Jalal Dawla of Khachen, whose Cathedral of Saint John the Baptist was consecrated in 1240. It served for centuries as the seat of the Catholicos of Aghvank and the burial place of…

greiz.s: Greiz is a town in eastern Thuringia, Germany, on the White Elster in the Vogtland. From 1564 it was the seat of the Elder Line of the House of Reuss, whose princes ruled from its Upper and Lower Castles and summer palace until 1918.

ghurak.s: Ghurak was the ikhshid, or king, of Samarkand in the early 8th century. He came to power around 710, shortly before the Umayyad general Qutayba ibn Muslim took the city in 712, and then ruled as a tributary of the caliphate.

gerhard-von-scharnhorst.s: Gerhard von Scharnhorst was a Hanoverian-born Prussian general and military reformer, trained at Count William of Schaumburg-Lippe's military school on the Wilhelmstein. After Prussia's defeat by Napoleon in 1806 he led the reform of its army with Gneisenau, creating a general…

gunther-xli-of-schwarzburg-arnstadt.s: Günther XLI, called the Warlike, was a count of Schwarzburg who ruled from Arnstadt. He served the Habsburgs as a military commander, including in the Netherlands, and was one of the leading German Protestant nobles in imperial service.

giovanni-antonio-orsini-del-balzo.s: Giovanni Antonio Orsini del Balzo, Prince of Taranto, was the most powerful baron of the Kingdom of Naples in the 15th century, holding much of Apulia. He supported Alfonso V of Aragon's conquest of Naples, but rebelled against Alfonso's son Ferrante from 1459 in alliance with…

gleb-sviatoslavich.s: Gleb Sviatoslavich was a Rus' prince, son of Sviatoslav II of Chernigov. He ruled the Black Sea principality of Tmutarakan, where an inscribed stone of 1068 records him measuring the width of the frozen Kerch Strait, the oldest dated East Slavic inscription.

george-ii-rakoczi.s: George II Rákóczi was Prince of Transylvania from 1648. Seeking the Polish crown, he invaded Poland in 1657 in alliance with Sweden without Ottoman permission; his army was destroyed, and the Ottomans and Crimean Tatars ravaged Transylvania in reprisal.

gediminas.s: Gediminas was Grand Duke of Lithuania from about 1316 until his death and founder of the Gediminid dynasty. He made Vilnius his capital, expanded his realm deep into the lands of Rus' weakened by the Mongols, and in letters of 1323 invited Western merchants, craftsmen and…

george-brown-canadian-politician.s: George Brown was a Scottish-born Canadian journalist and politician who founded the Toronto Globe and led the Reformers of Canada West. A champion of representation by population, he joined his rivals John A.

grand-trunk-railway.s: The Grand Trunk Railway was a railway company incorporated in the Province of Canada in 1852 to link Montreal, Toronto and an ice-free Atlantic port. By 1860 its line ran from Sarnia through Montreal to Portland, Maine, crossing the St Lawrence on the Victoria Bridge.

georgia-salzburgers.s: The Georgia Salzburgers were Lutheran refugees from the Archbishopric of Salzburg, expelled by Archbishop Leopold Anton von Firmian in 1731–1732, who settled in the Province of Georgia from 1734. They founded Ebenezer near Savannah, where they farmed, raised silk and for years…

germantown-philadelphia.s: Germantown is a district of north-western Philadelphia, founded in 1683 by German and Dutch Quaker and Mennonite families led by Francis Daniel Pastorius. Some of its residents issued the first organised protest against slavery in the English colonies in 1688.

gullah.s: The Gullah are African Americans of the Lowcountry of South Carolina and Georgia, descended from enslaved West and Central Africans brought to work the rice, indigo and cotton plantations. Relative isolation on the Sea Islands preserved much of their African heritage,…

guayana-province.s: Guayana Province was a Spanish colonial province covering the lower Orinoco basin and the lands to the south, in present-day eastern Venezuela. Its capital, Santo Tomé de Guayana, was moved in 1764 to Angostura, now Ciudad Bolívar.

guipuzcoan-company-of-caracas.s: The Guipuzcoan Company of Caracas was a Basque trading company chartered by the Spanish Crown in 1728 with a monopoly on trade between Spain and the province of Venezuela. It shipped cacao to Spain, fought smuggling and built ports and forts, but its low prices for cacao…

grover-cleveland.s: Grover Cleveland was the 22nd and 24th president of the United States, serving from 1885 to 1889 and from 1893 to 1897. A Democrat who opposed high tariffs and defended the gold standard, he withdrew the treaty to annex Hawaii in 1893 after the Blount Report found American…

gessius-florus.s: Gessius Florus was the Roman procurator of Judaea from 64 to 66 CE, appointed under Nero. Josephus portrays him as greedy and brutal, and his seizure of money from the Temple treasury and the violent suppression of protests in Jerusalem in 66 helped spark the First…

gaullism.s: Gaullism is the French political current that follows the ideas of Charles de Gaulle, stressing national independence, a strong state and a powerful head of state. It grew from the Free French and the Resistance and shaped the constitution of the Fifth Republic in 1958.

guanica.s: Guánica is a town on the south-western coast of Puerto Rico. On 25 July 1898, during the Spanish–American War, US troops under General Nelson Miles landed there to begin the invasion of Puerto Rico.

geshem-the-arab.s: Geshem the Arab was a 5th-century BCE Arab ruler named in the Book of Nehemiah as one of the opponents of Nehemiah's rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem. He is usually identified with Gashmu, king of Qedar, whose son Qaynu is named on a silver bowl from Tell el-Maskhuta in…

gabinius-king-of-the-quadi.s: Gabinius was a king of the Quadi, a Germanic people north of the middle Danube, in the 4th century. In 374, when the Romans built forts in Quadi territory, he went to protest and was murdered at a banquet on the orders of the Roman commander Marcellianus.

gaykhatu.s: Gaykhatu was the Mongol ruler of the Ilkhanate in Iran from 1291 to 1295, a son of Abaqa Khan. His extravagance emptied the treasury, and in 1294 his vizier introduced paper money modelled on the Chinese chao, which brought trade in Tabriz to a halt and was quickly withdrawn.

golden-tara-of-agusan.s: The Golden Tara of Agusan is a gold statuette of a seated female deity found in 1917 on the bank of the Wawa river in Agusan, Mindanao, in the southern Philippines. Probably made between the 9th and 13th centuries, it is variously identified as a Hindu or Buddhist goddess and…

great-mosque-of-kairouan.s: The Great Mosque of Kairouan, also called the Mosque of Uqba, is the principal mosque of Kairouan in Tunisia, founded by Uqba ibn Nafi around 670. Its present form dates mainly from the Aghlabid rebuilding of 836 and later 9th-century additions, including a square minaret that…

great-mosque-of-al-nuri.s: The Great Mosque of al-Nuri is a mosque in Mosul, Iraq, built in 1172–1173 by the Zengid ruler Nur al-Din. Its brick minaret, al-Hadba ('the hunchback'), leaned noticeably and became a symbol of the city.

grand-palace.s: The Grand Palace is a complex of royal buildings in Bangkok, Thailand, built from 1782 on Rattanakosin Island by King Rama I, founder of the Chakri dynasty, when he moved the capital from Thonburi. Surrounded by walls, it housed the royal court and government until the 20th…

glomma.s: The Glomma is the longest river in Norway, about 620 kilometres long. It rises near Røros and flows south through the Østerdalen valley and the farmlands of Romerike and Østfold to the Skagerrak at Fredrikstad.

gurs-internment-camp.s: Gurs was an internment camp in the foothills of the Pyrenees in south-western France, built in 1939 for refugees from the Spanish Civil War. Under the Vichy regime it held foreign Jews and others, including some 6,500 Jews deported from Baden and the Saar-Palatinate in October…

gran-chaco.s: The Gran Chaco is a vast, hot, semi-arid lowland plain in central South America shared by Paraguay, Bolivia, Argentina and a small part of Brazil. Covered with dry forest, scrub and seasonal wetlands, it was home to indigenous peoples who long resisted colonial rule.

gitega.s: Gitega is the political capital of Burundi and one of its largest cities, in the central highlands. A former royal centre and colonial administrative post, it houses the country's National Museum.

gustavo-petro.s: Gustavo Petro is a Colombian politician who became Colombia's first left-wing president, serving from August 2022 to August 2026. A former member of the M-19 guerrilla movement, he later served as a senator and as mayor of Bogotá from 2012 to 2015.

gerardo-machado.s: Gerardo Machado was a Cuban general of the independence war who was elected president in 1924 and took office in 1925. After extending his term unconstitutionally in 1928 he ruled as a dictator, violently suppressing students and opponents as the Great Depression hit…

granma-yacht.s: The Granma is the yacht that carried Fidel Castro, Che Guevara and 80 other revolutionaries from Tuxpan, Mexico, to eastern Cuba in late 1956. They landed on 2 December in difficult conditions and were scattered by government troops, and the survivors regrouped in the Sierra…

galapagos-islands.s: The Galápagos Islands are a volcanic archipelago in the Pacific Ocean about 1,000 km west of the coast of Ecuador, which annexed them in 1832. Their unique wildlife, including giant tortoises, marine iguanas and finches, influenced Charles Darwin's thinking on evolution after…

guayaquil-and-quito-railway.s: The Guayaquil and Quito Railway links the port of Guayaquil with Ecuador's capital, Quito, across the Andes. Promoted by Eloy Alfaro and built largely by American contractors with many Jamaican workers, it was completed in 1908, including the steep switchbacks of the Devil's…

goryokaku.s: Goryōkaku is a star-shaped Western-style fortress in Hakodate, Hokkaido, completed by the Tokugawa shogunate in 1864. In 1868–1869 it was the headquarters of the Republic of Ezo, and its surrender in June 1869 ended the Boshin War.

grebo-people.s: The Grebo are a Kru-speaking people of south-eastern Liberia and neighbouring south-western Côte d'Ivoire, living around Cape Palmas, along the coast and in the Cavalla River valley. Many Grebo worked as sailors and labourers on European ships.

goris.s: Goris is a town in the Syunik province of southern Armenia, near the border with Azerbaijan. It is known for the cave dwellings of Old Goris and for its town of stone houses laid out on a regular plan in the 1870s.

giulio-alberoni.s: Giulio Alberoni was an Italian cardinal and statesman who, as chief minister of Philip V of Spain from 1715 to 1719, tried to restore Spanish power in Italy and provoked the War of the Quadruple Alliance. Dismissed and exiled in 1719, he later returned to papal service as…

goms.s: Goms is the uppermost section of the Rhône valley in the canton of Valais, Switzerland, from the Rhône Glacier down to near Brig. It was one of the seven tenths (Zenden) that ruled the Republic of the Valais and is now a district.

grootfontein.s: Grootfontein is a town in the Otjozondjupa Region of north-eastern Namibia, named after a large spring. Dorsland Trek Boers settled there in 1885 and founded the short-lived Republic of Upingtonia.

gulf-of-roses.s: The Gulf of Roses is a bay of the Mediterranean on the Costa Brava in Catalonia, north-eastern Spain, between Cap de Creus and the Montgrí massif. The Greek colony of Rhode and the later town of Roses lay on its northern shore, and the ancient Greek port of Emporion lay near…

gurindam-dua-belas.s: The Gurindam Dua Belas ('Twelve Gurindam') is a Malay poem of moral and religious advice written by Raja Ali Haji on Penyengat island in 1847. Composed in twelve sections of rhyming couplets, it counts among the classics of Malay literature produced at the Riau-Lingga court.

genpei-war.s: The Genpei War was a civil war in Japan between the Taira and Minamoto clans from 1180 to 1185. It ended with the destruction of the Taira at the naval Battle of Dan-no-ura in 1185.

gracchi.s: The Gracchi were the brothers Tiberius and Gaius Sempronius Gracchus, tribunes of the plebs in Rome in 133 and 123–122 BCE. They proposed laws to redistribute public land to poor citizens and other reforms, and both were killed with many supporters by their opponents in the…

grosseto.s: Grosseto is a city in southern Tuscany, Italy, on the plain of the Ombrone River near the Tyrrhenian coast. It replaced the nearby Etruscan and Roman town of Rusellae as the seat of the bishopric in 1138.

grigory-shelikhov.s: Grigory Shelikhov was a Russian merchant and fur trader who founded the first permanent Russian settlement in North America, at Three Saints Bay on Kodiak Island, in 1784. His company, merged with rival firms after his death, became the Russian-American Company, chartered by…

georgy-lvov.s: Prince Georgy Lvov was a Russian liberal politician who headed the Provisional Government from March to July 1917, after the February Revolution. A leading figure of the zemstvo movement, he struggled to govern alongside the Petrograd Soviet and resigned after the July Days in…

ghumli.s: Ghumli is a ruined town in the Barda hills of Saurashtra, Gujarat, near Porbandar. Known in inscriptions as Bhutambilika, it was the capital of the Saindhava dynasty in the 8th to 10th centuries and later a seat of the Jethwa rulers.

gustav-iii.s: Gustav III was King of Sweden from 1771 to 1792. In 1772 he ended the Age of Liberty by a bloodless coup that restored royal power, and he promoted the arts, founding the Swedish Academy in 1786.

grand-banks-of-newfoundland.s: The Grand Banks are a group of shallow underwater plateaus on the North American continental shelf south-east of Newfoundland. Where the cold Labrador Current meets the warm Gulf Stream they supported one of the richest cod fisheries in the world, worked by European fishermen…

godwin-friday.s: Godwin Friday is a Vincentian politician who became prime minister of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines in November 2025. A lawyer and member of parliament for the Northern Grenadines since 2001, he became leader of the New Democratic Party in 2016.

gifu.s: Gifu is a city in central Japan, capital of Gifu Prefecture, on the Nagara river. Known as Inabayama, it was the castle town of the Saito lords of Mino until Oda Nobunaga captured it in 1567 and renamed it Gifu, making it his base for the advance on Kyoto.

gifu-castle.s: Gifu Castle stands on the summit of Mount Kinka, formerly Mount Inaba, above the city of Gifu in central Japan. As Inabayama Castle it was the stronghold from which Saito Dosan and his heirs ruled Mino province until Oda Nobunaga took it in 1567.

golden-man.s: The Golden Man is the burial of a richly dressed Saka person found in the Issyk kurgan near Almaty, Kazakhstan, in 1969–1970. The clothing and tall pointed headdress were covered with about 4,000 gold ornaments in the animal style, and a silver bowl in the grave bears a short,…

gaspar-vilela.s: Gaspar Vilela was a Portuguese Jesuit missionary who worked in Japan from 1556 until about 1570. He was the first Jesuit allowed to preach in Kyoto, where he obtained permission from the shogun Ashikaga Yoshiteru in 1560, and he founded Christian communities in Sakai and the…

georgians.s: The Georgians are a Kartvelian-speaking people of the southern Caucasus who form the majority of the population of Georgia. Christian since the conversion of the Kingdom of Iberia in the 4th century, they have their own script and church, the Georgian Orthodox Church.

gaius-sextius-calvinus.s: Gaius Sextius Calvinus was a Roman consul of 124 BCE who campaigned against the Salyes of southern Gaul at the request of Massalia. He completed the destruction of their stronghold of Entremont and in 122 BCE founded the garrison settlement of Aquae Sextiae, modern…

ghorpade.s: The Ghorpade are a Maratha clan of the Deccan whose members served the sultans of Bijapur and later the Maratha state as military commanders. Branches of the family ruled the princely states of Sandur and Mudhol under British paramountcy, and Murarirao Ghorpade of Gooty was a…

great-mosque-of-manisa.s: The Great Mosque of Manisa is a mosque in Manisa, western Turkey, built in 1366–1367 by Ishak Bey, ruler of the Turkmen beylik of Saruhan. Standing on the slope of Mount Sipylus, it combines a domed prayer hall with an arcaded courtyard and is joined by a madrasa and the…

ganjifa.s: Ganjifa is a family of card games played with round, hand-painted cards, introduced to India from Persia and popular at the Mughal court in the 16th century. The Mughal pack had eight suits of twelve cards, and Hindu variants such as Dashavatara Ganjifa, based on the ten…

gaius-porcius-cato-consul-114-bce.s: Gaius Porcius Cato was a Roman politician, a grandson of Cato the Elder, who was consul in 114 BCE. As governor of Macedonia he led an army against the Scordisci in Thrace, where it was destroyed, a defeat that opened a long series of Roman wars on the Balkan frontier.

gadsden-purchase.s: The Gadsden Purchase was the sale by Mexico to the United States of about 77,000 square kilometres of land south of the Gila River, in present-day southern Arizona and south-western New Mexico, for 10 million dollars. Negotiated by the American minister James Gadsden with…

georges-eugene-haussmann.s: Georges-Eugène Haussmann was a French administrator who, as prefect of the Seine from 1853 to 1870 under Napoleon III, directed the rebuilding of Paris. His works cut wide boulevards through the medieval centre, created parks, a new water supply and sewers, and imposed uniform…

gabriel-narutowicz.s: Gabriel Narutowicz was a Polish engineer and politician who became the first president of the Second Polish Republic in December 1922. A professor of hydraulic engineering in Zurich, he returned to Poland after independence and served as a minister.

gdynia.s: Gdynia is a port city on the Baltic coast of northern Poland, north of Gdańsk. A fishing village when Poland regained access to the sea in 1920, it was developed by the Second Polish Republic from the 1920s into a modern port independent of the Free City of Danzig.

gita-govinda.s: The Gita Govinda is a Sanskrit lyrical poem of the 12th century by Jayadeva, describing the love of the god Krishna and the cowherd Radha. Its songs became central to Vaishnava devotion in eastern India and are still sung in the temple of Jagannath at Puri.

ganjam-district.s: Ganjam is a coastal district of southern Odisha, India, centred on the city of Berhampur. In the 6th and 7th centuries it formed part of Kongoda, the kingdom of the Shailodbhava dynasty.

green-gang.s: The Green Gang was a Chinese secret society that grew out of the boatmen's brotherhoods of the Grand Canal and became the dominant criminal organisation of early 20th-century Shanghai. Under bosses such as Huang Jinrong and Du Yuesheng it ran opium, gambling and labour rackets…

gyeongsun-of-silla.s: Gyeongsun was the last king of Silla, placed on the throne in 927 by the rebel leader Gyeon Hwon of Later Baekje after the sack of Gyeongju. Ruling a kingdom reduced to its capital region, in 935 he surrendered peacefully to Wang Geon of Goryeo, who gave him high rank and…

goh-chok-tong.s: Goh Chok Tong (born 1941) is a Singaporean politician who served as the second prime minister of Singapore from 1990 to 2004, succeeding Lee Kuan Yew. A former shipping executive, he led the People's Action Party government through strong growth, the Asian financial crisis of…

gulf-of-izmir.s: The Gulf of Izmir is an inlet of the Aegean Sea on the west coast of Turkey, reaching far inland, with the city of Izmir, ancient Smyrna, at its head. Its sheltered waters made Smyrna one of the chief ports of the eastern Mediterranean from antiquity to the Ottoman period.

grodno.s: Grodno, or Hrodna, is a city in western Belarus on the Neman river, near the borders of Poland and Lithuania. First recorded in the 12th century, it became one of the main towns of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, where Sejms of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth often met; the…

goseong-county-south-gyeongsang.s: Goseong is a county on the south coast of South Gyeongsang Province, South Korea, facing a deeply indented bay. In the early centuries CE it was the centre of the Gaya polity of Sogaya ('Little Gaya'), whose burial mounds at Songhak-dong show contacts with Baekje, Silla and…

gulen.s: Gulen is a municipality in Vestland county in western Norway, at the mouth of the Sognefjord. It gave its name to the Gulating, the law assembly of western Norway, which met there from the Viking Age and whose law, the Gulating law, is among the oldest written laws of…

guangdong.s: Guangdong is a coastal province of southern China, with its capital at Guangzhou, and the most populous province of the country. Part of the historical region of Lingnan, it was a centre of maritime trade for over a thousand years, the base of the Southern Han kingdom in the…

government-of-ireland-act-1920.s: The Government of Ireland Act 1920 was a law of the British Parliament that divided Ireland into two self-governing areas, Northern Ireland, of six Ulster counties, and Southern Ireland, each with its own parliament under Westminster. It took effect in Northern Ireland, whose…

gijon.s: Gijón is the largest city of Asturias in northern Spain, a port on the Bay of Biscay with Roman origins. In the eighth century it was a seat of Muslim authority whose governor Munuza faced the revolt of Pelagius.

guale.s: The Guale were an indigenous people and chiefdom of the coast of present-day Georgia, between St. Catherines Island and the Altamaha River.

george-clifford-3rd-earl-of-cumberland.s: George Clifford, 3rd Earl of Cumberland (1558–1605), was an English courtier, naval commander and privateer who financed a dozen expeditions against Spanish shipping and colonies. In 1598 he captured San Juan in Puerto Rico, taking El Morro after a siege, and planned to hold…

grito-de-lares.s: The Grito de Lares was an uprising against Spanish rule in Puerto Rico on 23 September 1868, planned by Ramón Emeterio Betances from exile. Several hundred rebels took the mountain town of Lares and proclaimed the Republic of Puerto Rico, but Spanish militia defeated them the…

green-march.s: The Green March was a mass demonstration organised by King Hassan II of Morocco in November 1975, in which about 350,000 unarmed Moroccans crossed into Spanish Sahara to press Morocco's claim to the territory. Spain, weakened by Franco's final illness, avoided confrontation…

gotabaya-rajapaksa.s: Gotabaya Rajapaksa (born 1949) is a Sri Lankan former army officer and politician who was president of Sri Lanka from 2019 to 2022. As defence secretary under his brother President Mahinda Rajapaksa he directed the final campaign that defeated the Liberation Tigers of Tamil…

greeneville-tennessee.s: Greeneville is a town in north-eastern Tennessee, founded in 1783 and named after the Revolutionary War general Nathanael Greene. In 1785 it became the seat of government of the State of Franklin, the short-lived breakaway state of settlers west of the Appalachians.

general-company-of-grao-para-and-maranha.n: General Company of Grão-Pará and Maranhão
general-company-of-grao-para-and-maranha.s: The General Company of Grão-Pará and Maranhão was a Portuguese chartered trading company founded in 1755 by the Marquis of Pombal, with a monopoly of trade and shipping between Lisbon and northern Brazil. It shipped tens of thousands of enslaved Africans, mainly from Upper…

guangshan-county.s: Guangshan County is a county in Xinyang, in southern Henan province, China. Within it lay the State of Huang, and in 1983 archaeologists excavated there the tombs of a lord of Huang named Meng and his wife, dating from the seventh century BCE, with bronzes, jades and lacquer.

guan-zhong.s: Guan Zhong was chief minister of the State of Qi under Duke Huan from 685 BCE until his death in 645 BCE. His reforms of administration, taxation and the army, and state management of salt and iron, made Qi the first hegemon of the Spring and Autumn period.

gong-zhiqi.s: Gong Zhiqi was a minister of the small state of Yu in south-western Shanxi in the 7th century BCE. When Duke Xian of Jin asked for passage through Yu to attack Guo, he warned that 'when the lips are gone, the teeth are cold', since Yu and Guo depended on each other.

gongyang-zhuan.s: The Gongyang Zhuan is one of the three classical commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, traditionally attributed to Gongyang Gao, a disciple of Confucius's follower Zixia. Written down in the early Han dynasty in question-and-answer form, it reads hidden moral…

gongyang-of-goryeo.s: Gongyang was the last king of Goryeo, reigning from 1389 to 1392. Placed on the throne by the general Yi Seong-gye and his allies, he had little real power, and after the killing of the loyalist Jeong Mong-ju in 1392 he was deposed and Yi founded the Joseon dynasty.

galmudug.s: Galmudug is a federal member state of Somalia in the centre of the country, first formed in 2006 and reconstituted in 2015, with its capital at Dhusamareb. It covers the Galguduud region and the southern part of Mudug, including the coastal town of Hobyo, once the seat of the…

gobroon-dynasty.s: The Gobroon dynasty was the ruling house of the Geledi clan of southern Somalia, which rose to power at Afgooye on the Shabelle river in the early 18th century after the fall of the Ajuran Sultanate. Under sultans such as Yusuf Mahamud Ibrahim it dominated the region in the…

grand-trunk-road.s: The Grand Trunk Road is one of the oldest and longest roads in Asia, running about 2,500 kilometres from Chittagong and Bengal across northern India to Lahore, Peshawar and Kabul. An ancient route, it was rebuilt in the 1540s by Sher Shah Suri, who lined it with trees,…

guadeloupe-fund.s: The Guadeloupe Fund was a sum of 24 million francs that Britain paid Sweden in 1815 as compensation for giving up the Caribbean island of Guadeloupe, granted to it in 1813 and returned to France. The Riksdag assigned the money to Crown Prince Charles John and his heirs, and…

graaff-reinet.s: Graaff-Reinet is a town in the Eastern Cape, South Africa, founded in 1786 by the Dutch East India Company as the seat of its eastern frontier district. In 1795 its burghers, angry at the Company's frontier policy towards the Xhosa and San, expelled the landdrost and…

ghadames.s: Ghadames is an oasis town in western Libya near the borders of Tunisia and Algeria. The Romans held it as an outpost called Cydamus, and for centuries it was a key stop on trans-Saharan caravan routes linking the Mediterranean with the Niger bend.

gerald-the-fearless.s: Gerald the Fearless (Geraldo Sem Pavor) was a Portuguese warrior who seized several Muslim towns for Afonso I of Portugal through night-time surprise attacks. In 1165 he took Évora, and he went on to capture Trujillo, Cáceres and other places, but failed to hold Badajoz in 1169.

guadix.s: Guadix is a town in the province of Granada, Spain, on the high plateau north of the Sierra Nevada. Founded as the Roman colony of Acci, it became an early bishopric and, under Muslim rule, the town of Wadi Ash, briefly the seat of an independent taifa after 1145.

guadalentin.s: The Guadalentín is a river of south-eastern Spain, a tributary of the Segura, flowing through Lorca and the region of Murcia. Its valley has been irrigated since Roman and Islamic times, and Lorca's hilltop castle guarded it as a frontier stronghold between Castile and the…

gilao.s: The Gilão is a short river of the eastern Algarve in southern Portugal that flows through the town of Tavira to the Ria Formosa lagoon and the Atlantic; its upper course is called the Séqua. Tavira grew as a port at its lowest crossing, where an old bridge, traditionally…

goto-shinpei.s: Gotō Shinpei (1857–1929) was a Japanese physician and statesman. As head of civil administration in Taiwan from 1898 to 1906 under Governor-General Kodama Gentarō, he organised land surveys, censuses, public health, railways and state monopolies.

gharm.s: Gharm is a town in the Rasht valley of central Tajikistan, on the Surkhob river, and the traditional name of the surrounding mountain region. In the 1920s it was a centre of Basmachi resistance to Soviet rule, and in later decades many of its people were resettled in the…

gorno-badakhshan-autonomous-region.s: Gorno-Badakhshan is an autonomous region of eastern Tajikistan covering the Pamir Mountains, almost half of the country's area but with a small population. Created as an autonomous oblast in 1925, it is home to the Pamiri peoples, who speak Eastern Iranian languages and mostly…

garonne.s: The Garonne is a major river of south-western France, about 530 km long, rising in the Spanish Pyrenees and flowing past Toulouse and Bordeaux to join the Dordogne in the Gironde estuary. In antiquity it marked the boundary between the Aquitani and the Celtic Gauls, and it has…

gravisca.s: Gravisca (Graviscae) was the port of the Etruscan city of Tarquinii on the Tyrrhenian coast of Italy. From the early 6th century BCE it held a sanctuary used by Greek traders, with offerings to Aphrodite, Hera and Demeter, excavated from 1969.

glaukias.s: Glaukias was king of the Taulantii, an Illyrian people on the Adriatic coast around Epidamnus, in the late 4th century BCE. He aided Cleitus against Alexander the Great at Pelion in 335 BCE, and later sheltered the infant Pyrrhus of Epirus, refusing to hand him to Cassander…

gangotri.s: Gangotri is a town and Hindu pilgrimage site in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand, India, high in the Himalaya on the Bhagirathi, the headstream of the Ganges. Its temple to the goddess Ganga is one of the four sites of the Char Dham pilgrimage, together with Yamunotri,…

greben-cossacks.s: The Greben Cossacks were a community of Cossacks who settled in the foothills and along the middle Terek River in the North Caucasus from the 16th century. Many were Old Believers, and they lived in close contact with Chechens and Kumyks, adopting elements of their dress and…

gospel-of-luke.s: The Gospel of Luke is the third of the four canonical gospels of the New Testament, written in Greek probably around 80–90 CE by the same author as the Acts of the Apostles. It tells of the life, teaching, death and resurrection of Jesus, and alone records that Pontius Pilate…

gaulanitis.s: Gaulanitis was a region east of the Sea of Galilee and the upper Jordan, corresponding roughly to the modern Golan Heights. Part of the realm of Herod the Great, it passed after 4 BCE to his son Philip the Tetrarch, who refounded Bethsaida as Julias.

gunakamadeva.s: Gunakamadeva was a king of the Kathmandu Valley in the Thakuri period, traditionally placed in the 10th century. Later Nepalese chronicles credit him with founding the city of Kantipur, which became Kathmandu, and with establishing festivals and shrines there.

gebelein.s: Gebelein is an archaeological site on the west bank of the Nile about 30 kilometres south of Luxor in Upper Egypt. Its cemeteries have yielded some of the oldest Egyptian bodies, naturally preserved around 3400 BCE, and painted linen of the Predynastic period.

gondar.s: Gondar is a city in north-western Ethiopia, north of Lake Tana, founded as the royal capital by Emperor Fasilides around 1636. It remained the seat of the Ethiopian emperors until the mid-19th century, and its walled royal enclosure, Fasil Ghebbi, with castles and churches, is…

gateway-of-the-sun.s: The Gateway of the Sun is a monolithic stone portal at Tiwanaku, near Lake Titicaca in Bolivia, carved from a single block of andesite about 3 metres high. Above the doorway a frieze shows a central staff-holding deity flanked by rows of winged attendants, an image that spread…

goto-shojiro.s: Goto Shojiro was a samurai of the Tosa domain in Japan and a leading statesman of the Meiji era. Drawing on the ideas of Sakamoto Ryoma, he persuaded his lord Yamauchi Toyoshige to urge the shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu to return power to the emperor, which Yoshinobu did in 1867.

grand-zupan.s: Grand Župan was the title of the supreme ruler of several early medieval South Slavic states, above the župans who governed individual districts. It was used above all by the rulers of the Grand Principality of Serbia from the 11th to the early 13th century, including Stefan…

great-morava.s: The Great Morava is the principal river of central Serbia, formed by the meeting of the South and West Morava and flowing north about 185 kilometres to the Danube east of Belgrade. Its valley is the main route through the Balkans between the Danube and the Aegean.

ghuma-al-mahmudi.s: Ghuma al-Mahmudi was a tribal leader of the Jabal Nafusa in western Libya who led a long revolt against the Ottomans after they restored direct rule over Tripolitania in 1835. Captured and sent into exile, he later escaped, returned to Libya and renewed the fight.

gusiluo.s: Gusiluo was the Tibetan ruler of the Tsongkha kingdom in Amdo, around the Huangshui valley of present-day Qinghai. Brought in as a youth around 1008 by Tibetan clans who claimed he descended from the old imperial line, he later set up his own court at Qingtang, modern Xining.

gombodorj.s: Gombodorj was Tüsheet Khan, ruler of central Khalkha Mongolia, in the first half of the 17th century, a grandson of Abtai Sain Khan. He is best known as the father of Zanabazar, whom the Khalkha nobility recognised as a reincarnate lama in 1639 and who became the first…

gaspar-pacheco.s: Gaspar Pacheco was a Spanish conquistador in the conquest of Yucatán. In 1544, serving under the Montejos, he and his son Melchor Pacheco led the campaign that conquered Uaymil, Chetumal and neighbouring Maya provinces in the south-east of the peninsula.

gbaya-people.s: The Gbaya are a people of the western Central African Republic and eastern Cameroon, mainly farmers, speaking Gbaya languages. In the 19th century many were raided or ruled by the Fulbe lamidates of Adamawa, such as Ngaoundéré.

gubbio.s: Gubbio, the ancient Iguvium, is a town in north-eastern Umbria, Italy, on the slopes of Monte Ingino. It was an important Umbrian community and then a Roman municipium, and the Iguvine Tablets found there in 1444 preserve its ancient religious rituals.

galati.s: Galați is a city and port on the lower Danube in eastern Romania, in the historical region of Moldavia. As Moldavia's only port on the river, it grew in the 19th century as a grain-exporting free port and became the seat of the European Commission of the Danube, created in 1856.

guantanamo-bay-naval-base.s: Guantánamo Bay Naval Base is a United States naval base on Guantánamo Bay in south-eastern Cuba, leased under an agreement of 1903 that followed the Platt Amendment. A treaty of 1934 made the lease permanent unless both parties agree to end it, and the Cuban government has…

gan-addu-atoll.s: Gan is the southernmost island of Addu Atoll in the Maldives. The British built an airfield there during the Second World War, and from 1957 to 1976 it was the RAF Gan staging post on routes to the Far East and a main source of local employment.

gilgamesh.s: Gilgamesh was a king of Uruk in the Early Dynastic period, perhaps around 2700 BCE, who became the hero of the oldest great epic of world literature. The Sumerian King List names him as a ruler of Uruk, and later tradition credited him with building the city's walls.

gihon-spring.s: The Gihon Spring is the main natural spring of ancient Jerusalem, in the Kidron valley below the City of David. Its water made settlement on the ridge possible, and massive towers were built to protect it in the Middle Bronze Age.

governors-palace-uxmal.s: The Governor's Palace is a long palace building at the Maya city of Uxmal in Yucatán, Mexico, built on a huge artificial platform around 900–1000. About 100 metres long, its upper façade carries an intricate stone mosaic of fretwork, latticework and masks of the rain god, and…

girnar.s: Girnar is a group of volcanic peaks near Junagadh in Gujarat, India, sacred to Jains and Hindus. A rock at its foot carries inscriptions of the Mauryan emperor Ashoka, of the Western Satrap Rudradaman and of the Gupta period.

gelimer.s: Gelimer was the last king of the Vandals in North Africa. In 530 he deposed his pro-Roman cousin Hilderic, giving Emperor Justinian a pretext for war.

gipuzkoa.s: Gipuzkoa is the smallest province of Spain and one of the three provinces of the Basque Country, on the Bay of Biscay along the French border, with its capital at San Sebastián. Long part of the Kingdom of Navarre's sphere, it passed to Castile in 1200 while keeping its own…

gironde.s: Gironde is a department of south-west France, in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region, with its prefecture at Bordeaux. Created in 1790 and named after the Gironde estuary, it is the largest department of metropolitan France.

gironde-estuary.s: The Gironde estuary is the great estuary formed by the meeting of the Garonne and Dordogne rivers below Bordeaux in south-west France, about 75 km long and the largest in Western Europe. It separates the Médoc from Saintonge and has long been the route for the wine trade of…

guntur.s: Guntur is a city in Andhra Pradesh, India, in the fertile plain south of the Krishna river delta. The surrounding region, known in the Middle Ages as Velanadu, was ruled by the Velanati Chodas and later by the Kakatiyas, the Vijayanagara Empire and the Qutb Shahis.

gask-ridge.s: The Gask Ridge is a line of Roman forts, fortlets and timber watchtowers along a ridge in Perthshire, Scotland, north of the Earn valley. Built probably in the 70s or 80s CE, during or soon after the campaigns of Agricola, it guarded the road towards the Tay and may be the…

green-mountain-boys.s: The Green Mountain Boys were a militia formed around 1770 by settlers holding land grants from New Hampshire in what is now Vermont, to resist New York's claims to the area. Led by Ethan Allen, they drove off New York officials and surveyors.

gokstad-ship.s: The Gokstad ship is a Viking ship of about 890, found in a burial mound at Gokstad near Sandefjord in Vestfold, Norway, and excavated in 1880. About 23 metres long, built of oak with sixteen pairs of oars and a sail, it was seaworthy enough for a replica to cross the Atlantic…

gandaki-river.s: The Gandaki, known as the Gandak in India and the Narayani in its lower course in Nepal, is a river that rises in the Himalayas of Nepal and flows south across the plains of Bihar to join the Ganges near Patna. It is often identified with the Sadanira of the Shatapatha…

gaston-de-foix-duke-of-nemours.n: Gaston de Foix, Duke of Nemours
gaston-de-foix-duke-of-nemours.s: Gaston de Foix was a French nobleman and commander, nephew of Louis XII, who exchanged his viscounty of Narbonne for the duchy of Nemours in 1507. Leading the French army in Italy against the Holy League in the War of the League of Cambrai, he won a series of rapid victories…

guarnacci-museum.s: The Guarnacci Museum in Volterra, Tuscany, is one of the oldest public museums in Europe, founded in 1761 when the priest and scholar Mario Guarnacci gave his collection of antiquities to the city. It holds some 600 Etruscan alabaster and tufa cinerary urns, as well as the…

gnaeus-marcius-coriolanus.s: Gnaeus Marcius Coriolanus was a legendary Roman hero of the early 5th century BCE, said to have earned his name by capturing the Volscian town of Corioli. According to Livy and Plutarch, he was exiled after opposing grain distributions to the plebs, led a Volscian army against…

glappe.s: Glappe was a leader of the Warmians, one of the Baltic Prussian peoples, during the Great Prussian Uprising against the Teutonic Order that began in 1260. According to the chronicler Peter of Dusburg he led Warmian forces in the fighting around Königsberg, but he was later…

ginuwa.s: Ginuwa was a prince of the Benin Empire who, according to Itsekiri tradition, left Benin around 1480 with a group of followers and settled in the creeks of the western Niger Delta. His descendants founded the kingdom of Warri, and Ginuwa is remembered as the first Olu of…

gustav-stresemann.s: Gustav Stresemann (1878–1929) was a German statesman who led the German People's Party and served as chancellor in 1923 and as foreign minister from 1923 until his death. He ended passive resistance in the Ruhr, helped stabilise the currency, and pursued reconciliation with…

gadag.s: Gadag is a city in northern Karnataka, India, which with neighbouring Betageri forms a twin city. It was an important religious and artistic centre under the Western Chalukyas in the 11th and 12th centuries, when the richly carved Trikuteshwara and Saraswati temples were built.

gommateshwara-statue.s: The Gommateshwara statue is a monolithic stone statue of the Jain figure Bahubali, about 17 metres high, on the hill of Vindhyagiri at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka, India. It was commissioned around 983 by Chavundaraya, minister and general of the Western Ganga kings, and is…

guanlong-aristocracy.s: The Guanlong aristocracy was a group of military and civil families of north-western China, named after the Guanzhong and Longxi regions, that formed under the Western Wei and Northern Zhou in the 6th century. Brought together by Yuwen Tai, it combined Xianbei and Chinese…

guianas.s: The Guianas are the region of north-eastern South America between the Orinoco and Amazon rivers, bounded inland by the Guiana Highlands. From the early 17th century Dutch, English and French traders and planters founded colonies along its coast.

gibeon-namibia.s: Gibeon is a village in the Hardap Region of southern Namibia, founded around 1863 when the Witbooi Nama under Kido Witbooi settled there and a Rhenish Mission station was established. It became the seat of the Witbooi captains, including Hendrik Witbooi, who led the Nama…

gansu.s: Gansu is a province of north-western China, stretching from the Loess Plateau along the narrow Hexi (Gansu) Corridor towards Xinjiang, with Lanzhou as its capital. Its eastern valleys were the early homeland of the state of Qin, and the corridor carried the Silk Road between…

great-cloud-sutra.s: The Great Cloud Sutra (Mahamegha Sutra) is a Mahayana Buddhist scripture translated into Chinese in the early 5th century. In 690 monks supporting Wu Zetian circulated a commentary on it which presented her rule as foretold by the Buddha, and she ordered Great Cloud temples…

gao-shida.s: Gao Shida (died 616) was a rebel leader in Hebei during the risings against Emperor Yang of Sui. He sheltered the village headman Dou Jiande and made him his chief commander.

guerrero.s: Guerrero is a state of south-western Mexico on the Pacific coast, with Chilpancingo as its capital and Acapulco as its largest city. Its rugged Sierra Madre del Sur was home to the Yopes (Tlapanecs) and other peoples, some never subdued by the Aztecs.

guangxi.s: Guangxi is an autonomous region of southern China bordering Vietnam, with Nanning as its capital. Its karst landscape around Guilin is famous, and it is home to the Zhuang, China's largest ethnic minority.

guizhou.s: Guizhou is a mountainous province of south-western China, with Guiyang as its capital. Home to many non-Han peoples such as the Miao, Buyei and Dong, it lay in ancient times within the lands of Yelang and other south-western kingdoms.

gebre-mesqel-lalibela.s: Gebre Mesqel Lalibela was a king of the Zagwe dynasty of Ethiopia who reigned in the late 12th and early 13th centuries. Tradition credits him with the rock-hewn churches at his capital Roha, conceived as a 'New Jerusalem', and the town was later renamed Lalibela after him.

geghard.s: Geghard is a medieval monastery in the Kotayk province of Armenia, partly carved out of the cliffs of the Azat river gorge. Founded according to tradition in the 4th century, its main church dates from 1215, built under the Zakarid princes, and the Proshyan family later added…

gbudwe.s: Gbudwe (c. 1835–1905) was the most powerful of the Avongara kings of the Zande, ruling a kingdom in what is now South Sudan.

guiengola.s: Guiengola is a fortified Zapotec hilltop site near Tehuantepec in Oaxaca, Mexico, with temples, palaces, a ball court and long defensive walls. In the late 1490s the Zapotec king Cocijoeza withstood a long siege there by the armies of the Aztec ruler Ahuitzotl.

geresenje.s: Geresenje was the youngest son of Dayan Khan, the ruler who reunited the eastern Mongols around 1500. He received the Khalkha Mongols of northern Mongolia as his share of the inheritance, and his seven sons divided them into appanages.

great-mosque-of-al-nuri-mosul.s: The Great Mosque of al-Nuri was a mosque in the old city of Mosul, Iraq, built by the Zengid ruler Nur al-Din in 1172. Its leaning brick minaret, al-Hadba, "the hunchback", became the symbol of the city.

geng-jingzhong.s: Geng Jingzhong was a Chinese general who inherited his family's fief in Fujian as one of the Three Feudatories under the Qing dynasty. He joined Wu Sangui's rebellion in 1674 but surrendered to the Qing in 1676 when his position collapsed.

gonbad-e-qabus-tower.s: Gonbad-e Qabus is a brick tomb tower in the town of the same name in Golestan province, north-eastern Iran, built in 1006 to 1007 for the Ziyarid ruler Qabus ibn Vushmgir. More than 50 metres high, on a ten-pointed star plan with a conical roof, it is one of the earliest dated…

ghazni.s: Ghazni is a city in eastern Afghanistan on the road between Kabul and Kandahar. From 977 it was the capital of the Ghaznavid Empire, whose ruler Mahmud of Ghazni filled it with palaces, mosques and the spoils of his Indian raids, making it a centre of Persian culture.

gothic-war-376-382.s: The Gothic War of 376–382 was fought between the Roman Empire and Gothic groups, chiefly the Tervingi and Greuthungi, who had crossed the Danube fleeing the Huns. Mistreatment by Roman officials provoked a revolt, and in 378 the Goths destroyed the eastern Roman army and…

gallic-wars.s: The Gallic Wars were the campaigns of Julius Caesar in Gaul from 58 to 50 BCE, which brought the whole of Gaul west of the Rhine under Roman rule. They included expeditions across the Rhine and to Britain and the defeat of the great revolt under Vercingetorix at Alesia in 52 BCE.

gothic-war-535-554.s: The Gothic War was fought from 535 to 554 between the Byzantine Empire of Justinian I and the Ostrogothic Kingdom of Italy. Belisarius took Rome and Ravenna by 540, but the Goths recovered under Totila; Narses finally defeated them at Taginae (552) and Mons Lactarius, and the…

greco-turkish-war-1919-1922.s: The Greco-Turkish War of 1919–1922 was fought between Greece and the Turkish nationalist movement after the First World War. Greek forces landed at Smyrna in 1919 and advanced deep into Anatolia, but were stopped at the Sakarya in 1921 and routed in 1922; the Treaty of…

guelders-wars.s: The Guelders Wars were a series of conflicts from 1502 to 1543 between the Duchy of Guelders, led by Duke Charles of Egmond and supported by France, and the Habsburg rulers of the Netherlands. Charles kept Guelders independent for decades, but after his death Emperor Charles V…

gran-colombia-peru-war.s: The Gran Colombia–Peru War was fought in 1828–1829 between Gran Colombia and Peru over the border provinces of Jaén and Maynas and Peruvian resentment of Bolívar's influence. Antonio José de Sucre defeated the Peruvian army under José de La Mar at the Battle of Tarqui in…

goryeo-khitan-war.s: The Goryeo–Khitan War was a series of invasions of the Korean kingdom of Goryeo by the Khitan Liao dynasty between 993 and 1019. Goryeo retained land south of the Yalu by diplomacy in 993 and resisted a major invasion in 1010, which burned the capital Kaesong.

gwalior-campaign.s: The Gwalior campaign was a short war in December 1843 between the British East India Company and the Maratha state of Gwalior under the Scindia dynasty, provoked by a succession dispute and the growth of the Gwalior army. British forces under Sir Hugh Gough won the battles of…

german-polish-war-1002-1018.s: The German–Polish War of 1002–1018 was a series of conflicts between the Polish duke Bolesław I the Brave and the German king and emperor Henry II over Lusatia, Meissen and Bohemia. Fighting broke out several times after Bolesław seized the marches in 1002.
